He was a trained mechanic, and so had a complete knowledge of his tanks and what he could expect of them. He studied in depth the psychology of the opposing army and its generals. He interacted with almost all of his soldiers, and had a clear sense of how far he could push them. Whatever he studied, he did so with incredible intensity and depth. A point was reached where all of these details became internalized. They fused together in his brain, giving him a feel for the whole picture and a sense of this interactive dynamic.

在战争中，我们可以列举伟大的德国将军埃尔温·隆美尔，据说他拥有战争史上记载的最高超的指尖触觉。他能精准地感知敌人的攻击目标，并挫败他们的计划；他能精准地攻击敌人防线的薄弱环节。他仿佛长了后脑勺的眼睛，拥有预知未来的神通。这一切都是在北非沙漠中完成的，那里几乎不可能对地形有任何清晰的了解。然而，隆美尔的力量并非神秘莫测。他只是比其他将军对战争的各个方面都拥有更深刻的了解。他经常驾驶自己的飞机飞越沙漠，从空中俯瞰地形。他是一位训练有素的机械师，因此对自己的坦克以及可能遇到的情况了如指掌。他深入研究了敌军及其将领的心理。他几乎与所有士兵都互动，并且清楚地知道自己能把他们逼到什么程度。无论他学习什么，他都以惊人的专注和深度投入其中。到了一定程度，所有这些细节都融入了他的大脑，融为一体，让他对全局有了整体的感知，并感受到这种互动的动态。

The ability to have this intuitive grasp of the whole and feel this dynamic is simply a function of time. Since it has been shown that the brain is literally altered after approximately 10,000 hours of practice, these powers would be the result of a transformation that happens in the brain after some 20,000 hours and beyond. With this much practice and experience, all kinds of connections have been formed in the brain between different forms of knowledge. Masters thus have a sense of how everything interacts organically, and they can intuit patterns or solutions in an instant. This fluid form of thinking does not occur through a step-by-step process, but rather comes in flashes and insights as the brain makes sudden connections between disparate forms of knowledge, causing us to sense the dynamic in real time.

这种对整体的直觉把握和感受动态的能力仅仅是时间的函数。由于研究表明，大脑在大约10,000小时的练习后会发生实质性的改变，因此这些能力可能是大脑在大约20,000小时甚至更长时间后发生转变的结果。凭借如此丰富的练习和经验，大脑中不同形式的知识之间形成了各种联系。因此，大师们能够感知万物如何有机地互动，并能够瞬间直觉地找到模式或解决方案。这种流畅的思维方式并非循序渐进，而是随着大脑在不同形式的知识之间建立突然联系而产生的灵光一闪和顿悟，让我们能够实时感知动态。

Some people like to imagine that such intuitions do operate sequentially, but simply happen too fast for the thinker to see the steps. This reasoning comes from the desire to reduce every form of intelligence to the same rational level. But with a discovery like the theory of simple relativity, if Albert Einstein himself could not begin to reconstruct the steps in retrospect that led to his insight on the relativity of time, then why should it be imagined that such steps exist? We must trust the experience and descriptions of these Masters, all people with high levels of self-awareness and analytical skills.

有些人喜欢想象，这种直觉确实是按顺序运作的，只是发生得太快，思考者无法看清其中的步骤。这种推理源于一种将各种形式的智力降低到同一理性水平的愿望。但是，对于像简单相对论这样的发现，如果爱因斯坦本人都无法在回顾中重建他洞察时间相对性的步骤，那么我们又何必想象存在这样的步骤呢？我们必须相信这些大师的经验和描述，他们都是具有高度自我意识和分析能力的人。

It would be a misconception, however, to imagine that Masters are simply following their intuitions and moving beyond rational thinking. First, it is through all of their hard work, the depth of their knowledge, and the development of their analytical skills that they reach this higher form of intelligence. Second, when they experience this intuition or insight, they invariably subject it to a high degree of reflection and reasoning. In science, they must spend months or years verifying their intuitions. In the arts, they must work out the ideas that come to them intuitively and rationally shape them into a form. This is hard for us to imagine, because we find intuition and rationality mutually exclusive, but in fact at this high level they operate together in a seamless fashion. The reasoning of Masters is guided by intuition; their intuition springs from intense rational focus. The two are fused.

然而，如果认为大师们只是遵循直觉，超越理性思考，那就错了。首先，他们通过辛勤的付出、深厚的知识积累以及分析能力的提升，才达到了这种更高层次的智慧。其次，当他们体验到这种直觉或洞见时，他们总是会对其进行高度的反思和推理。在科学领域，他们必须花费数月甚至数年的时间来验证自己的直觉。在艺术领域，他们必须将直觉中涌现的想法付诸实践，并理性地将其转化为具体的形式。这对我们来说很难想象，因为我们认为直觉和理性是相互排斥的，但事实上，在这种高层次上，它们却天衣无缝地协同运作。大师们的推理受直觉引导；他们的直觉源于对理性的高度专注。两者融为一体。

Although time is the critical factor in attaining Mastery and this intuitive feel, the time we are talking about is not neutral or simply quantitative. An hour of Einstein’s thinking at the age of sixteen does not equal an hour spent by an average high school student working on a problem in physics. It is not a matter of studying a subject for twenty years, and then emerging as a Master. The time that leads to mastery is dependent on the intensity of our focus.

虽然时间是获得精通和这种直觉的关键因素，但我们所说的时间并非中性或简单的量化。爱因斯坦十六岁时思考的一小时，远不及普通高中生解决物理问题的一小时。这不是花二十年时间钻研一门学科，然后成为大师的问题。通往精通所需的时间取决于我们专注的强度。

The key, then, to attaining this higher level of intelligence is to make our years of study qualitatively rich. We don’t simply absorb information—we internalize it and make it our own by finding some way to put this knowledge to practical use. We look for connections between the various elements we are learning, hidden laws that we can perceive in the apprenticeship phase. If we experience any failures or setbacks, we do not quickly forget them because they offend our self-esteem. Instead we reflect on them deeply, trying to figure out what went wrong and discern whether there are any patterns to our mistakes. As we progress, we start to question some of the assumptions and conventions we have learned along the way. Soon, we begin to experiment and become increasingly active. At all points in the various moments leading to mastery, we attack with intensity. Every moment, every experience contains deep lessons for us. We are continuously awake, never merely going through the motions.

因此，达到更高智慧水平的关键在于，让我们多年的学习成果更加丰富。我们并非简单地吸收信息，而是将其内化，并通过找到某种方式将这些知识付诸实践，使其成为我们自己的知识。我们寻找所学各个要素之间的联系，以及在学徒阶段能够感知到的隐性规律。如果我们经历任何失败或挫折，我们不会因为它们伤害了我们的自尊而轻易忘记。相反，我们会深入反思，试图找出问题所在，并辨别我们的错误是否存在规律。随着我们的进步，我们开始质疑一路走来学到的一些假设和惯例。很快，我们就会开始尝试，并变得越来越积极主动。在通往精通的各个阶段，我们都会全力以赴。每个时刻，每一次经历都蕴含着深刻的教训。我们始终保持清醒，而非敷衍了事。

The person who best exemplifies this usage of time for mastery is Marcel Proust, whose great novel, In Search of Lost Time, concerns this very subject. In French the word for “lost” is perdu, which equally means “wasted.” And to Proust, and to many of those who knew him as a young man, he seemed the least likely person ever to attain mastery, because on the surface he appeared to waste so much valuable time. All he ever seemed to do was read books, take walks, write interminable letters, attend parties, sleep during the day, and publish frothy society articles. When he finally applied himself to translating Ruskin, he took an incredibly long time and involved himself in seemingly irrelevant tasks, like traveling to locations Ruskin described, something no other translator would think of doing.

最能体现这种利用时间成就大师的人是马塞尔·普鲁斯特，他的伟大小说《追忆似水年华》就探讨了这个主题。法语中“迷失”的意思是“perdu”，意思同样是“浪费”。对普鲁斯特以及许多认识他年轻时的人来说，他似乎是最不可能成就大师的人，因为表面上他似乎浪费了太多宝贵的时间。他似乎所做的一切就是读书、散步、写没完没了的信、参加派对、白天睡觉以及发表一些浮夸的社会文章。当他最终致力于翻译罗斯金的作品时，他花费了令人难以置信的长时间，并让自己沉浸在看似无关紧要的任务中，比如前往罗斯金描述的地方旅行，这是其他译者想都不敢想的事情。

Proust himself complained endlessly about the time that he had wasted as a young man and how little he had accomplished, but these complaints cannot be taken at face value, because he never gave up. Despite his physical weakness and bouts of depression, he continued to try new endeavors and kept widening the scope of his knowledge. He was tireless and tenacious. These moments of self-doubt were his way of propelling himself forward and reminding himself of the short amount of time remaining to him. He had a deep awareness of a sense of destiny, of an overall purpose for his strangeness, that he was called to fulfill through his writing.

普鲁斯特本人也曾无休止地抱怨自己年轻时浪费的光阴和所获的成就，但这些抱怨并非表面功夫，因为他从未放弃。尽管身体虚弱，且时常抑郁，他仍坚持尝试新的尝试，不断拓展知识面。他不知疲倦，意志坚韧。这些自我怀疑的时刻正是他前进的动力，提醒自己时间所剩无几。他深刻地意识到自己的命运，意识到自己奇特的特质背后有一个最终目标，他必须通过写作来实现它。

What made those twenty years qualitatively different from those of an ordinary person was the intensity of his attention. He did not simply read books—he took them apart, rigorously analyzed them, and learned valuable lessons to apply to his own life. All of this reading implanted in his brain various styles that would enrich his own writing style. He did not merely socialize—he strained to understand people at their core and to uncover their secret motivations. He did not just analyze his own psychology, but went so deeply into the various levels of consciousness he found within himself that he developed insights about the functioning of memory that foreshadowed many discoveries in neuroscience. He did not merely translate, but strove to inhabit the mind of Ruskin himself. In the end, he even used the death of his mother to intensify his development. With her gone, he would have to write himself out of his depression, and find a way to re-create the feelings between them in the book he was to write. As he later described it, all of these experiences were like seeds, and once he had started his novel he was like a gardener tending and cultivating the plants that had taken root so many years before.

这二十年与常人截然不同的，是他专注的专注力。他并非只是读书——他把书拆开，严谨地分析，并从中汲取宝贵的教训，应用于自己的人生。所有这些阅读都在他的脑海中植入了各种风格，丰富了他的写作风格。他并非只是社交——他努力理解人们的内心，揭示他们隐秘的动机。他并非只是分析自己的心理，而是深入探究自身内在的不同意识层面，最终对记忆的运作方式产生了深刻的洞见，这预示了神经科学领域的许多发现。他并非只是翻译，而是努力融入罗斯金的内心世界。最终，他甚至利用母亲的去世来强化自己的发展。母亲去世后，他必须通过写作走出抑郁，并在即将撰写的书中找到一种方式来重塑他们之间的情感。正如他后来所描述的那样，所有这些经历都像种子一样，一旦他开始写小说，他就像一个园丁，照料和培育多年前扎根的植物。

Through his own efforts, he transformed himself from an apprentice to a mature writer and translator, and from there to a novelist who figured out what to write about, which voice to assume, and how to attack his subject. At some point after he began writing his novel, he underwent a third transformation. Memories and ideas came flooding into his mind. Even as the book kept expanding, he could intuit its overall shape and the relationships between the many tiles of the mosaic. This immense novel had a living, breathing dynamic that was now completely alive within him. He was inside his characters and the whole slice of French society he was writing about. More important, he was completely inside the narrator (who is Proust himself), and in his novel it’s as if we are literally, from the inside, experiencing the thoughts and sensations of another person. He was able to achieve this effect through the intuitive powers he had gained from close to thirty years of perpetual work and analysis.

通过自身的努力，他从一个学徒蜕变成一位成熟的作家和翻译家，并最终成为一名小说家，他清楚自己该写什么，该采用何种语气，以及如何深入挖掘主题。在开始创作小说的某个时刻，他经历了第三次蜕变。记忆和想法涌入他的脑海。即使书本不断扩展，他依然能够直观地感知到它的整体形态以及马赛克拼图中众多图块之间的关系。这部宏大的小说拥有一种鲜活的、呼吸的动力，如今这种动力已完全融入他的内心。他融入了书中的人物，融入了他所描写的整个法国社会。更重要的是，他完全融入了叙述者（也就是普鲁斯特本人）的内心，在他的小说中，我们仿佛置身于其中，体验着另一个人的思想和感受。他之所以能够达到这种效果，是因为他近三十年来不断钻研和分析所获得的直觉力。

Like Proust, you must also maintain a sense of destiny, and feel continuously connected to it. You are unique, and there is a purpose to your uniqueness. You must see every setback, failure, or hardship as a trial along the way, as seeds that are being planted for further cultivation, if you know how to grow them. No moment is wasted if you pay attention and learn the lessons contained in every experience. By constantly applying yourself to the subject that suits your inclinations and attacking it from many different angles, you are simply enriching the ground for these seeds to take root. You may not see this process in the present, but it is happening. Never losing your connection to your Life’s Task, you will unconsciously hit upon the right choices in your life. Over time, mastery will come to you.

像普鲁斯特一样，你也必须保持对命运的感知，并始终与之相连。你是独一无二的，你的独特之处自有其意义。你必须将每一次挫折、失败或艰辛视为人生道路上的一次考验，如同一颗颗正在播下的种子，如果你懂得如何培育它们。如果你用心学习，并从每一次经历中汲取教训，那么每一刻都不会被浪费。通过不断地钻研符合你兴趣的领域，并从不同的角度进行探索，你实际上是在为这些种子的生根发芽提供更肥沃的土壤。你或许现在看不到这个过程，但它正在发生。永不失去与你人生使命的联系，你将在不知不觉中做出正确的人生选择。随着时间的推移，你将获得成功。

The high-level intuitive powers we are talking about have roots in our development as the thinking animal; they have an evolutionary purpose that is extremely helpful to understand, and one that is highly relevant to the times in which we live.

我们所谈论的高级直觉能力根植于我们作为思维动物的发展；它们有一个非常有助于理解的进化目的，并且与我们生活的时代高度相关。

# ↩

The Roots of Masterly Intuition

大师级直觉的根源

For nearly all animals, speed is the critical factor in survival. A few seconds can spell the difference between avoiding a predator or meeting death. And for the purposes of such speed, organisms have evolved elaborate instincts. An instinctual response is immediate and is generally triggered by certain stimuli. Sometimes organisms possess instincts that are so finely calibrated to circumstances that they seem to have uncanny abilities.

对于几乎所有动物来说，速度都是生存的关键因素。几秒钟的时间就足以决定是躲避捕食者还是面临死亡。为了应对这种速度，生物进化出了精妙的本能。本能反应是即时的，通常由某些刺激触发。有时，生物拥有的本能会根据环境进行精准的调整，以至于它们似乎拥有不可思议的能力。

Take, for instance, the Ammophila wasp. With incredible speed the female Ammophila is able to sting her various victims—spiders, beetles, caterpillars—in precisely the right place to paralyze but not kill them. Into the paralyzed flesh she lays her eggs, providing her larvae with fresh meat to feast upon for several days. In each of these victims the stinging points are different—for instance, with the caterpillar, she must hit at three separate points to paralyze the entire creature. Because it is such a delicate operation, sometimes the Ammophila misses and kills the victim, but generally, her success rate is high enough to ensure the survival of her offspring. In this process there is no time for calculating the kind of victim and the exact spot to hit. It is instant, as if the wasp has a feel for the nerve centers of her various victims, and can sense them from the inside.

以沙蜂（Ammophila）为例。雌性沙蜂能够以惊人的速度螫住各种受害者——蜘蛛、甲虫、毛毛虫——的准确位置，使其瘫痪但不会死亡。在瘫痪的肉体中，它会产卵，为幼虫提供鲜肉，供其享用数日。每个受害者的螫针位置各不相同——例如，对于毛毛虫，它必须螫针三个不同的位置才能使整个受害者瘫痪。由于螫针操作非常精细，有时沙蜂会失手杀死受害者，但通常情况下，它的成功率足以确保后代的生存。在这个过程中，沙蜂没有时间计算受害者的种类和确切的螫针位置。整个过程瞬间完成，仿佛沙蜂能够感知到各种受害者的神经中枢，并从内部感知到它们。

Our primitive ancestors had their own sets of instincts, many of which remain buried within us to this day. But as these ancestors slowly developed reasoning powers, they had to detach themselves from their immediate circumstances and depend less on instinct. To notice behavior patterns in the animals they were tracking, they had to connect them to other actions that were not immediately apparent. They had to make similar calculations when it came to locating food sources, or to navigating the long distances they traveled on foot. With this ability to detach themselves from the environment and see patterns, they gained tremendous mental powers, but this development also presented a great danger—increasing amounts of information for the brain to process and a consequent loss of speed in reacting to events.

我们的原始祖先拥有一套独特的本能，其中许多至今仍深藏于我们心中。但随着这些祖先逐渐发展出推理能力，他们不得不脱离眼前的环境，减少对本能的依赖。为了注意到追踪动物的行为模式，他们必须将其与其他并非立即显现的行为联系起来。在寻找食物来源或长途跋涉时，他们也必须进行类似的计算。凭借这种脱离环境、洞察模式的能力，他们获得了强大的心智能力，但这种发展也带来了巨大的危险——大脑需要处理的信息量增加，导致对事件的反应速度下降。

Such slowness could have spelled doom for us as a species if not for a compensatory power that the human brain developed. Years of tracking particular animals and observing their surroundings gave our ancestors a feel for their environment in all of its complexity. Knowing the behavior patterns of various animals, they could anticipate where predators might strike, and sense where prey might lie. They came to know so well the long distances they traveled that they could negotiate these spaces quickly and effectively, without having to calculate. In other words, they developed a primitive form of intuition. Through continual experience and practice, our ancestors recovered some of the immediacy and speed they had lost. They could respond intuitively instead of instinctually. On this level, intuition was more powerful than instinct in that it was not tied to very specific circumstances or stimuli, but could be applied to a much wider arena of action.

如果不是人类大脑发展出了一种补偿能力，如此缓慢的速度或许会给我们这个物种带来厄运。长年追踪特定动物并观察其周围环境，使我们的祖先能够感知周围环境的复杂性。通过了解各种动物的行为模式，他们可以预测捕食者可能袭击的地点，并感知猎物可能藏身之处。他们对自己行进的长距离了如指掌，因此能够快速有效地穿越这些空间，而无需计算。换句话说，他们发展出了一种原始的直觉。通过不断的经验和实践，我们的祖先恢复了一些他们已经失去的即时性和速度。他们可以直觉地做出反应，而不是本能。在这个层面上，直觉比本能更强大，因为它不受特定环境或刺激的束缚，而是可以应用于更广泛的行动领域。

These ancestors’ brains were not yet burdened by all of the information that comes through language or the complexities of living in large groups. Interacting so directly with their environment, they could develop an intuitive feel over the course of a handful years. But for us, living in a much more complex environment, this process can take fifteen to twenty years. Our high-level intuition , however, has its roots firmly in the primitive version.

这些祖先的大脑尚未承受语言带来的信息量，也未适应群体生活的复杂性。通过与环境如此直接的互动，他们能够在短短几年内培养出直觉。但对于我们这些生活在复杂得多的环境中的人来说，这个过程可能需要十五到二十年。然而，我们高级的直觉却深深植根于原始版本。

Intuition, primitive or high level, is essentially driven by memory. When we take in information of any kind, we store it in mnemonic networks in the brain. The stability and durability of these networks depends on repetition, intensity of experience, and how deeply we pay attention. If we are half listening to a vocabulary lesson in a foreign language, we are not likely to retain it on any level. But if we are in the country where the language is spoken, we will hear the same words repeated in context; we will tend to pay deeper attention because we need to, and the memory trace will be that much more stable.

直觉，无论是原始的还是高级的，本质上都是由记忆驱动的。当我们接收任何类型的信息时，我们都会将其存储在大脑的记忆网络中。这些网络的稳定性和持久性取决于重复次数、经验的强度以及我们注意力的深度。如果我们只是半心半意地听一堂外语词汇课，我们不太可能记住它。但如果我们身处使用该语言的国家，我们会听到相同的单词在语境中重复出现；我们会倾向于更加专注，因为我们需要这样做，记忆痕迹也会更加稳定。

According to the model developed by the psychologist Kenneth Bowers, whenever we encounter a problem—a face we need to recognize, a word or phrase we need to recall—mnemonic networks within the brain become activated as the search for the answer is guided along certain pathways. All of this occurs below the level of consciousness. When a particular network is sufficiently activated, we suddenly become conscious of a possible name for the face, or a phrase that might be appropriate. These are low-level forms of intuition that come to us in our everyday life; we cannot reconstruct the steps that went into recognizing a person’s face and remembering their name.

根据心理学家肯尼斯·鲍尔斯（Kenneth Bowers）提出的模型，每当我们遇到问题——比如需要识别一张面孔，或者需要回忆一个单词或短语——大脑中的记忆网络就会被激活，因为我们会沿着特定的路径引导我们寻找答案。所有这些都发生在意识层面之下。当某个特定的网络被充分激活时，我们会突然意识到这张面孔可能对应一个名字，或者一个可能合适的短语。这些都是我们在日常生活中产生的低级直觉；我们无法重建识别一个人的面孔并记住其名字的步骤。

People who spend years studying a particular subject or field develop so many of these memory networks and pathways that their brains are constantly searching for and discovering connections between various pieces of information. When confronted with a high-level problem, the search goes in a hundred directions below conscious awareness, guided by an intuitive sense of where the answer might lie. All kinds of networks become activated, ideas and solutions suddenly rising to the surface. Those that seem particularly fruitful and appropriate stick in the memory and are acted upon. Instead of having to reason an answer through a step-by-step process, the answer comes to consciousness with a feeling of immediacy. The extremely high number of experiences and memory networks that become hardwired allow the brains of Masters to explore an area that is so wide that it has the dimensions and feel of reality itself, of the dynamic .

那些在特定学科或领域潜心钻研多年的人，会发展出如此丰富的记忆网络和路径，以至于他们的大脑会不断搜寻和发现各种信息之间的联系。面对高层次的问题时，他们的大脑会在潜意识层面上，沿着上百个方向进行探索，并由直觉引导，判断答案可能在哪里。各种网络都被激活，各种想法和解决方案顿时浮现。那些看起来特别有效、合适的想法会留在记忆中，并被付诸行动。答案无需通过循序渐进的过程推理，而是会立即出现在意识中。大量的经验和记忆网络被固化，使得大师们的大脑能够探索广阔的领域，以至于它拥有现实本身的维度和感觉，充满动态。

For someone like the chess Master Bobby Fischer, the number of times he experienced similar sets of circumstances and witnessed the various movements and reactions of different opponents created powerful memory traces. He internalized incredible numbers of patterns. At some point in his development, all of these memories fused into a feel for the overall dynamic of the game. He was no longer seeing simple moves on the chessboard and recalling various countermoves he had made in the past, but rather was able to see and recollect long sequences of potential moves that presented themselves as fields of force, sweeping the board as a whole. With such a sense for the game, he could entrap his opponents well before they were aware of what was happening, and could finish them off as quickly and precisely as the Ammophila delivered her sting.

对于像国际象棋大师鲍比·菲舍尔这样的人来说，他经历过无数次类似的情况，目睹过不同对手的各种动作和反应，这让他积累了强大的记忆痕迹。他内化了数量惊人的模式。在成长的某个阶段，所有这些记忆融合成对棋局整体动态的感知。他不再只是看到棋盘上的简单走法，回忆起过去做出的各种反击，而是能够看到并回忆起一系列潜在的走法，这些走法如同力场一般席卷整个棋盘。凭借这种对棋局的感知，他能够在对手察觉之前就将其困住，并像沙蜂花的刺一样迅速精准地终结对手。

In fields such as sports or warfare, or any competitive endeavor where time is of the essence, Masters’ decisions based on intuition will be much more effective than if they had tried to analyze all of the components and figure out the best answer. There is too much information to consider in too short a time. Although the power of intuition was originally developed for the rapidity it brought, it has become something that can be applied to the sciences or the arts, or to any field in which there are complex elements and time is not necessarily the critical factor.

在体育、战争等领域，或任何时间至关重要的竞争性活动中，大师们基于直觉做出的决策，比试图分析所有因素并找出最佳答案要有效得多。在如此短的时间内，需要考虑的信息实在太多。虽然直觉的力量最初是为了快速而发展起来的，但它如今已发展成为一种可以应用于科学、艺术，或任何包含复杂因素且时间并非关键因素的领域。

This high-level intuition, like any skill, requires practice and experience. At first, our intuitions might be so faint that we do not pay attention to them or trust them. All Masters talk of this phenomenon. But over time they learn to notice these rapid ideas that come to them. They learn to act on them and verify their validity. Some lead nowhere, but others lead to tremendous insights. Over time, Masters find that they can call up more and more of these high-level intuitions, which are now sparking all over the brain. Accessing this level of thinking on a more regular basis, they can fuse it even more deeply with their rational forms of thinking.

这种高层次的直觉，如同任何技能一样，需要练习和经验的积累。起初，我们的直觉可能非常微弱，以至于我们不会留意或信任它们。所有大师都会谈论这种现象。但随着时间的推移，他们学会了留意这些快速涌现的想法。他们学会了根据这些想法采取行动，并验证其有效性。有些想法毫无进展，但有些却能带来深刻的洞见。随着时间的推移，大师们发现他们能够唤起越来越多这样的高层次直觉，这些直觉如今在大脑中迸发出火花。通过更频繁地接触这种层次的思维，他们可以将其与理性思维方式更加深入地融合。

Understand: this intuitive form of intelligence was developed to help us process complex layers of information and gain a sense of the whole. And in the world today, the need to attain such a level of thinking is more critical than ever before. To follow any career path is difficult, and requires the cultivation of much patience and discipline. We have so many elements to master that it can be intimidating. We must learn to handle the technical aspects, the social and political gamesmanship, the public reactions to our work, and the constantly changing picture in our field. When we add to this already-daunting quantity of study the vast amounts of information now available to us, and that we must keep on top of, it all seems beyond our capability.

要知道：这种直觉智慧的出现是为了帮助我们处理层层复杂的信息，并掌握全局。在当今世界，达到这种思维水平比以往任何时候都更加重要。任何职业道路都充满挑战，需要培养极大的耐心和自律。我们需要掌握的要素如此之多，甚至可能令人望而生畏。我们必须学会应对技术层面、社会和政治博弈、公众对我们工作的反应，以及我们领域不断变化的格局。当我们在这本已令人望而生畏的学习任务上，再加上如今唾手可得的海量信息，以及我们必须掌握的海量信息时，这一切似乎都超出了我们的能力范围。

What happens to many of us when faced with such complexity is that we feel subtly discouraged before we even try anything. More and more people in this overheated environment will be tempted to opt out. They will develop a greater taste for ease and comfort; they will increasingly settle on simplified ideas of reality and conventional ways of thinking; they will fall prey to seductive formulas that offer quick and easy knowledge. They will lose a taste for developing skills that require time and a resilient ego—it can hurt our self-esteem in the initial phases of learning a skill, as we are made so aware of our awkwardness. Such people will rail against the world and blame others for their problems; they will find political justifications for opting out, when in truth they simply cannot handle the challenges of engaging with complexity. In trying to simplify their mental lives, they disconnect themselves from reality and neutralize all of the powers developed by the human brain over so many millions of years.

我们许多人面对如此复杂的情况时，都会在尝试任何事之前就感到一阵微妙的沮丧。在这种过热的环境中，越来越多的人会倾向于选择退出。他们会更加追求安逸舒适；他们会越来越沉迷于简化的现实观念和传统的思维方式；他们会被那些提供快速简便知识的诱人公式所吸引。他们会对培养需要时间和韧性自我的技能失去兴趣——在学习技能的初期，这会损害我们的自尊，因为我们会意识到自己的笨拙。这样的人会抱怨世界，把问题归咎于他人；他们会为选择退出寻找政治借口，而事实上，他们根本无法应对应对复杂挑战的挑战。在试图简化精神生活的过程中，他们使自己脱离了现实，并抵消了人类大脑数百万年来发展的所有能力。

This desire for what is simple and easy infects all of us, often in ways we are mostly unaware of. The only solution is the following: We must learn how to quiet the anxiety we feel whenever we are confronted with anything that seems complex or chaotic. In our journey from apprenticeship to mastery we must patiently learn the various parts and skills that are required, never looking too far ahead. In moments of perceived crisis, we must develop the habit of maintaining our cool and never overreacting. If the situation is complex and others are reaching for simple black-and-white answers, or for the usual conventional responses, we must make a point of resisting such a temptation. We maintain our Negative Capability and a degree of detachment. What we are doing is gaining a tolerance and even a taste for chaotic moments, training ourselves to entertain several possibilities or solutions. We are learning to manage our anxiety, a key skill in these chaotic times.

这种对简单易行的渴望感染着我们所有人，往往以我们大多未曾察觉的方式。唯一的解决办法是：我们必须学会如何平息面对任何看似复杂或混乱的事物时产生的焦虑。在从学徒到精通的过程中，我们必须耐心学习所需的各个环节和技能，切勿眼光过远。在察觉到危机的时刻，我们必须养成保持冷静、切勿反应过度的习惯。如果情况复杂，而其他人试图给出简单的非黑即白的答案，或采取惯常的应对方式，我们必须努力抵制这种诱惑。我们要保持消极应对的能力和一定程度的超然。我们所做的就是培养对混乱时刻的容忍度，甚至品味它，训练自己去考虑多种可能性或解决方案。我们正在学习管理焦虑，这是在这个混乱时期的一项关键技能。

To go along with this self-control, we must do whatever we can to cultivate a greater memory capacity—one of the most important skills in our technologically oriented environment. The problem that technology presents us is that it increases the amount of information at our disposal, but slowly degrades the power of our memory to retain it. Tasks that used to exercise the brain—remembering phone numbers, doing simple calculations, navigating and remembering streets in a city—are now performed for us, and like any muscle the brain can grow flabby from disuse. To counteract this, in our spare time we should not simply look for entertainment and distractions. We should take up hobbies—a game, a musical instrument, a foreign language—that bring pleasure but also offer us the chance to strengthen our memory capacities and the flexibility of our brain. In doing so, we can train ourselves to process large amounts of information without feeling anxious or overtaxed.

为了保持这种自控力，我们必须竭尽所能地提升记忆力——这在如今科技主导的环境中至关重要。科技带来的问题是，它增加了我们可支配的信息量，却逐渐削弱了我们记忆保留信息的能力。过去那些需要锻炼大脑的任务——记住电话号码、进行简单的计算、在城市中导航和记住街道——现在都由我们自己完成，而大脑就像任何肌肉一样，久而久之就会变得松弛。为了解决这个问题，我们在闲暇时间不应该仅仅寻找娱乐和消遣。我们应该培养一些爱好——游戏、乐器、外语——它们不仅能给我们带来乐趣，还能让我们有机会增强记忆力和大脑的灵活性。通过这样做，我们可以训练自己处理大量信息，而不会感到焦虑或负担过重。

Faithfully pursuing this course over enough time, we will eventually be rewarded with intuitive powers. That whole living, breathing, changing beast that is our field will become internalized and live within us. Possessing even a part of such power will instantly separate us from all of the others who find themselves overwhelmed and straining to simplify what is inherently complex. We will be able to respond faster and more effectively than others. What seemed chaotic to us before will now seem to be simply a fluid situation with a particular dynamic that we have a feel for and can handle with relative ease.

只要我们忠实地践行这条道路，并坚持足够长的时间，最终就能获得直觉的力量。我们能量场中那活生生、呼吸着、不断变化着的巨兽，将会被内化，并驻扎在我们体内。哪怕只是拥有其中的一部分力量，我们也能瞬间脱颖而出，与那些不知所措、竭力简化复杂事物的人区分开来。我们将能够比其他人更快、更有效地做出反应。之前在我们看来混乱不堪的事物，现在看起来只不过是一种流动的局面，拥有一种我们能够感知并相对轻松地应对的特定动态。

What is interesting to note is that many Masters who come to possess this high-level intuitive power seem to become younger in mind and spirit with the passing years—something that should be encouraging to us all. They do not need to expend a great deal of energy in order to understand phenomena, and can think creatively with increasing speed. Unless debilitated by disease, they can maintain their spontaneity and mental fluidity well into their seventies and beyond. Among such types are the Zen Master and artist Hakuin, who made paintings in his sixties that are now considered among the greatest works of his time, remarkable for the spontaneity of expression they reveal. Another example is the Spanish filmmaker Luis Buñuel, whose surrealist films seemed to get richer and more startling as he reached his sixties and seventies. But the quintessence of this phenomenon would have to be Benjamin Franklin.

值得注意的是，许多拥有这种高超直觉力的大师似乎随着岁月的流逝，心智和精神都变得更年轻——这应该令我们所有人都感到鼓舞。他们无需耗费大量精力就能理解现象，并能以越来越快的速度进行创造性思考。除非疾病缠身，否则他们即使在古稀之年甚至更久之后，也能保持自发性和思维的流畅性。禅师兼艺术家白隐便是其中一员，他在六十多岁时创作的画作如今被认为是他那个时代最伟大的作品之一，其表达方式的自发性令人叹为观止。另一个例子是西班牙电影制片人路易斯·布努埃尔，他的超现实主义电影在他六七十岁时似乎变得更加丰富多彩，更加令人惊叹。但这种现象的典范当属本杰明·富兰克林。

Franklin had always been an acute observer of natural phenomena, but these powers only increased with the years. In his seventies and on into his eighties he continued with a series of speculations that are now considered uncannily ahead of his time—including advanced ideas on health and medicine, weather, physics, geophysics, evolution, the use of aircraft for military and commercial purposes, and more. As he aged, he applied his renowned inventiveness to his growing physical weaknesses. Trying to improve his eyesight and quality of life, he invented bifocals. Unable to reach books on the tops of his shelves, he invented an extendible mechanical arm. Needing copies of his own work and not wanting to leave his house, he invented a rolling press that could make an accurate copy of a document in less than two minutes. In his last years, he had insights into politics and the future of America that made people think of him as a seer, as someone with magical abilities. William Pierce, a delegate to the Constitutional Convention, met Franklin near the end of his life and wrote: “Dr. Franklin is well known to be the greatest philosopher of the present age; all the operations of nature he seems to understand…. He is eighty-two years old, and possesses an activity of mind equal to a youth of twenty-five years of age.”

富兰克林一直以来都是一位敏锐的自然现象观察者，而这种能力与日俱增。在他七八十岁之际，他继续进行着一系列如今被认为超越时代的推测——包括关于健康与医学、气象、物理学、地球物理学、进化论、飞机的军事和商业用途等方面的先进思想。随着年龄的增长，他将自己著名的创造力运用到日益衰弱的身体状况中。为了改善视力和生活质量，他发明了双光眼镜。由于够不到书架顶部的书籍，他发明了一种可伸缩的机械臂。由于需要复印自己的作品而又不愿离开家，他发明了一种可以在两分钟内精确复印一份文件的滚压机。在他生命的最后几年，他对政治和美国未来的洞见使人们将他视为一位预言家，一位拥有神奇力量的人。制宪会议代表威廉·皮尔斯在富兰克林临终前与他会面，并写道：“众所周知，富兰克林博士是当代最伟大的哲学家；他似乎洞悉了自然界的一切运作……他已经八十二岁了，但他的思维活跃程度却与二十五岁的年轻人相当。”

It is interesting to speculate what depths of understanding such Masters could have reached if they had lived even longer. Perhaps in the future, with life expectancy increasing, we will witness examples of the Benjamin Franklin variety stretching to even more advanced ages.

有趣的是，如果这些大师们能活得更长寿，他们的理解力会达到何种程度。或许在未来，随着预期寿命的延长，我们会看到像本杰明·富兰克林那样的杰出人物活到更高的年龄。

# ↩

The Return to Reality

回归现实

People can argue endlessly about what constitutes reality, but let us start our definition with a simple, undeniable fact: some 4 billion years ago, life began on this planet in the shape of simple cells. These cells, perhaps even one cell in particular, were the common ancestors to all life forms that followed. From that single source, various branches of life emerged. Some 1.2 billion years ago there appeared the first multicellular creatures; 600 million years ago there emerged perhaps the greatest development of all—organisms with a central nervous system, the starting point that eventually led to the brains we now possess. From the Cambrian explosion of life some 500 million years ago came the first simple animals, followed by the first vertebrates. Some 360 million years ago we see the first traces on land of amphibious creatures, and 120 million years ago the first mammals. Branching off in a new mammalian direction about 60 million years ago, we see signs of the earliest primates from whom we are directly descended. The earliest human ancestors arrived some 6 million years ago, and 4 million years later our most recent ancestor, Homo erectus . And just 200,000 years ago the anatomically modern human emerged, with more or less the same brain size that we now possess.

关于什么是现实，人们可以无休止地争论，但让我们从一个简单而无可否认的事实开始我们的定义：大约40亿年前，生命以简单的细胞形式在这个星球上诞生。这些细胞，甚至可能是一个特定的细胞，是所有后续生命形式的共同祖先。从这个单一源头，生命的各个分支出现了。大约12亿年前，出现了第一批多细胞生物；6亿年前，出现了也许是所有生命中最伟大的发展——具有中枢神经系统的生物，这最终导致了我们今天所拥有的大脑的形成。大约5亿年前的寒武纪生命大爆发，出现了第一批简单动物，随后是第一批脊椎动物。大约3.6亿年前，我们在陆地上看到了第一批两栖动物的踪迹，1.2亿年前，第一批哺乳动物出现了。大约6000万年前，生命朝着新的哺乳动物方向发展，我们看到了最早的灵长类动物的踪迹，而我们正是它们的直系后代。最早的人类祖先大约在600万年前出现，400万年后，我们最近的祖先——直立人出现了。而就在20万年前，解剖学意义上的现代人类出现了，他们的脑容量与我们现在的差不多。

In this remarkably complex chain of circumstances, we can identify, at certain turning points, a single ancestor from whom we humans have evolved (the first cells, simple animals, mammals, then primates). Some archeologists have speculated about a single female ancestor from whom all modern humans have descended. Moving up the chain, backwards in time, it is clear that who we are today—our particular physiological makeup—is intimately connected to each one of these original ancestors, as far back as the first cells of life. Since all life forms are descended from this common beginning, they are all interconnected in some way, and we humans are intimately implicated in this network. This is undeniable.

在这个极其复杂的环境链中，我们可以在某些转折点上找到人类进化的单一祖先（最初的细胞、简单动物、哺乳动物，然后是灵长类动物）。一些考古学家推测，所有现代人类都起源于同一个女性祖先。沿着这条链向上追溯，回溯到时间，很明显，我们今天的身份——我们独特的生理构造——与这些原始祖先中的每一个都息息相关，最早可以追溯到生命的第一个细胞。由于所有生命形式都源于这个共同的开端，它们都以某种方式相互关联，而我们人类也与这个网络紧密相连。这是不可否认的。

Let us call this interrelatedness of life the ultimate reality . And in relation to this reality, the human mind tends to go in one of two directions. On the one hand, the mind tends to move away from this interconnectedness and focus instead on the distinctions between things, taking objects out of their contexts and analyzing them as separate entities. At the extreme this tendency leads to highly specialized forms of knowledge. In the world today, we can see many signs of this tendency—the microscopic divisions between fields in our universities, the narrowest of specializations in the sciences. In the culture at large, people will make the finest distinctions between closely related or overlapping subjects, and argue endlessly about the differences. They will distinguish between military and civilian society, even though in a democracy such a distinction is not so easy to make. (Perhaps keeping people and fields of study so rigorously separated can be considered the ultimate ploy of those in power, a version of divide and conquer.) At this level of thinking, a sense of the interrelatedness of life and phenomena is lost, and in becoming so specialized ideas can become quite weird and disconnected from reality.

我们将生命的这种相互关联性称为终极现实。而与此现实相关的是，人类思维倾向于两种方向之一。一方面，思维倾向于远离这种相互关联性，转而关注事物之间的区别，将事物脱离其背景，并将它们作为独立的实体进行分析。在极端情况下，这种趋势会导致高度专业化的知识形式。在当今世界，我们可以看到许多这种趋势的迹象——大学里学科之间的细微划分，以及科学领域最狭窄的专业化。在整个文化中，人们会对密切相关或重叠的学科进行极其细微的区分，并无休止地争论这些差异。他们会区分军事社会和平民社会，即使在民主国家，这种区分并不容易。 （也许将人和研究领域如此严格地分开可以被认为是当权者的终极策略，一种分而治之的做法。）在这种思维水平上，人们对生活和现象的相互关联性失去了认识，并且在变得如此专业化的过程中，思想会变得相当奇怪且脱离现实。

On the other hand, there is the opposing tendency of the brain to want to make connections between everything. This generally occurs among individuals who pursue knowledge far enough that these associations come to life. Although this tendency is easier to spot in Masters, we can see in history certain movements and philosophies in which this return to reality becomes widespread in a culture, part of the zeitgeist. For instance, in the ancient world there was Taoism in the East, and Stoicism in the West, both movements that endured for centuries. In Taoism, there is the concept of the Way, and in Stoicism, that of the Logos—the ordering principle of the universe that connects all living things. As Marcus Aurelius expresses it, “Keep reminding yourself of the way things are connected, of their relatedness. All things are implicated in one another and in sympathy with each other. This event is the consequence of some other one. Things push and pull on each other, and breathe together, and are one.”

另一方面，大脑还有一种相反的倾向，那就是想要在万物之间建立联系。这通常发生在那些对知识追求足够深入，以至于这些联系能够鲜活呈现的个体身上。虽然这种倾向在大师身上更容易被发现，但我们在历史上也能看到某些运动和哲学，在这些运动和哲学中，这种回归现实的现象在某种文化中广泛传播，成为时代精神的一部分。例如，在古代世界，东方有道家思想，西方有斯多葛主义，这两种思想都持续了几个世纪。道家有“道”的概念，斯多葛主义有“逻各斯”的概念——连接所有生物的宇宙秩序原则。正如马可·奥勒留所说：“不断提醒自己事物的联系和关联性。万物都相互关联，相互呼应。一件事是另一件事的结果。万物相互推拉，共同呼吸，合而为一。”

Perhaps the greatest example of this was the Renaissance, a cultural movement for which the ideal was the Universal Man—a person who has managed to connect all branches of knowledge and approximate the intellectual reach of the Creator.

或许最伟大的例子就是文艺复兴，这是一场文化运动，其理想是“全能人”——一个能够将所有知识分支联系起来并接近造物主智力范围的人。

Perhaps today we are witnessing the early signs of a return to reality, a Renaissance in modern form. In the sciences, the first seeds of this began with Faraday, Maxwell, and Einstein, who focused on the relationships between phenomena, fields of force instead of individual particles. In the larger sense, many scientists are now actively seeking to connect their various specializations to others—for instance, how neuroscience intersects so many other disciplines. We see signs of this also in the growing interest in theories of complexity applied to such disparate fields as economics, biology, and computers. We can see it in the broadening of our thinking to ecosystems, as a way to truly conceptualize the dynamic interactions in nature. We can see it in health and medicine, in the sane approach many are taking to consider the body as a whole. This trend is the future, because the purpose of consciousness itself has always been to connect us to reality.

或许，今天我们正见证着回归现实的早期迹象，一场现代形式的文艺复兴。在科学领域，这股复兴的种子始于法拉第、麦克斯韦和爱因斯坦，他们关注的是现象之间、力场之间而非单个粒子之间的关系。从更广阔的意义上讲，许多科学家如今正积极探索将各自专业与其他领域联系起来——例如，神经科学如何与众多其他学科交叉。我们也从人们对复杂性理论应用于经济学、生物学和计算机等不同领域日益增长的兴趣中看到了这种迹象。我们可以从将思维拓展到生态系统中看到这一点，以此真正概念化自然界的动态相互作用。我们可以从健康和医学领域看到这一点，许多人正在采取理智的方法来将身体视为一个整体。这种趋势代表着未来，因为意识本身的目的始终是将我们与现实联系起来。

As individuals, we can participate in this trend simply by pursuing mastery. In our apprenticeships, we naturally begin by learning the parts and making various distinctions—the right and wrong way to proceed, the individual skills to master and their particular techniques, the various rules and conventions that govern the group. In the Creative-Active we begin to melt these distinctions as we experiment with, shape, and alter these conventions to suit our purposes. And in mastery we come full circle, returning to a sense of the whole. We intuit and see the connections. We embrace the natural complexity of life, making the brain expand to the dimensions of reality instead of shrinking it to the narrowest of specializations. This is the inevitable outcome of deep immersion in a field. We can define intelligence as moving toward thinking that is more contextual, more sensitive to the relationships between things.

作为个体，我们只需追求精通，就能参与到这一趋势中。在学徒期，我们自然而然地从学习各个部分开始，并做出各种区分——正确和错误的行事方式，需要掌握的个人技能及其特定技巧，以及管理群体的各种规则和惯例。在创造-主动阶段，我们开始消解这些区分，并根据自身目标对这些惯例进行实验、塑造和修改。在精通阶段，我们完成了一个完整的循环，回归了对整体的感知。我们直觉地感知并发现其中的联系。我们拥抱生命自然的复杂性，让大脑扩展到现实的维度，而不是将其收缩到最狭窄的专业领域。这是深度沉浸于某个领域的必然结果。我们可以将智力定义为朝着更具情境性、对事物之间关系更敏感的思维方向发展。

Think of it this way: the ultimate distinction you make is between yourself and the world. There is the inside (your subjective experience) and there is the outside. But every time you learn something, your brain is altered as new connections are formed. Your experience of something that occurs in the world physically alters your brain. The boundaries between you and the world are much more fluid than you might imagine. When you move toward mastery, your brain becomes radically altered by the years of practice and active experimentation. It is no longer the simple ecosystem of years gone by. The brain of a Master is so richly interconnected that it comes to resemble the physical world, and becomes a vibrant ecosystem in which all forms of thinking associate and connect. This growing similarity between the brain and complex life itself represents the ultimate return to reality.

不妨这样想：你最终的区分在于你自身与世界。世界分为内在（你的主观体验）和外在。但每当你学习新事物时，你的大脑就会随着新连接的形成而改变。你对世间所发生之事的体验会从本质上改变你的大脑。你与世界之间的界限远比你想象的更加模糊。当你走向精通时，你的大脑会因多年的实践和积极的实验而发生根本性的改变。它不再是过去那个简单的生态系统。大师的大脑拥有如此丰富的互联互通，以至于它变得与物质世界相似，成为一个充满活力的生态系统，所有形式的思维都在其中相互关联、相互联系。大脑与复杂生命本身之间日益增长的相似性，代表着最终回归现实。

STRATEGIES FOR ATTAINING MASTERY

精通策略

The intuitive mind is a sacred gift and the rational mind is a faithful servant. We have created a society that honors the servant and has forgotten the gift.

直觉是神圣的天赋，理性是忠实的仆人。我们创造了一个尊崇仆人而遗忘天赋的社会。

—A LBERT E INSTEIN

—阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦

Mastery is not a function of genius or talent. It is a function of time and intense focus applied to a particular field of knowledge. But there is another element, an X factor that Masters inevitably possess, that seems mystical but that is accessible to us all. Whatever field of activity we are involved in, there is generally an accepted path to the top. It is a path that others have followed, and because we are conformist creatures, most of us opt for this conventional route. But Masters have a strong inner guiding system and a high level of self-awareness. What has suited others in the past does not suit them, and they know that trying to fit into a conventional mold would only lead to a dampening of spirit, the reality they seek eluding them.

精通并非天才或天赋的产物，而是时间和对特定知识领域的专注的成果。但大师们必然拥有的另一个要素，一个X因素，看似神秘，实则人人皆可触及。无论我们从事哪个领域，通常都有一条通往巅峰的公认之路。这条路其他人也曾走过，而由于我们都是墨守成规的生物，大多数人都会选择这条传统的路线。但大师们拥有强大的内在指引系统和高度的自我认知。过去适合他人的东西并不适合他们，他们知道，试图融入传统的模式只会导致精神萎靡，他们所追求的现实也会随之消失。

And so inevitably, these Masters, as they progress on their career paths, make a choice at a key moment in their lives: they decide to forge their own route, one that others will see as unconventional, but that suits their own spirit and rhythms and leads them closer to discovering the hidden truths of their objects of study. This key choice takes self-confidence and self-awareness—the X factor that is necessary for attaining mastery. The following are examples of this X factor in action and the strategic choices it leads to. The examples given are meant to show the importance of this quality and how we might adapt it to our own circumstances.

因此，这些大师们在职业道路上不断前进时，不可避免地会在人生的关键时刻做出选择：他们决定开辟一条属于自己的道路，这条道路在旁人看来或许标新立异，但却符合他们自身的精神和节奏，并引领他们更接近发现研究对象背后隐藏的真理。这一关键抉择需要自信和自我认知——这是成就精通的必要X因素。以下列举了这一X因素的实际应用案例，以及它所带来的战略选择。这些案例旨在展现这一品质的重要性，以及我们如何根据自身情况进行调整。

# ↩

1. Connect to your environment—Primal Powers

1. 连接你的环境——原始力量

Among the many feats of human navigation of the sea, perhaps none are more remarkable and mysterious than the voyages of the indigenous peoples in the area known as Oceania—comprising the islands of Micronesia, Melanesia, and Polynesia. In an area that is 99.8 percent water, the inhabitants of this region were able for many centuries to deftly navigate the vast spaces between the islands. Some 1,500 years ago they managed to travel the several thousand miles to Hawaii, and perhaps at one point even voyaged as far as parts of North and South America, all in canoes with the same design and technology as those of the Stone Age. During the nineteenth century, mostly because of Western interference and the introduction of charts and compasses, these ancient navigating skills died out, and the source of their uncanny skill remained mostly a mystery. But in the area of Micronesia known as the Caroline Islands, certain islanders maintained the ancient traditions well into the twentieth century. And the first Westerners who traveled with them were astonished at what they witnessed.

在人类众多航海壮举中，或许没有比大洋洲（由密克罗尼西亚、美拉尼西亚和波利尼西亚三个岛屿组成）原住民的航海更令人瞩目和神秘的了。在这片99.8%被海水覆盖的土地上，数百年来，这里的居民能够娴熟地在岛屿间的广阔空间中航行。大约1500年前，他们航行数千英里到达夏威夷，甚至一度远至南北美洲的部分地区，而他们所驾驶的独木舟，其设计和技术与石器时代相同。19世纪，主要由于西方势力的干涉以及海图和指南针的传入，这些古老的航海技艺逐渐消亡，而他们这门神奇技艺的来源，至今仍是一个谜。但在密克罗尼西亚的卡罗林群岛，一些岛民却将这一古老传统一直传承到20世纪。第一批与他们一起旅行的西方人对他们所目睹的景象感到惊讶。

The Islanders would travel in outrigger canoes fitted with a sail with three or four men aboard, one serving as the chief navigator. They had no charts or instruments of any kind, and for the Westerners who accompanied them this could be a disconcerting experience. Taking off at night or day (it didn’t matter to them), there would be apparently nothing to guide them along the way. The islands were so far apart that one could travel for days without spotting land. To go off course only slightly (and storms or weather changes could certainly cause that) would mean never spotting their destination, and probably death—it would take too long to find the next island in the chain, and supplies would run out. And yet they would embark on their sea voyages with a remarkably relaxed spirit.

岛民们会乘坐装有帆的舷外支架独木舟出行，船上载有三到四名船员，其中一人担任首席领航员。他们没有任何海图或仪器，对于随行的西方人来说，这可能是一次令人不安的经历。无论白天还是夜晚出发（这对他们来说并不重要），沿途似乎都没有任何东西可以指引他们。岛屿之间相距甚远，人们可能航行数日都看不到陆地。即使只是稍微偏离航线（风暴或天气变化肯定会造成这种情况），也意味着永远找不到目的地，甚至可能丧命——找到岛链中的下一个岛屿需要很长时间，而且补给也会耗尽。然而，他们仍然会以一种异常轻松的精神踏上海上航行。

The chief navigator would occasionally glance at the night sky or the position of the sun, but mostly he talked with the others or stared straight ahead. Sometimes one of the men would lie belly down in the middle of the outrigger canoe and report some information he had gleaned. In general they gave the impression of being passengers on a train, serenely taking in the passing scenery. They seemed even calmer at night. When they were supposedly getting closer to their destination, they would become slightly more alert. They would follow the paths of birds in the sky; they would look deeply into the water, which they would sometimes cup in their hands and smell. When they arrived at their destination, it was all with the air of pulling into the train station on time. They seemed to know exactly how long it would take and how many supplies were required for the voyage. Along the way, they would make perfect adjustments to any changes in weather or currents.

首席领航员偶尔会瞥一眼夜空或太阳的位置，但大多数时候他都在和其他人交谈，或者直视前方。有时，有人会趴在独木舟的中央，汇报他收集到的信息。总的来说，他们给人的感觉就像火车上的乘客，静静地欣赏着沿途的风景。夜晚，他们显得更加平静。当他们即将接近目的地时，他们会变得更加警觉。他们会追寻天空中鸟儿的踪迹；他们会深深地凝视着水面，有时还会用手捧着水闻一闻。当他们到达目的地时，一切都像是准时到达火车站一样。他们似乎清楚地知道航行需要多长时间，需要多少补给。一路上，他们会根据天气或水流的变化做出完美的调整。

Curious as to how this was possible, some Westerners asked to be initiated into their secrets, and over the decades such travelers managed to piece together the system the Islanders used. As these Westerners discovered, one of their principal means of navigation was following the paths of stars in the night sky. Over the course of centuries, they had devised a chart comprising the path of fourteen different constellations. These constellations, along with the sun and the moon, described arcs in the sky that could translate into thirty-two different directions around the circle of the horizon. These arcs remained the same, no matter the season. From their own island, they could map out the location of all of the islands in their area by locating what stars they should be under at particular moments at night, and they knew how this position would change to another star as they traveled toward their destination. The Islanders had no writing system. Apprentice navigators simply had to memorize this elaborate map, which was in continual motion.

一些西方人好奇这究竟是如何实现的，于是请求了解他们的秘密。几十年来，这些旅行者设法拼凑出岛民使用的导航系统。这些西方人发现，他们主要的导航方式之一是追踪夜空中星辰的轨迹。几个世纪以来，他们绘制了一张包含十四个不同星座轨迹的星图。这些星座与太阳和月亮一起，在天空中划出弧线，这些弧线可以沿着地平线旋转三十二个不同的方向。无论季节如何，这些弧线都保持不变。在他们自己的岛上，他们可以通过确定夜晚特定时刻应该位于哪颗星辰下方来绘制出其所在区域所有岛屿的位置，并且他们知道在前往目的地的过程中，这个位置会如何变化。岛民没有书写系统。航海学徒只需记住这张不断移动的复杂地图即可。

During the day, they would chart a course by the sun. Toward the middle of the day they could read the exact direction they were headed in by the shadows that were cast on the mast. At dawn or at sunset they could use the moon, or the stars sinking below the horizon or starting to rise. To help them measure the distance they had covered, they would choose an island somewhere off to the side as a reference point. By following the stars in the sky they could calculate when they would be passing by this reference island, and how much time remained to reach their destination.

白天，他们会根据太阳绘制航线。到了中午，他们可以通过桅杆上投射的阴影来确定确切的方向。黎明或日落时分，他们可以利用月亮，或者正在沉入地平线或开始升起的星星。为了测量已经航行的距离，他们会选择一处偏僻的岛屿作为参考点。通过追踪天空中的星星，他们可以计算出何时会经过这个参考岛屿，以及距离目的地还有多长时间。

As part of this system, they envisioned that their canoe was completely still—the stars moved above them, and the islands in the ocean were moving toward and then away from them as they passed them. Acting as if the canoe were stationary made it easier to calculate their position within their reference system. Although they knew that islands did not move, after many years of traveling this way, they would literally experience the trip as if they were sitting still. This would account for the impression they gave of looking like passengers in a train viewing the passing landscape.

作为这个系统的一部分，他们设想独木舟完全静止——星辰在他们上方移动，海洋中的岛屿在他们经过时向他们靠近，然后又远离他们。假设独木舟静止不动，更容易计算他们在参考系中的位置。虽然他们知道岛屿不会移动，但经过多年的这种旅行，他们会体验到如同静止不动的旅程。这解释了他们给人的印象，就像火车上的乘客一样，欣赏着路过的风景。

Their sky chart was complemented by dozens of other signs they had learned to read. In their apprenticeship system, young navigators would be taken to sea and made to float in the ocean for several hours. In this way, they could learn to distinguish the various currents by how they felt on their skin. After much practice, they could read these currents by lying down on the floor of the canoe. They had developed a similar sensitivity to winds, and could identify various wind currents by how they moved the hairs on their head, or the sail on the outrigger.

除了星图之外，他们还学会了解读其他几十种星座。在学徒制度下，年轻的航海家会被带到海上，在海上漂浮数小时。通过这种方式，他们学会了通过皮肤上的感觉来辨别不同的洋流。经过大量的练习，他们甚至可以躺在独木舟的船底来解读这些洋流。他们对风的敏感度也与此类似，可以通过头发或舷外支架上帆的摆动来识别不同的风向。

Once they approached an island, they knew how to interpret the paths of land birds, which left in the morning to fish or returned at dusk to their homes. They could read the changes in the phosphorescence of the water that indicated closeness to land, and they could gauge whether the clouds in the distance were reflecting land beneath them, or simply ocean. They could touch the water to their lips, sensing any changes in temperature that indicated they were approaching an island. There were many more such indicators; the Islanders had learned to see everything in this environment as a potential sign.

一旦接近岛屿，他们就知道如何解读陆鸟的路径，这些鸟类清晨飞离捕鱼，黄昏归巢。他们能够解读水面磷光的变化，以此判断距离陆地的距离；他们还能判断远处的云层反射的是陆地，还是仅仅是海洋。他们可以用嘴唇触摸水面，感受任何温度的变化，以此判断他们正在接近岛屿。类似的迹象还有很多；岛民们已经学会将这种环境中的一切都视为潜在的征兆。

What was most remarkable was that the chief navigator hardly seemed to be paying attention to this complex network of signs. Only an occasional glance upward or downward would indicate any kind of reading that was going on. Apparently, Master navigators knew the sky chart so well that with the sight of one star in the sky they could immediately sense where all of the others were located. They had learned how to read the other navigational signs so well that it all had become second nature. They had a complete feel for this environment, including all of the variables that seemed to make it so chaotic and dangerous. As one Westerner put it, such Masters could travel hundreds of miles from island to island as easily as an experienced cab driver could negotiate the labyrinthine streets of London.

最令人称奇的是，首席航海家似乎几乎没怎么留意这复杂的标志网络。只有偶尔抬头或低头一看，才能发现任何读数。显然，大师级航海家对星图了如指掌，只要看到天空中的一颗星星，就能立刻感知到其他所有星星的位置。他们已经熟练地掌握了其他导航标志的解读方法，几乎成了他们的第二天性。他们对这片环境有着完全的感知，包括所有使其如此混乱和危险的变量。正如一位西方人所说，这样的大师级航海家可以轻松地从一个岛屿行驶数百英里，另一个岛屿之间，就像经验丰富的出租车司机在伦敦迷宫般的街道上穿梭一样。

At some point in history, the original navigators in this region must have felt a great degree of fear as they confronted the need to travel to find other food sources, realizing the tremendous dangers this involved. The ocean must have seemed much more chaotic than the tiny patch of land on their islands. They slowly overcame this fear and evolved a system that was magnificently suited to the environment they lived in. In this part of the world, the night sky is particularly clear through much of the year, giving them the ability to use the changing position of stars to great effect. Using smaller craft allowed them to maintain closer contact with the water, which they had learned to read as accurately as the undulating earth on their island. Imagining themselves as stationary and the islands as moving helped them keep track of their reference points and had a calming effect. They did not depend on a single tool or instrument; this elaborate system existed entirely in their minds. By building a deep connection to the environment and reading all of the available signs, the Islanders could approximate the remarkable instinctual powers of animals, such as various bird species that can navigate around the globe through their extreme sensitivity to the earth’s geomagnetic field.

在历史上的某个时期，最初抵达该地区的航海家们在面对寻找其他食物来源的需要时，一定感到了极大的恐惧，因为他们意识到其中蕴含的巨大危险。海洋肯定比他们岛屿上那一小块陆地更加混乱。他们慢慢克服了这种恐惧，并发展出一套非常适合他们所处环境的系统。在这个地区，一年中大部分时间的夜空都格外清澈，这使得他们能够有效地利用星星位置的变化。使用较小的船只使他们能够与海水保持更密切的联系，他们已经学会了像解读岛上起伏的地面一样精准地解读海水。想象自己静止不动，而岛屿在移动，这有助于他们追踪参考点，并产生镇定的作用。他们不依赖任何单一的工具或仪器；这套精妙的系统完全存在于他们的脑海中。通过与环境建立深度联系并解读所有可用的迹象，岛民可以模仿动物非凡的本能力量，例如各种鸟类可以通过对地球地磁场的极端敏感性在全球范围内导航。

Understand: the ability to connect deeply to your environment is the most primal and in many ways the most powerful form of mastery the brain can bring us. It applies equally well to the waters of Micronesia as it does to any modern field or office. We gain such power by first transforming ourselves into consummate observers. We see everything in our surroundings as a potential sign to interpret. Nothing is taken at face value. Like the Islanders, we can break these observations down into various systems. There are the people with whom we work and interact—everything they do and say reveals something hidden below the surface. We can look at our interactions with the public, how they respond to our work, how people’s tastes are constantly in flux. We can immerse ourselves in every aspect of our field, paying deep attention, for example, to the economic factors that play such a large role. We become like the Proustian spider, sensing the slightest vibration on our web. Over the years, as we progress on this path, we begin to merge our knowledge of these various components into an overall feel for the environment itself. Instead of exerting and overtaxing ourselves to keep up with a complex, changing environment, we know it from the inside and can sense the changes before they happen.

要知道：与周围环境深度连接的能力是大脑所能赋予我们的最原始、在很多方面也是最强大的掌控力。它不仅适用于密克罗尼西亚的水域，也适用于任何现代领域或办公室。我们获得这种力量，首先是将自己转变为完美的观察者。我们将周围的一切视为潜在的、值得解读的信号。任何事物都不会被表面所解读。像岛民一样，我们可以将这些观察分解成不同的系统。我们与之共事互动的人——他们的一言一行都揭示了隐藏在表面之下的真谛。我们可以观察与公众的互动，他们对我们工作的反应，以及人们的品味如何不断变化。我们可以沉浸在我们领域的各个方面，例如，深入关注那些发挥着巨大作用的经济因素。我们会变得像普鲁斯特笔下的蜘蛛一样，能够感知蛛网上最细微的震动。随着时间的推移，随着我们在这条道路上不断前进，我们开始将对这些不同组成部分的了解融合成对环境本身的整体感受。我们不需要费尽心机去适应复杂多变的环境，而是从内部了解环境，在变化发生之前就能感知到变化。

For the Caroline Islanders, there was nothing unconventional in their approach to mastery; their method fit perfectly their circumstances. But for us, in our advanced technological age, such mastery involves making an unconventional choice. To become such sensitive observers, we must not succumb to all of the distractions afforded by technology; we must be a little primitive. The primary instruments that we depend on must be our eyes for observing and our brains for analyzing. The information afforded to us through various media is only one small component in our connection to the environment. It is easy to become enamored with the powers that technology affords us, and to see them as the end and not the means. When that happens, we connect to a virtual environment, and the power of our eyes and brain slowly atrophy. You must see your environment as a physical entity and your connection to it as visceral. If there is any instrument you must fall in love with and fetishize, it is the human brain—the most miraculous, awe-inspiring, information-processing tool devised in the known universe, with a complexity we can’t even begin to fathom, and with dimensional powers that far outstrip any piece of technology in sophistication and usefulness.

对于卡罗琳群岛的居民来说，他们掌控事物的方式并无不寻常之处；他们的方法完美契合自身处境。但对于我们这个科技发达的时代，掌控事物需要做出非同寻常的选择。要成为如此敏锐的观察者，我们不能屈服于科技带来的所有干扰；我们必须保持一些原始的本能。我们赖以生存的主要工具必须是我们观察的眼睛和分析的大脑。通过各种媒介获得的信息只是我们与环境联系的一小部分。我们很容易沉迷于科技赋予我们的力量，并将其视为最终目标而非手段。当这种情况发生时，我们连接到虚拟环境，我们眼睛和大脑的力量就会逐渐萎缩。你必须将你的环境视为一个物理实体，并将你与它的联系视为本能的。如果有什么工具会让你爱上并迷恋它，那就是人类的大脑——这是已知宇宙中最神奇、最令人敬畏的信息处理工具，它的复杂性是我们无法想象的，其维度力量在复杂性和实用性方面远远超过任何技术。

# ↩

2. Play to your strengths—Supreme Focus

2. 发挥你的优势——高度专注

A. In the first years of the life of their child, the parents of Albert Einstein (1879–1955) had cause for concern. It took longer than usual for little Albert to talk, and his first attempts at language were always so halting. (See here and here for more on Einstein.) He had a strange habit of first muttering to himself the words he was going to speak out loud. His parents were concerned that their son might have a mental deficiency, and they consulted a doctor. Soon, however, he lost his hesitancy with words and revealed some hidden mental strengths—he was good with puzzles, had a knack for certain sciences, and he loved playing the violin, particularly anything by Mozart, whose music he would play over and over.

答：在孩子出生后的最初几年，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦（1879-1955）的父母曾一度担忧。小阿尔伯特比一般孩子学说话的时间更长，而且他最初尝试说话总是磕磕绊绊。（更多关于爱因斯坦的信息，请参见此处和此处。）他有一个奇怪的习惯，总是先自言自语，然后才大声说出自己想要说的话。他的父母担心儿子可能有智力缺陷，于是咨询了医生。然而，很快，他便不再犹豫不决，展现出了一些隐藏的智力优势——他擅长解谜，对某些科学知识很有天赋，而且他喜欢拉小提琴，尤其是莫扎特的所有作品，他会一遍又一遍地演奏他的乐曲。

The problems began again, however, as he advanced his way through school. He was not a particularly good student. He hated having to memorize so many facts and numbers. He hated the stern authority of the teachers. His grades were mediocre and, concerned for his future, the parents decided to send their sixteen-year-old son to a more liberal-minded school in the town of Aarau, near their home in Zurich. This school used a method developed by the Swiss educational reformer Johann Pestalozzi, which emphasized the importance of learning through one’s own observations, leading to the development of ideas and intuitions. Even mathematics and physics were taught in this manner. There were no drills or facts to memorize; instead, the method placed supreme importance on visual forms of intelligence, which Pestalozzi saw as the key to creative thinking.

然而，随着他不断升学，问题再次出现。他并非一名特别优秀的学生。他讨厌死记硬背大量事实和数字，也讨厌老师的严厉权威。他的成绩平平，出于对未来发展的担忧，父母决定将16岁的儿子送到苏黎世家附近阿劳镇一所思想更为开明的学校。这所学校采用了瑞士教育改革家约翰·裴斯泰洛齐（Johann Pestalozzi）开发的方法，强调通过自身观察学习的重要性，从而促进思想和直觉的发展。甚至数学和物理也采用这种方式教学。这种方法没有练习题或需要死记硬背的事实；相反，它极其重视视觉形式的智力，裴斯泰洛齐认为这是创造性思维的关键。

In this atmosphere, young Einstein suddenly thrived. He found the place intensely stimulating. The school encouraged students to learn on their own, wherever their inclinations would take them, and for Einstein this meant delving even more deeply into Newtonian physics (a passion of his) and recent advances in the study of electromagnetism. In his studies of Newton while at Aarau, he came upon some problems in the Newtonian concept of the universe that deeply troubled him and caused him many sleepless nights.

在这样的氛围下，年轻的爱因斯坦突然蓬勃发展。他发现这里充满了激励。学校鼓励学生自学，无论他们的兴趣爱好是什么，对爱因斯坦来说，这意味着他可以更深入地钻研牛顿物理学（他最热衷的领域）以及电磁学研究的最新进展。在阿劳大学研究牛顿时，他发现了牛顿宇宙观中的一些问题，这些问题深深地困扰着他，让他许多个夜晚都难以入眠。

According to Newton, all phenomena in nature can be explained through simple mechanical laws. Knowing them, we can deduce the causes for almost everything that happens. Objects move through space according to these mechanical laws, such as laws of gravity, and all of these movements can be measured mathematically. It is a universe that is highly ordered and rational. But Newton’s concept relied upon two assumptions that could never be proven or verified empirically: the existence of absolute time and space, both of which were thought to exist independently of living beings and objects. Without these assumptions there would be no supreme standard of measurement. The brilliance of his system, however, was hard to call into question, considering that based on his laws scientists could accurately measure the movements of sound waves, the diffusion of gases, or the motion of stars.

牛顿认为，自然界的所有现象都可以用简单的力学定律来解释。了解这些定律后，我们几乎可以推断出所有事件的起因。物体在空间中运动遵循这些力学定律，例如引力定律，所有这些运动都可以用数学方法测量。这是一个高度有序且理性的宇宙。然而，牛顿的理论依赖于两个无法通过经验证明或验证的假设：绝对时间和空间的存在，这两者都被认为独立于生物和物体而存在。没有这些假设，就不会有最高的测量标准。然而，考虑到科学家能够基于他的定律精确测量声波的运动、气体的扩散或恒星的运动，他的体系的卓越性毋庸置疑。

In the late nineteenth century, however, certain cracks began to emerge in Newton’s concept of the mechanical universe. Based on the work of Michael Faraday, the great Scottish mathematician James Maxwell made some interesting discoveries about the properties of electromagnetism. Developing what became known as field theories, Maxwell asserted that electromagnetism should not be described in terms of charged particles, but rather in terms of fields in space that have the continual potential to be converted into electromagnetism; this field consists of vectors of stress that can be charged at any point. By his calculations, electromagnetic waves move at the speed of 186,000 miles per second, which happens to be the speed of light. This could not simply be some coincidence. Light must therefore be a visible manifestation of an entire spectrum of electromagnetic waves.

然而，十九世纪末，牛顿的机械宇宙观开始出现一些裂痕。伟大的苏格兰数学家詹姆斯·麦克斯韦基于迈克尔·法拉第的研究成果，对电磁学的性质做出了一些有趣的发现。麦克斯韦发展了后来被称为场论的理论，他断言电磁学不应用带电粒子来描述，而应用空间中的场来描述，这些场具有持续转化为电磁力的潜力；这种场由可以在任何一点带电的应力矢量组成。根据他的计算，电磁波的传播速度为每秒186,000英里，恰好是光速。这不可能仅仅是巧合。因此，光必定是整个电磁波谱的可见表现形式。

This was a groundbreaking and novel concept of the physical universe, but to make it consistent with Newton, Maxwell and others assumed the existence of a “light-bearing ether,” a substance that could oscillate and produce these electromagnetic waves, analogous to water for ocean waves, or air for sound waves. This concept added one more absolute to the Newtonian equation—that of absolute rest. The speed of the movement of these waves could only be measured against the backdrop of something at rest, which would be the ether itself. This ether would have to be something strange—covering the entire universe but not in any way interfering with the movement of planets or objects.

这是一个开创性的、新颖的物理宇宙概念，但为了与牛顿的理论相一致，麦克斯韦等人假设存在一种“载光以太”，这种物质能够振荡并产生电磁波，类似于水之于海浪，或空气之于声波。这个概念为牛顿方程增添了一个绝对值——绝对静止。这些波的运动速度只能以某种静止的物质为背景来测量，而这种静止的物质就是以太本身。这种以太必须是一种奇特的物质——覆盖整个宇宙，但又不会以任何方式干扰行星或物体的运动。

Scientists around the world had been struggling for decades to prove somehow the existence of this ether, concocting all sorts of elaborate experiments, but it seemed an impossible quest, and this raised increasingly more questions about the Newtonian universe and the absolutes on which it depended. Albert Einstein devoured everything he could about Maxwell’s work and the questions it raised. Einstein himself had a basic need to believe in laws, in the existence of an ordered universe, and experiencing doubts on these laws caused him great anxiety.

几十年来，世界各地的科学家一直在努力证明以太的存在，他们设计了各种复杂的实验，但这似乎是一个不可能完成的任务，也引发了人们对牛顿宇宙及其所依赖的绝对性越来越多的质疑。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦如饥似渴地阅读着麦克斯韦的著作及其提出的问题。爱因斯坦本人也渴望相信定律，相信有序宇宙的存在，而对这些定律的怀疑让他深感焦虑。

One day, in the midst of all of these thoughts and while still attending the school at Aarau, an image appeared in his mind: that of a man moving at the speed of light itself. As he pondered this image, it turned into a sort of puzzle, or what he would later call a thought experiment: if the man were moving at the speed of light alongside a light beam, he should be able to “observe such a beam of light as an electromagnetic field at rest though spatially oscillating.”

有一天，当他还在阿劳上学，思绪万千的时候，一个画面出现在他的脑海中：一个人以光速运动。当他思考这个画面时，它变成了一个谜题，或者说，他后来称之为一个思想实验：如果这个人以光速与一束光并排运动，他应该能够“观察到这束光，就像一个静止的电磁场，尽管它在空间上振荡”。

Intuitively, however, this made no sense to him for two reasons. The moment the man would look at the light source to see the beam, the light pulse would be moving ahead of him at the speed of light; he could not perceive it otherwise, since visible light travels at that constant speed. The speed of the light pulse with respect to the observer would still be 186,000 miles per second. The law governing the speed of light or any electromagnetic wave would have to be the same to someone standing still on Earth, or someone theoretically moving at the speed of light. There could not be two separate laws. And yet in theory it still could be supposed that one could catch up with and see the wave itself before it appeared as light. It was a paradox, and it made him unbearably anxious as he contemplated it.

然而，直觉上，这对他来说毫无意义，原因有二。当这个人看向光源看到光束时，光脉冲正以光速在他前方移动；否则他无法感知到它，因为可见光以光速恒定传播。光脉冲相对于观察者的速度仍然是每秒186,000英里。光速或任何电磁波的速度定律，对于静止在地球上的人，或理论上以光速运动的人，都必须是相同的。不可能存在两条独立的定律。然而，理论上仍然可以假设，人们可以在波以光的形式出现之前追上并看到它。这是一个悖论，当他思考这个问题时，他感到无比焦虑。

The next year Einstein entered the Zurich Polytechnic Institute, and once again his dislike for traditional schooling returned. He did not do particularly well at math. He disliked the way physics was taught, and he started taking many classes in totally unrelated fields. He was not a promising student, and had not attracted the attention of any important professor or mentor. He quickly developed a disdain for academia and the constrictions it placed on his thinking. Still deeply troubled by his thought experiment, he continued to work on it on his own. He spent months devising an experiment that could perhaps allow him to detect the ether and its effects on light, but a professor at the Polytechnic revealed to him that his experiment was unworkable. He gave Einstein a paper describing all of the failed attempts to detect ether that had been attempted by eminent scientists, perhaps trying to deflate the pretensions of a twenty-year-old student who thought he could uncover what the greatest scientists in the world had failed to accomplish.

第二年，爱因斯坦进入苏黎世理工学院，他对传统学校教育的厌恶再次复发。他的数学成绩并不特别好。他不喜欢物理的教学方式，开始选修许多完全不相关的课程。他并非一个有前途的学生，也没有引起任何重要教授或导师的关注。他很快就对学术界及其对他思维的束缚产生了厌恶。由于他的思想实验仍然深陷困扰，他继续独自研究。他花了几个月的时间设计一个实验，或许可以探测到以太及其对光的影响，但理工学院的一位教授告诉他，他的实验不可行。他给了爱因斯坦一篇论文，其中描述了所有杰出科学家探测以太的失败尝试，或许是为了打消这位二十岁学生的自负，因为他自以为能够发现世界上最伟大的科学家们都未能完成的事情。

A year later, in 1900, Einstein came to a life-changing decision about himself: He was not an experimental scientist. He was not good at devising experiments and he did not enjoy the process. He had several strengths—he was a marvel at solving abstract puzzles of any kind; he could turn them over in his mind, converting them into images he could manipulate and shape at will. And because of his natural disdain of authority and conventions, he could think in ways that were novel and flexible. This meant of course that he would never succeed in the slippery world of academia. He would have to blaze his own path, but this could be an advantage. He would not be burdened by the need to fit in or adhere to the standard paradigm.

一年后，也就是1900年，爱因斯坦做出了一个改变人生的决定：他不是一名实验科学家。他不擅长设计实验，也不喜欢实验过程。他有一些优势——他擅长解决各种抽象的难题；他可以在脑海中反复思考，将它们转化为可以随意操控和塑造的图像。而且，由于他天生不屑于权威和惯例，他的思维方式新颖灵活。这当然意味着他永远无法在学术界这个捉摸不定的世界里取得成功。他必须开辟自己的道路，但这或许也是一种优势。他不必被迎合或墨守成规所束缚。

Continuing to work on his thought experiment day and night, he finally came to a conclusion—something had to be wrong with the entire notion of the physical universe as described by Newton. Scientists were going at the problem from the wrong end: they were straining to prove the existence of the ether in order to maintain the Newtonian edifice. Although Einstein admired Newton, he had no ties to any school of thought. Considering his decision to work on his own, he could be as daring as he liked. He would throw out the idea of the ether itself and all of the absolutes that could not be verified. His way forward would be to deduce the laws, the principles that governed motion, through his reasoning powers and through mathematics. He did not need a university position or any laboratory to do this. Wherever he found himself, he could work on these problems.

他日夜不停地进行着他的思想实验，最终得出结论——牛顿所描述的整个物理宇宙概念肯定出了问题。科学家们从错误的角度来解决这个问题：他们竭力证明以太的存在，以维护牛顿的理论体系。爱因斯坦虽然钦佩牛顿，但他与任何学派都毫无关联。考虑到他决定独立研究，他可以随心所欲地大胆尝试。他会抛弃以太本身的概念以及所有无法验证的绝对真理。他的前进方向是通过他的推理能力和数学推导出运动的定律和原理。他不需要大学职位或任何实验室来做这件事。无论身在何处，他都可以研究这些问题。

As the years went by, it would seem to others that Einstein was a bit of a failure. He had graduated from the Polytechnic close to the bottom of his class. He could not find any kind of teaching job and had settled for a mediocre, low-paid position as an evaluator of inventions for the Swiss patent office in Bern. But free to continue on his own, he worked with unbelievable tenacity at this one problem. Even while apparently on the job at the patent office, he would focus for hours on the theory that was forming in his mind; even when out for a walk with friends, he would continue to ponder his ideas—he had the unusual ability to listen on one track and think on another. He carried with him a little notebook and filled it up with all kinds of ideas. He reflected on his original paradox and all of the embellishments it had undergone and played around with them endlessly in his mind, imagining a thousand different possibilities. During almost every waking hour he contemplated the problem from some angle or other.

随着岁月的流逝，在别人眼中，爱因斯坦似乎有些失败。他从理工学院毕业时，成绩几乎垫底。他找不到任何教职，只能在伯尔尼的瑞士专利局做一份平庸低薪的发明评估员。但他可以自由地继续自己的事业，并以令人难以置信的毅力攻克这个难题。即使表面上在专利局工作，他也会连续数小时专注于脑海中正在形成的理论；即使和朋友一起散步，他也会继续思考自己的想法——他拥有一种非凡的能力，能听出一个方向，却又想到另一个方向。他随身带着一个小笔记本，里面记满了各种各样的想法。他反思自己最初的悖论以及它所经历的所有修饰，并在脑海中不断地推演，想象出上千种不同的可能性。几乎在醒着的每一刻，他都会从各种角度思考这个问题。

In the course of his deep thinking, he came up with two important principles that would guide him further. First, he determined that his original intuition had to be correct—the laws of physics had to apply equally to someone at rest as to someone traveling at a uniform speed in a spaceship. Nothing else would make sense. And second, that the speed of light was a constant. Even if a star moving at several thousand miles per hour emitted light, the speed of such light would remain at 186,000 miles per second and not any faster. In this way he would adhere to Maxwell’s law on the invariable speed of electromagnetic waves.

在深入思考的过程中，他提出了两个重要的原则，它们将指引他进一步前进。首先，他认定自己最初的直觉必然正确——物理定律必须同样适用于静止的人和在宇宙飞船中匀速行进的人。其他任何定律都站不住脚。其次，光速是一个常数。即使一颗以每小时数千英里运动的恒星发出光，其光速也将保持在每秒186,000英里，不会更快。这样，他就遵循了麦克斯韦关于电磁波速度不变的定律。

As he contemplated these principles further, however, another paradox emerged in his mind in the shape of yet another image. He imagined a train speeding along a track with its lights beaming. A man standing on the embankment would see the light of the beam moving at the expected speed. But what if a woman were running toward or away from the train on the tracks? The woman’s speed relative to the train would depend on how quickly she was moving and in which direction, but wouldn’t it be the same with the light beam? Certainly, the light beam from the train relative to the woman would travel at a different speed if she were running away or running toward it, and the speed of this beam would be different from the speed relative to the man on the tracks. This one image seemingly called into question all of his guiding principles up until then.

然而，当他进一步思考这些原则时，另一个悖论以另一幅图像的形式浮现在他的脑海中。他想象一列火车沿着轨道飞驰，车灯闪烁。站在路堤上的男人会看到光束以预期的速度移动。但如果一个女人在轨道上朝着火车跑去或逃离呢？女人相对于火车的速度取决于她移动的速度和方向，但光束的速度不也一样吗？当然，如果女人朝着火车跑去或逃离火车，火车光束相对于女人的速度会有所不同，这束光的速度也不同于相对于轨道上男人的速度。这幅图像似乎使他迄今为止的所有指导原则都受到了质疑。

For months he pondered this paradox, and by May 1905 he had decided to give up the entire matter. It seemed beyond solution. On a beautiful, sunny day in Bern, he walked with a friend and colleague from the patent office, explaining to him the dead end he had reached, his frustration, and his decision to give up. Just as he said all of this, as Einstein later recalled, “I suddenly understood the key to the problem.” It came to him in a grand, intuitive flash, first with an image and then with words—a split-second insight that would forever alter our own concept of the universe.

他思考了这个悖论好几个月，到了1905年5月，他决定彻底放弃。因为这似乎无解。在伯尔尼一个阳光明媚的日子里，他和一位朋友兼专利局同事一起散步，向他解释了自己陷入的困境、他的挫败感以及他放弃的决定。就在他说完这些话的时候，爱因斯坦后来回忆道：“我突然明白了问题的症结所在。” 一瞬间，他灵光一闪，先是一幅图像，然后是文字——这瞬间的顿悟永远地改变了我们对宇宙的理解。

Later Einstein would illustrate his insight through the following image: Suppose a train is moving past an embankment at a constant velocity. A man stands in the center of the embankment. Just as the train moves by, lightning strikes simultaneously at two equidistant points, A and B, to the right and left of the man. Suppose there is a woman seated in the middle of the train, who is passing just in front of the man on the embankment as the lightning strikes. She will be moving closer to point B as the light signal travels. She will see it strike ever so slightly ahead of the lightning at point A. What is simultaneous for the man on the embankment is not so for the woman on the train. No two events can ever be said to be simultaneous, because every moving reference frame has its own relative time, and everything in the universe is moving in relation to something else. As Einstein put it, “There is no audible tick-tock everywhere in the world that can be considered as time.” If time is not absolute, then neither is space or distance. Everything is relative to everything else—speed, time, distance, and so on—except for the speed of light, which never changes.

后来，爱因斯坦用以下的比喻来阐述他的洞见：假设一列火车以恒定速度驶过路堤。一名男子站在路堤中央。火车驶过时，闪电同时击中该男子左右两侧等距的两个点A和B。假设火车中央坐着一名女子，闪电击中时，她正从路堤上男子的正前方经过。随着光信号的传播，她将靠近B点。她将看到闪电击中A点的时间略早于闪电击中的时间。对于路堤上男子来说是同时发生的事情，对于火车上女子来说却并非如此。任何两件事都不能被称为同时发生，因为每个运动的参考系都有其自身的相对时间，宇宙中的一切都是相对于其他事物运动的。正如爱因斯坦所说：“世界上没有任何一个地方可以听到的滴答声可以被认为是时间。”如果时间不是绝对的，那么空间和距离也不是绝对的。速度、时间、距离等等一切都是相对的，除了光速，它永远不变。

This was called his theory of Simple Relativity, and in the years to come it would shake the foundations of physics and science. Several years later, Einstein would repeat the exact same process for his discovery of General Relativity and what he called the “curvature of spacetime,” applying relativity to gravitational force. He again began with an image, a thought experiment that he pondered for close to ten years, leading to his breakthrough theory in 1915. From this theory alone he deduced that the course of light rays must be bent by the curvature of spacetime, and had gone even further to speculate the exact bend of the arc for rays of starlight grazing the sun. To the astonishment of scientists and the public alike, during the solar eclipse of 1919, astronomers were able to precisely verify Einstein’s speculation. It seemed that only someone with superhuman brain capabilities could deduce such a measurement simply through abstract reasoning. The fame and reputation of Albert Einstein as a freakish genius was born at that moment and has remained ever since.

这就是他的“简单相对论”，并在随后的岁月中撼动了物理学和科学的基石。几年后，爱因斯坦重复了同样的过程，发现了广义相对论以及他所谓的“时空曲率”，将相对论应用于引力。他再次从一幅图像开始，进行了一个思想实验，并为此思考了近十年，最终在1915年提出了突破性的理论。仅凭这一理论，他就推断出光线的路径必定会因时空曲率而弯曲，甚至更进一步推测了星光掠过太阳时弧线的确切弯曲程度。令科学家和公众都感到惊讶的是，在1919年的日食期间，天文学家能够精确地验证爱因斯坦的推测。似乎只有拥有超人大脑能力的人才能仅凭抽象推理就推导出这样的测量结果。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦作为天才的名声和声誉从那一刻诞生，并一直延续至今。

Although we like to assume that a genius like Albert Einstein had powers far beyond our capabilities, his great discoveries depended on two very simple decisions he made as a young man. First, at the age of twenty he determined that he would be a mediocre experimental scientist. Even though a heavy immersion in mathematics and experimentation was the conventional route in physics, he would go his own way—a daring decision. Second, he would consider his primal distaste for authority and conventions as a great strength. He would attack from the outside and unburden himself of all the assumptions that were torturing scientists in relation to Newton. These two decisions allowed him to play to his strengths. A third factor can be identified as well: his love of the violin and the music of Mozart. To others who would marvel at his feel for Mozart, he would reply, “It’s in my blood.” He meant that he had played this music so often that it had become part of him, his essence. He had an inside understanding of the music. This would become the unconscious model for his approach to science: he would think himself inside complex phenomena.

尽管我们总认为像阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦这样的天才拥有远超我们人类的能力，但他的伟大发现却源于他年轻时做出的两个非常简单的决定。首先，二十岁时，他就决心成为一名平庸的实验科学家。尽管沉浸于数学和实验是物理学的传统路线，但他却坚持走自己的路——这是一个大胆的决定。其次，他认为自己对权威和传统的本能厌恶是一股强大的力量。他从外部发起挑战，摆脱所有那些困扰着牛顿科学家的固有观念。这两个决定让他得以充分发挥自己的优势。此外，还有第三个因素：他对小提琴和莫扎特音乐的热爱。当有人惊叹他对莫扎特音乐的感受时，他会回答：“它融入了我的血液。”他的意思是，他经常演奏莫扎特的音乐，以至于它已经成为他的一部分，他的本质。他对莫扎特音乐有着深入的理解。这将成为他研究科学的无意识模型：他会认为自己处于复杂的现象之中。

Although we tend to imagine Einstein as the ultimate abstract thinker, his way of thinking was remarkably concrete—almost always in terms of images that related to the everyday objects around him, such as trains, clocks, and elevators. Thinking in this concrete way, he could turn a problem over and over in his mind, consider it from all angles while walking, talking to others, or sitting at his desk at the patent office. He would later explain that imagination and intuition played a far larger role in his discoveries than his knowledge of science and mathematics. If he had any qualities that were extraordinary, they were his patience mixed with his extreme tenacity. After what can only be considered as well beyond 10,000 hours of contemplation of one problem, he reached a transformation point. The various aspects of a supremely complicated phenomenon had become internalized, leading to an intuitive grasp of the whole—in this case, the sudden image that came to him revealing the relativity of time. His two theories of relativity have to be considered as perhaps the greatest intellectual feats in history, the fruits of intense labor and not of some extraordinary, inexplicable genius.

尽管我们倾向于将爱因斯坦视为终极抽象思想家，但他的思维方式却异常具体——几乎总是以与他周围日常事物相关的图像来呈现，例如火车、钟表和电梯。凭借这种具体的方式，他可以在脑海中反复思考一个问题，无论是在行走、与他人交谈，还是坐在专利局的办公桌前，都能从各个角度进行思考。他后来解释说，想象力和直觉在他的发现中发挥的作用远大于他对科学和数学的理解。如果说他有什么非凡的品质，那就是他的耐心与极强的毅力的结合。在对一个问题进行了远超一万小时的思考之后，他达到了一个转变点。一个极其复杂现象的各个方面都被内化，从而对整体有了直观的把握——在这种情况下，他脑海中突然浮现的图像揭示了时间的相对性。他的两种相对论或许可以被视为历史上最伟大的智力壮举，是辛勤劳动的成果，而不是某些非凡的、无法解释的天才的成果。

There are many paths to mastery, and if you are persistent you will certainly find one that suits you. But a key component in the process is determining your mental and psychological strengths and working with them. To rise to the level of mastery requires many hours of dedicated focus and practice. You cannot get there if your work brings you no joy and you are constantly struggling to overcome your own weaknesses. You must look deep within and come to an understanding of these particular strengths and weaknesses you possess, being as realistic as possible. Knowing your strengths, you can lean on them with utmost intensity. Once you start in this direction, you will gain momentum. You will not be burdened by conventions, and you will not be slowed down by having to deal with skills that go against your inclinations and strengths. In this way, your creative and intuitive powers will be naturally awakened.

通往精通的道路有很多，只要你坚持不懈，就一定能找到一条适合自己的道路。但其中的关键在于，明确你的精神和心理优势，并加以利用。要达到精通的境界，需要长时间的专注和练习。如果你的工作无法给你带来快乐，并且你总是努力克服自身的弱点，你就无法达到精通的境界。你必须深入内心，尽可能实事求是地理解你所拥有的这些优势和劣势。了解自己的优势，你就能最大限度地利用它们。一旦你朝着这个方向迈进，你就会获得动力。你不会被陈规旧俗所束缚，也不会因为需要处理与你的倾向和优势相悖的技能而放慢脚步。这样，你的创造力和直觉力就会自然而然地被唤醒。

B. In thinking back to her earliest years in the 1950s, Temple Grandin could only recall a dark and chaotic world. Born with autism, she could remember spending hours on the beach watching grains of sand pour through her hands. (For more on Grandin see here and here .) She lived in a world of constant terrors—any sudden noise would overwhelm her.
