It took her much longer than other children to learn language, and as she slowly did, she became painfully aware of how different she was from other children. Often alone, she naturally gravitated toward animals, particularly horses. It was more than just a need for companionship—she somehow felt an unusual identification and empathy with the world of animals. Her great passion was to go horseback riding in the country around Boston where she was raised. In riding horses, she could deepen her connection to them.

B. 回想起20世纪50年代的童年，坦普·格兰丁只记得那是一个黑暗混乱的世界。她天生患有自闭症，记得自己曾在海滩上度过数小时，看着沙子从手中流过。（更多关于格兰丁的信息，请参见此处和此处。）她生活在一个充满恐惧的世界里——任何突如其来的噪音都会让她不知所措。她比其他孩子花了更长的时间来学习语言，而随着学习的逐渐深入，她痛苦地意识到自己与其他孩子的不同。她经常独自一人，自然而然地被动物吸引，尤其是马。这不仅仅是出于对陪伴的需求——不知何故，她对动物世界产生了一种不同寻常的认同感和同理心。她最大的爱好是在她长大的波士顿周边的乡村骑马。骑马能加深她与马的联系。

Then one summer, as a young girl, she was sent to visit her Aunt Ann, who had a ranch in Arizona. Temple felt an instant connection with the cattle on the ranch, and she would watch them for hours. What particularly intrigued her was the squeeze chute they would enter to be vaccinated. The pressure from the side panels of the chute was designed to help relax them while they were injected.

后来的一个夏天，年幼的她被送去探望在亚利桑那州拥有牧场的安姨妈。坦普尔立刻对牧场上的牛群产生了一种亲近感，她会一连观察它们好几个小时。尤其让她着迷的是牛群接种疫苗时要进入的挤压槽。挤压槽侧板的压力是为了帮助牛群在注射时放松下来而设计的。

As far back as she could remember, she had always been trying to wrap herself in blankets or bury herself under cushions and pillows to somehow feel squeezed. As with the cows, any sort of gradual compression would relax her. (As is common for autistic children, being hugged by humans was overstimulating for her and induced anxiety; she had no control over the experience.) She had long dreamed about some kind of device that could squeeze her, and seeing the cattle in the chute she realized the answer. One day she begged her aunt to let her into the chute to be squeezed like a cow, and the aunt agreed. For thirty minutes she experienced what she had always wanted, and afterwards felt a complete calmness. It was at such a moment that she realized that she had some kind of strange connection to cattle, that her destiny was somehow tied up with these animals.

从她记事起，她就一直试图用毯子裹住自己，或者把自己埋在垫子和枕头下，感受被挤压的感觉。就像奶牛一样，任何逐渐的挤压都能让她放松。（就像自闭症儿童常见的情况一样，被人拥抱对她来说是一种过度刺激，并引发焦虑；她无法控制这种体验。）她一直梦想着某种可以挤压她的装置，看到滑槽里的牛，她顿悟了答案。有一天，她恳求姑姑让她进入滑槽，像牛一样被挤压，姑姑同意了。在三十分钟里，她体验到了一直渴望的感觉，之后感到彻底的平静。正是在那一刻，她意识到自己与牛有着某种奇特的联系，她的命运与这些动物息息相关。

Curious about this connection, a few years later in high school she decided to research the subject of cattle. She also wanted to find out whether other autistic children and adults felt the same way. She could find very little information on cattle and their emotions or how they might experience the world; there was much more on autism, and she devoured books on the subject. In this way, she discovered an interest in the sciences; doing research allowed her to channel her nervous energy and learn about the world. She had tremendous powers to focus completely on one subject.

出于对这种联系的好奇，几年后，在高中时，她决定研究牛。她也想了解其他自闭症儿童和成人是否也有同样的感受。她几乎找不到关于牛及其情绪或它们如何体验世界的信息；而关于自闭症的资料却很多，她如饥似渴地阅读了这方面的书籍。就这样，她发现了自己对科学的兴趣；做研究让她能够疏导紧张的情绪，了解世界。她拥有强大的力量，可以全身心地投入到一个主题上。

Slowly, she transformed herself into a promising student, which allowed her to gain admittance into a liberal arts school in New Hampshire where she majored in psychology. She had chosen the field because of her interest in autism—she had a personal, inside knowledge of the subject, and following this major would help her to understand more of the science behind the phenomenon. After graduating, she decided to pursue a PhD in psychology at Arizona State University, but when she went back to the Southwest and visited her aunt, she reconnected with her childhood fascination with cattle. Not really knowing why or what it would lead to, she decided to switch her major to animal sciences. For her thesis, she would focus largely on cattle.

慢慢地，她蜕变成一名有前途的学生，并被新罕布什尔州一所文理学院录取，主修心理学。她选择这个专业是因为她对自闭症感兴趣——她对这个领域有着切身的了解，而攻读这个专业将有助于她更深入地理解这一现象背后的科学原理。毕业后，她决定在亚利桑那州立大学攻读心理学博士学位，但当她回到美国西南部探望姑妈时，童年时对牛的迷恋又重新燃起。她并不清楚原因，也不知道这会带来什么结果，于是决定转专业到动物科学。她的论文将主要关注牛。

Grandin had always done much of her thinking in visual terms, often having to translate words into images before she could understand them. Perhaps this was the result of the unique wiring of her brain. As part of the fieldwork for her major, she visited a couple of cattle feedlots in the state, and she was appalled by what she saw. It suddenly became clear to her that her propensity to think in visual terms was not shared by most others. How else to explain the highly irrational design of many of these feedlots and the remarkable lack of attention paid to details that were so visible to her eyes?

格兰丁一直以来都以视觉思维进行思考，常常需要将文字转化为图像才能理解。这或许源于她独特的大脑结构。作为专业田野调查的一部分，她参观了该州的几个牛饲养场，眼前的景象让她震惊不已。她突然意识到，她这种以视觉思维思考的倾向并非大多数人所共有。否则，如何解释这些饲养场中许多极其不合理的设计，以及人们对那些在她眼中显而易见的细节如此漠不关心呢？

She would watch with dismay as the animals were herded through cattle chutes that were far too slippery. She would imagine what it must feel like to be a 1,200 pound animal suddenly sensing a loss of control on surfaces that were clearly too slick. The animals would bellow and stop in their tracks as they slid into one another, causing a sudden pileup. At one feedlot, almost all of the cows would stop at the same point; something in their visual field was obviously terrifying them. Didn’t anyone stop to consider what was causing this? At another feedlot, she witnessed the horrifying spectacle of cattle being herded onto ramps leading to a dip vat—a pool of water full of disinfectant to help rid them of ticks and parasites. The ramp was too steep and the drop into the water too great; some of the cattle would tumble upside down into the pool and drown.

她会惊恐地看着牛群被赶过滑得不行的牛槽。她会想象一头1200磅重的牛在明显太滑的路面上突然失去控制会是什么感觉。牛群会大声吼叫并停下脚步，互相撞在一起，导致突然的连环相撞。在一个饲养场，几乎所有的牛都会停在同一个地方；显然，它们的视野中有什么东西吓到了它们。难道没有人停下来想想是什么原因造成的吗？在另一个饲养场，她目睹了令人恐惧的景象：牛群被赶上通往浸水池的斜坡——一个装满消毒剂的水池，可以帮助它们去除蜱虫和寄生虫。斜坡太陡，落差太大；有些牛会头朝下翻入水池溺水身亡。

Based on what she had seen, she decided to do a detailed analysis of the efficiency of these feedlots, and how they could be improved, for her master’s thesis. She now visited dozens of these sites, and each time she would stand close to the chutes, recording the reactions of the cattle as they were branded and vaccinated. On her own, she would approach the cattle and touch them. When she used to ride horses as a girl, she often could sense the mood of the horse just by the contact with her legs and hands. She began to experience the same with the cattle, as she would press her hands on their sides and feel their relaxing response. She noticed that when she was calm, they would react to her in a calmer manner. Slowly, she was getting a sense of their perspective, and how so much of their behavior was guided by perceived threats that we could not necessarily notice.

基于所见所闻，她决定在硕士论文中详细分析这些饲养场的效率，并探讨如何改进。她走访了数十个这样的饲养场，每次都会站在滑槽附近，记录牛在被烙印和接种疫苗时的反应。她还会独自靠近牛群，触摸它们。小时候骑马时，她常常能通过与马腿和手的接触，感受到马的情绪。现在，她也开始在牛群身上体验到同样的感觉，她会用手按压牛的体侧，感受它们放松的反应。她注意到，当她平静下来时，牛群也会以更平静的方式回应她。慢慢地，她开始了解牛群的视角，以及它们的许多行为是如何被我们未必能察觉到的感知到的威胁所引导的。

It soon became obvious to Grandin that in the animal sciences department she was essentially alone in her interest in the emotions and experience of animals. Such subjects were considered beneath scientific interest. She persisted, however, in these lines of investigation—for her own sake and because she felt they had relevance to her thesis. She began to carry a camera with her on her tours of the feedlots. Knowing that cattle are very sensitive to any contrasts in their visual field, she would follow the course of the animals through the various chutes, kneeling and taking black-and-white photographs from their point of view. Her camera would pick up all kinds of sharp contrasts in their field of vision—bright reflections from the sun, sudden shadows, the glare from a window. It was clear to her that seeing these sharp contrasts is what caused the cattle to stop repeatedly in their tracks. Sometimes the sight of a suspended plastic bottle or a dangling chain would cause the same reaction—somehow these things represented dangers to them.

格兰丁很快意识到，在动物科学系，她基本上是唯一一个对动物情感和体验感兴趣的人。这类话题被认为不属于科学研究范畴。然而，她坚持这些研究方向——不仅为了她自己，也因为她觉得这些研究与她的论文息息相关。她开始在巡视饲养场时随身携带相机。她知道牛对视野中的任何反差都非常敏感，所以她会跪下来，从牛的视角跟随牛群穿过各种溜槽，拍摄黑白照片。她的相机会捕捉到牛群视野中各种鲜明的反差——阳光的明亮反射、突如其来的阴影、窗户的眩光。她很清楚，正是这些鲜明的反差让牛群频频停下脚步。有时，悬挂的塑料瓶或悬垂的链条也会引起同样的反应——这些东西对它们来说似乎代表着危险。

The instincts of these animals were obviously not designed for living in an industrial feedlot, and this created a great strain. Whenever the animals would become instinctively frightened by something and react, the fieldworkers would grow irritated and hurry them along, which only exacerbated the cattle’s fear. The number of injuries and deaths was rather appalling, and the time lost when they all piled up into gridlock was incredibly high; and yet, as she knew now, this was all quite easy to fix.

这些牲畜的本能显然不适合在工业饲养场生活，这给他们带来了巨大的压力。每当牲畜本能地被某种东西吓到并做出反应时，田间工人就会恼怒地催促它们前进，这只会加剧牛群的恐惧。伤亡人数令人震惊，而当牛群挤成一团时，时间的浪费更是令人难以置信；然而，正如她现在所知，这一切都很容易解决。

After graduating, she got her first series of jobs working on various design elements for feedlots throughout the Southwest. For meatpacking plants, she devised cattle ramps and restrainer systems that were infinitely more humane than what was there before. Some of this was accomplished through attention to simple details, such as making a ramp curved so the cattle could not see anything to the sides or too far ahead, which kept them calmer. At another site, she redesigned the dip vat so that the incline leading to it sloped gently and had deep grooves in the concrete to help them with their footing. The drop into the water was ever so slight. She also redesigned the area where they dried off, making it a much more placid environment for them.

毕业后，她获得了第一批工作，为西南地区的饲养场设计各种元素。她为肉类加工厂设计了牛坡道和约束系统，这些系统比以前的系统更加人性化。其中一些设计是通过对一些简单细节的关注来实现的，例如将坡道设计成弧形，这样牛就看不到侧面或太远的东西，从而保持它们的平静。在另一个工地，她重新设计了浸水槽，使通往浸水槽的斜坡坡度平缓，并在混凝土上刻有深槽，以帮助牛站立。浸水槽的落差非常小。她还重新设计了牛晾干的区域，为牛创造了一个更加平静的环境。

In the case of the dip vat, the cowboys and fieldworkers would stare at her as if she were from Mars. They secretly mocked her “touchy-feely” approach to farm animals. But when her design was finished, they would watch in amazement as the cattle would blithely approach the dip vat and plop into it with hardly a sound or a complaint. There were no injuries or deaths, and no time lost with pileups or group panic. Such an increase in efficiency would occur in all of her other designs, and this would win her begrudging respect from the skeptical men on the job. Slowly, she was making a name for herself in the field, and considering how far she had come from her earliest days as a severely impaired autistic child, such achievements gave her an incredible feeling of pride.

说到浸槽，牛仔和田间工人会盯着她看，仿佛她来自火星。他们暗自嘲笑她对待农场动物的“感情用事”。但当她的设计完成后，他们会惊奇地看到牛群轻快地靠近浸槽，扑通一声跳进去，几乎一声不吭，甚至没有抱怨。没有造成人员伤亡，也没有因为连环相撞或群体恐慌而浪费时间。这种效率的提升也体现在她所有其他的设计中，这让她赢得了那些持怀疑态度的男工们的勉强尊重。慢慢地，她在田间地头声名鹊起，考虑到她从最初那个患有严重自闭症的孩子到如今取得的进步，这样的成就让她感到无比自豪。

As the years went by, her knowledge of cattle continued to grow, both through research and through frequent contact with them. Soon her work expanded to other farm animals, such as hogs, and later to antelope and elk. She became a sought-after consultant to farms and zoos. She seemed to possess a sixth sense for the inner lives of the animals she dealt with and a remarkable power to calm them down. She herself felt that she had reached a point where she could imagine the thought processes of these various animals. This was based both on her intense scientific investigations and a great deal of thinking inside their minds. She determined, for instance, that animals’ memory and thinking is largely driven by images and other sense traces. Animals are more than capable of learning, but their reasoning process cycles through images. Although we might find it hard to imagine such thinking, before the invention of language we reasoned in a similar way. The distance between humans and animals is not nearly as great as we like to believe, and this connection fascinated her.

随着岁月的流逝，她对牛的了解不断增长，这既源于研究，也源于与牛的频繁接触。很快，她的研究范围扩展到其他农场动物，例如猪，后来又扩展到羚羊和麋鹿。她成为了农场和动物园炙手可热的顾问。她似乎拥有一种第六感，能够洞悉她所接触的动物的内心世界，并拥有一种非凡的能力，能够让它们平静下来。她自己感觉自己已经达到了能够想象这些不同动物思维过程的境界。这既基于她深入的科学研究，也基于对它们大脑的大量思考。例如，她发现动物的记忆和思维主要由图像和其他感官痕迹驱动。动物不仅具有学习能力，它们的推理过程也依赖于图像。尽管我们可能难以想象这样的思维方式，但在语言发明之前，我们也是以这种方式进行推理的。人类与动物之间的距离远没有我们想象的那么远，这种联系让她着迷。

With cattle, she could read their moods by the movement of their ears, the look in their eyes, the tension she could feel through their skin. In studying the brain dynamics of cattle, she had the strange feeling that they resembled people with autism in many ways. A scan of her own brain revealed that she possessed fear centers that were three times larger than normal. She always had to manage higher levels of anxiety than most other people, and she would see continual threats in the environment. Cattle, as prey species, were continually on guard and anxious. Perhaps her own enlarged fear center, she reasoned, was a throwback to the deep past, when humans were prey as well. These reactions are now largely blocked or hidden to us, but because of her autism, her brain had retained this ancient trait. She noticed other similarities between cattle and people with autism, such as the dependence on habit and routine.

对于牛，她可以通过它们耳朵的运动、眼神以及透过皮肤感受到的紧张来解读它们的情绪。在研究牛的大脑动力学时，她有一种奇怪的感觉，它们在很多方面都与自闭症患者相似。对她自己大脑的扫描显示，她的恐惧中心比正常人大三倍。她总是要比大多数人承受更高程度的焦虑，而且她会持续看到环境中的威胁。作为猎物，牛一直保持警惕，焦虑不安。她推断，也许她自己扩大的恐惧中心是对遥远过去的一种回溯，那时人类也是猎物。这些反应现在对我们来说基本上被阻止或隐藏了，但由于她患有自闭症，她的大脑保留了这种古老的特征。她注意到牛和自闭症患者之间的其他相似之处，比如对习惯和常规的依赖。

Thinking in this way led her back to her early interest in the psychology behind autism, and to deepening studies of the neuroscience involved. Her condition as someone who had emerged from autism to a career in science gave her a unique perspective on the subject. As she had done with animals, she could explore it both from the outside (science) and the inside (empathy). She could read about the latest discoveries on autism and relate them to her own experiences. She could illuminate aspects of the condition that no other scientist was able to describe or understand. As she delved deeply into the subject and wrote books on her experiences, she quickly became an extremely popular consultant and lecturer on the subject, as well as a role model for young people with autism.

这种思考方式让她重拾了早期对自闭症背后心理学的兴趣，并深入研究了其中涉及的神经科学。作为一名从自闭症走向科学之路的人，她的经历赋予了她对自闭症这一主题独特的视角。如同她对动物的研究一样，她能够从外部（科学）和内部（共情）两个角度探索自闭症。她可以阅读关于自闭症的最新发现，并将其与自身经历联系起来。她能够阐明其他科学家无法描述或理解的自闭症方面。随着她对自闭症的深入研究，并根据自己的经历撰写书籍，她很快成为了一位备受欢迎的自闭症顾问和讲师，同时也是年轻自闭症患者的榜样。

As she looks back on her life from the present, Temple Grandin has a strange sensation. She emerged from the darkness and chaos of her earliest years of autism, her mind partially guided out of it by her love of animals and her curiosity about their inner lives. Through her experience on her aunt’s ranch with cattle, she became interested in science, which then opened her mind to studying autism itself. Returning to animals for her career, through science and deep observation, she made innovative designs and unique discoveries. These discoveries led her back to autism yet again, a field to which she could now apply her scientific training and thinking. It would appear that some form of destiny kept directing her to the particular fields that she could explore and understand with single-minded purpose, and master in her own ingenious way.

坦普·格兰丁从现在回顾自己的人生，心中涌起一种奇特的感觉。她摆脱了自闭症早期的黑暗与混乱，部分原因是她对动物的热爱以及对动物内心世界的好奇。在姑姑的牧场养牛的经历，让她对科学产生了兴趣，并由此开启了她对自闭症本身的研究。她重回动物研究，通过科学研究和深入观察，做出了创新的设计和独特的发现。这些发现再次引领她回归自闭症，让她得以将自己的科学训练和思维运用到这个领域。似乎某种命运一直在指引她走向那些她能够专心探索、理解并以自己独创的方式精通的领域。

For someone like Temple Grandin, the possibility of achieving mastery in any field would normally seem like an impossible dream. The obstacles in the path of someone with autism are enormous. And yet she managed to find her way to the two subjects that opened up possibilities for advancement. Although it might seem as if luck or blind fate led her there, even as a child she intuited her natural strengths—her love and feel for animals, her visual powers of thinking, her ability to focus on one thing—and leaned on them with all of her energy. Moving with these strengths gave her both the desire and resiliency to put up with all of the doubters, all those who saw her as strange and different and who found the subject matters she chose to study too unconventional. Working in a field where she could use her natural empathy and her particular way of thinking to great effect, she was able to delve deeper and deeper into her chosen subject, arriving at a powerful inside sense of the world of animals. Once she had mastery in this realm, she was able to apply her skills to her other great interest—autism.

对于像坦普·格兰丁这样的人来说，在任何领域取得精通通常都如同遥不可及的梦想。自闭症患者的道路上障碍重重。然而，她最终找到了通往成功之路的两门学科。虽然这似乎是运气或命运的安排，但早在孩提时代，她就直觉地意识到自己与生俱来的优势——对动物的热爱和感知，视觉思维能力，以及专注于一件事的能力——并倾尽全力地运用它们。凭借这些优势，她既有渴望，也有韧性，能够忍受所有质疑，所有视她为奇特和与众不同的人，以及所有认为她所研究学科过于标新立异的人。在一个能够充分发挥她与生俱来的同理心和独特思维方式的领域工作，她得以对所选学科进行越来越深入的探究，最终对动物世界产生了强烈的内在感知。一旦她掌握了这个领域，她就能将自己的技能应用到她感兴趣的另一领域——自闭症。

Understand: achieving mastery in life often depends on those first steps that we take. It is not simply a question of knowing deeply our Life’s Task, but also of having a feel for our own ways of thinking and for perspectives that are unique to us. A deep level of empathy for animals or for certain types of people may not seem like a skill or an intellectual strength, but in truth it is. Empathy plays an enormous role in learning and knowledge. Even scientists, renowned for their objectivity, regularly engage in thinking in which they momentarily identify with their subject. Other qualities we might possess, such as a penchant for visual forms of thinking, represent other possible strengths, not weaknesses. The problem is that we humans are deep conformists. Those qualities that separate us are often ridiculed by others, or criticized by teachers. People with a high visual sense are often labeled as dyslexic, for example. Because of these judgments, we might see our strengths as disabilities and try to work around them in order to fit in. But anything that is peculiar to our makeup is precisely what we must pay the deepest attention to and lean on in our rise to mastery. Mastery is like swimming—it is too difficult to move forward when we are creating our own resistance or swimming against the current. Know your strengths and move with them.

要明白：人生的成功往往取决于我们迈出的第一步。这不仅关乎我们对人生使命的深刻理解，也关乎对我们自身思维方式和独特视角的感受。对动物或某些类型的人拥有深厚的同理心，看似不是一项技能或智力优势，但事实上它的确如此。同理心在学习和知识中扮演着至关重要的角色。即使是以客观性著称的科学家，也会经常进行一些让他们与研究领域产生短暂共鸣的思考。我们可能拥有的其他特质，例如对视觉思维的偏爱，代表着其他可能的优势，而非弱点。问题在于，我们人类是根深蒂固的墨守成规者。这些让我们与众不同的特质常常遭到他人嘲笑或老师批评。例如，视觉感强的人常常被贴上诵读困难的标签。由于这些评判，我们可能会将自己的优势视为缺陷，并试图绕过它们以融入其中。但任何我们特有的特质，恰恰是我们通往精通之路时必须最深入关注和依靠的。精通就像游泳——当我们制造阻力或逆流而上时，前进将异常艰难。了解你的优势，并与之携手前行。

# ↩

3. Transform yourself through practice—The Fingertip Feel

3. 通过练习改变自己——指尖感受

As narrated in chapter 2 ( here ), after graduating from the Citadel in 1981, Cesar Rodriguez decided to enter the pilot training program for the United States Air Force. But soon he had to confront a harsh reality—he was not naturally gifted for flying a jet plane. Among those in the program were some who were known as “golden boys.” They seemed to have a knack for flying at high speeds. They were in their element. From the very beginning Rodriguez loved to fly, and he had ambitions to become a fighter pilot, the most elite and coveted position within the air force. But he would never reach such a goal unless he somehow managed to raise himself up to the skill level of the golden boys. His problem was that he was quickly overwhelmed by the glut of information that a pilot had to process. The key was to learn how to take a scan pattern of all the instruments—a quick reading here and there—while maintaining a feel for one’s overall position in the sky. Losing situational awareness could prove fatal. For him, this scanning ability could only come through endless hours of practice on the simulator and in flying, until it became relatively automatic.

正如第二章（此处）所述，1981年从城堡军校毕业后，塞萨尔·罗德里格斯决定参加美国空军的飞行员训练项目。但很快他就不得不面对一个残酷的现实——他并非天生擅长驾驶喷气式飞机。该项目中有一些被称为“金童”的飞行员。他们似乎拥有高速飞行的天赋，如同身临其境。罗德里格斯从一开始就热爱飞行，并渴望成为一名战斗机飞行员，这是空军中最精英、最令人垂涎的职位。但除非他设法提升自己的技能水平，达到“金童”飞行员的水平，否则他永远无法实现这一目标。他的问题在于，飞行员需要处理的海量信息很快就会让他应接不暇。关键在于学会如何扫描所有仪表——快速读取一些数值——同时保持对自身在天空中整体位置的感知。失去态势感知能力可能会致命。对他来说，这种扫描能力只有通过在模拟器和飞行中不断练习才能获得，直到它变得相对自动化。

Rodriguez had played sports in high school and he knew the value of practice and repetition, but this was a lot more complex than any sport or any skill he had ever tried to master. As soon as he became comfortable with the instruments, he would be faced with the daunting task of learning to execute various flying maneuvers (like rolls), and to develop a feel for the exact speeds needed to enter them. All of this required extremely rapid mental calculations. The golden boys would ace these maneuvers in no time. For Rodriguez, it would require a lot of repetition and intense focus every time he entered the cockpit. He noticed sometimes that his body would get there ahead of his mind; his nerves and his fingers would intuit a sense of what command of the maneuver should feel like; he would then consciously aim to recreate that feeling.

罗德里格斯高中时参加过体育运动，他深知练习和重复的重要性，但这比他尝试掌握的任何运动或技能都要复杂得多。一旦他熟悉了仪表，他就会面临一项艰巨的任务：学习执行各种飞行动作（例如滚转），并培养对进入这些动作所需精确速度的感觉。所有这些都需要极其快速的心算。这些“金童”们很快就能掌握这些动作。对罗德里格斯来说，每次进入驾驶舱都需要大量的重复练习和高度集中注意力。他有时会注意到，他的身体会先于思维到达目的地；他的神经和手指会本能地感知到操控这些动作的感觉；然后他会有意识地去重现那种感觉。

Once this mark was passed, he would have to learn how to fly in formation, working with other pilots in an intricately coordinated team. Flying in formation meant juggling several skills at the same time, and the complexity of it all could be mind-boggling. Part of him was motivated by the great excitement he felt commanding such a jet and working with the team, and part of him was also motivated by the challenge. He had noticed that in gaining control of the jet and the various maneuvers, he had developed acute powers of concentration. He could tune everything out and immerse himself completely in the moment. This made every new skill set a little easier to master.

一旦通过这项测试，他就必须学习如何进行编队飞行，与其他飞行员组成一个协调复杂的团队。编队飞行意味着要同时掌握多种技能，其复杂性令人难以置信。驾驶这样的飞机并与团队协作，他感到无比兴奋，而挑战也激励着他。他注意到，在控制飞机和进行各种机动的过程中，他的注意力得到了极大的集中。他可以抛开一切，完全沉浸在当下。这使得每一项新技能都更容易掌握。

Slowly, through sheer tenacity and practice, he rose to the top of his class, and was considered among the few who could serve as fighter pilots. But there remained one last hurdle in his ascent to the top: flying in the high-scale exercises run by all branches of the military. In this case it was a matter of understanding the overall mission and operating in an intricately orchestrated land-air-sea campaign. It required an even higher level of awareness, and at moments during these exercises Rodriguez had an odd sensation—he was no longer focusing on the various physical elements of flying or on the individual skill components, but was thinking and feeling the overall campaign and how he fit into it in a seamless fashion. It was a sensation of mastery, and it was fleeting. He also noticed a slight gap between himself and the golden boys. They had relied for so long on their natural skills that they had not cultivated the same level of concentration that he now possessed. In many ways, he had surpassed them. After participating in a few of these exercises, Rodriguez had risen to elite status.

凭借着顽强的毅力和不懈的练习，他慢慢地跻身同级别顶尖飞行员之列，并被认为是少数能够胜任战斗机飞行员的人才。但他晋升的道路上还存在最后一个障碍：参加各军种组织的大规模演习。在这种情况下，关键在于理解整体任务，并在错综复杂的陆海空三军战役中行动。这需要更高水平的意识，而罗德里格斯在演习中有时会有一种奇怪的感觉——他不再专注于飞行的各种体能要素或单个技能要素，而是在思考和感受整个战役，以及自己如何天衣无缝地融入其中。这是一种精通的感觉，转瞬即逝。他也注意到自己与那些“金童”之间略有差距。他们长期以来依赖天赋技能，以至于没有培养出他如今拥有的这种专注力。在很多方面，他都超越了他们。在参加了几次这样的演习之后，罗德里格斯就晋升为精英。

On January 19, 1991, in the space of a few minutes, all of his elaborate training and practice would be put to the ultimate test. A few days before, the United States and allied forces had launched Operation Desert Storm in response to Sadaam Hussein’s invasion of Kuwait. The morning of the 19th Rodriguez and his wingman, Craig “Mole” Underhill, flew into Iraq as part of a thirty-six-aircraft strike force, heading toward a target near Baghdad. It was his first real taste of combat. Flying F-15s, he and Mole quickly spotted a pair of Iraqi MiG fighters in the distance and decided to give chase. Within seconds they realized that they had been lured into a trap, the pursuer turning into the pursued, as two MiGs now bore down on them from an unexpected direction.

1991年1月19日，短短几分钟内，他所有精心训练和练习都将面临终极考验。几天前，美国及其盟军发动了“沙漠风暴”行动，以回应萨达姆·侯赛因入侵科威特的行动。19日上午，罗德里格斯和他的僚机克雷格·“鼹鼠”·安德希尔作为由36架飞机组成的打击部队的一部分飞往伊拉克，前往巴格达附近的一个目标。这是他第一次真正体验战斗。他和鼹鼠驾驶着F-15战斗机，很快在远处发现了两架伊拉克米格战斗机，于是决定进行追击。几秒钟后，他们意识到自己被引诱到了一个陷阱里，追击者变成了被追击者，因为两架米格战斗机正从意想不到的方向向他们逼近。

Realizing how quickly one of the enemy planes was approaching, Rodriguez suddenly jettisoned his fuel tanks for greater speed and maneuverability. He then dove toward the ground, below the level of the approaching MiG, doing everything he could to make it difficult for the enemy to get a read on him with his radar, including flying at a right angle to the ground to make his plane as skinny as possible. Without a radar reading, the MiG could not launch a missile. Everything was happening so fast. At any moment his own radar could light up, indicating the enemy had locked into him and he was as good as dead. He had one chance to make it: evading the MiG until it got too close to fire, and drawing it into a dogfight—a circular battle in the air that was a rare occurrence in modern warfare. At the back of his mind he was also trying to buy enough time for his wingman to help him out, and he could somehow sense Mole’s presence following him from a distance. But time would bring another danger—the presence of the second MiG on the scene.

意识到一架敌机逼近的速度之快，罗德里格斯突然抛弃了副油箱，以提高速度和机动性。然后，他俯冲至地面，低于正在接近的米格机的高度，竭尽所能地让敌方雷达难以识别他，包括垂直于地面飞行，使飞机尽可能地瘦小。没有雷达读数，米格机无法发射导弹。一切都发生得太快了。他自己的雷达随时可能亮起，表明敌机已经锁定了他，他等于死了。他只有一次机会：躲避米格机，直到它靠近到可以开火的程度，并将其引入空中缠斗——这种空中的环形战在现代战争中并不常见。在他的内心深处，他也在努力争取足够的时间让僚机来支援他，而且他能感觉到远处跟踪他的莫尔。但时间会带来另一个危险——第二架米格机的出现。

He tried every evasive maneuver in the book. He saw the MiG getting closer and closer when suddenly he heard from Mole, who had been following him and had now maneuvered into position. As Rodriguez looked over his shoulder, he could see the enemy MiG exploding—Mole’s missile had struck it. As the chase had unfolded, everything had gone as Rodriguez wanted, but there was not a second to relax. The second MiG was now rapidly approaching.

他试遍了所有规避技巧。眼看米格机越来越近，突然听到了一直在跟踪他的摩尔的动静，他已经机动到位。罗德里格斯回头一看，发现敌方米格机爆炸了——摩尔的导弹击中了它。追逐逐渐展开，一切进展顺利，正如罗德里格斯所料，但他一刻也不能放松。第二架米格机正快速逼近。

Mole ascended to 20,000 feet. As the MiG bore down on Rodriguez’s plane, its pilot realized Mole’s presence above him, and began to maneuver up and down to somehow escape being trapped between the two of them. Using this instant of confusion, Rodriguez was able to get inside the MiG’s turning circle. It had now turned into a classic two-circle dogfight in which each plane tried to circle onto the tail of the other and into firing range, moving closer to the ground with each succeeding loop. They circled and circled around each other. Finally, at 3,600 feet, Rodriguez got a reading and locked his missiles on the MiG. The Iraqi pilot went into a hard evasive maneuver, turning directly toward the ground, flipping upside down and trying to circle into a reverse direction to escape, but in the few seconds of the dogfight the pilot had lost awareness of how close they had drifted to the ground, and he crashed into the desert below.

摩尔上升到20000英尺的高度。当米格机向罗德里格斯的飞机逼近时，飞行员意识到摩尔就在上方，于是开始上下移动，试图摆脱被夹在中间的局面。罗德里格斯趁着这瞬间的混乱，成功进入了米格机的转弯圈内。现在，局面变成了一场经典的双环缠斗，两架飞机都试图绕到对方的尾部进入射程，每转一圈就离地面更近一些。它们不停地绕着对方转。最终，在3600英尺的高度，罗德里格斯获得了目标信息，并将导弹锁定在米格机上。伊拉克飞行员采取了强硬的规避动作，直接转向地面，翻个身，试图反方向盘旋逃脱，但在几秒钟的缠斗中，飞行员已经忘记了他们已经飞到离地面有多近，最终坠毁在下方的沙漠中。

Mole and Rodriguez returned to the base to debrief their superiors on the mission, but as Rodriguez went over it all and watched video of the encounters, he had a strange sensation. He could not really recall any moment of it. It had happened so fast. The entire encounter with the MiGs had only lasted three to four minutes, and the final dogfight a matter of seconds. He must have been thinking in some way—he had executed some nearly perfect maneuvers. For instance, he had no recollection of deciding to jettison the fuel tanks nor where such an idea came from. It must have been something he had learned, and somehow in the moment it had simply occurred to him, and very easily might have saved his life. The evasive maneuvers he executed with the first MiG astounded his superiors—they were so fast and effective. His awareness during the dogfight must have been exceptionally keen; he had circled to his opponent’s tail in ever-faster cycles, never losing sight of the desert floor they were approaching. How could he explain all of these maneuvers? He could hardly remember them. All he knew was that in the moment he hadn’t been experiencing fear, but rather an intense adrenalin rush that made his body and mind operate in total harmony, with a kind of thinking that moved in milliseconds and was too fast for him to analyze.

摩尔和罗德里格斯返回基地向上级汇报任务情况。但当罗德里格斯回顾整个过程并观看遭遇战录像时，他有一种奇怪的感觉。他完全记不起任何细节。一切都发生得太快了。与米格战机的整个遭遇战只持续了三四分钟，最后的缠斗也不过几秒钟。他肯定在思考——他执行了一些近乎完美的动作。比如，他不记得自己决定抛弃油箱，也不知道这个想法是从哪里冒出来的。这肯定是他学到的，只是在那一刻突然想到的，而这很可能救了他的命。他面对第一架米格战机时执行的规避动作令他的上级感到震惊——这些动作如此迅速有效。他在缠斗中的意识一定异常敏锐；他以越来越快的速度绕向对手的尾部，始终没有失去他们正在接近的沙漠地面。他该如何解释所有这些动作？他几乎记不清了。他只知道，那一刻他感受到的并非恐惧，而是一阵强烈的肾上腺素激增，让他的身心完全协调运作，他的思维以毫秒为单位进行，快得他无法分析。

For three days after the encounter he could not sleep, the adrenalin still coursing through his veins. It made him realize that the body possesses latent physiological powers—unleashed in such dramatic moments—that elevate the mind to an even higher level of focus. Rodriguez would go on to have one more kill in Desert Storm, and another in the 1999 Kosovo campaign, more than any pilot in recent combat, earning him the nickname the Last American Ace.

那次遭遇战后，他整整三天都无法入睡，肾上腺素依然在他的血管里奔腾。这让他意识到，身体蕴藏着潜在的生理力量——在如此激动人心的时刻被释放——能够将人的注意力提升到更高的高度。罗德里格斯后来在“沙漠风暴”行动中又斩获一枚炸弹，在1999年的科索沃战役中又斩获一枚，比近来战斗中的任何飞行员都多，因此获得了“美国最后的王牌”的绰号。

In our daily, conscious activity we generally experience a separation between the mind and the body. We think about our bodies and our physical actions. Animals do not experience this division. When we start to learn any skill that has a physical component, this separation becomes even more apparent. We have to think about the various actions involved, the steps we have to follow. We are aware of our slowness and of how our bodies respond in an awkward way. At certain points, as we improve, we have glimpses of how this process could function differently, of how it might feel to practice the skill fluidly, with the mind not getting in the way of the body. With such glimpses, we know what to aim for. If we take our practice far enough the skill becomes automatic, and we have the sensation that the mind and the body are operating as one.

在我们日常的意识活动中，我们通常会感受到身心分离。我们会思考自己的身体和身体动作。动物则不会感受到这种分离。当我们开始学习任何涉及身体动作的技能时，这种分离会变得更加明显。我们必须思考其中涉及的各种动作，以及我们必须遵循的步骤。我们意识到自己的迟缓，以及身体反应的笨拙。随着我们不断进步，在某些时候，我们会瞥见这个过程可以如何以不同的方式运作，以及流畅地练习技能，让思维不妨碍身体，会是什么感觉。有了这样的瞥见，我们就知道该瞄准什么。如果我们练习得足够深入，技能就会变得自动化，我们会感觉到身心合一。

If we are learning a complex skill, such as flying a jet in combat, we must master a series of simple skills, one on top of the other. Each time one skill becomes automatic, the mind is freed up to focus on the higher one. At the very end of this process, when there are no more simple skills to learn, the brain has assimilated an incredible amount of information, all of which has become internalized, part of our nervous system. The whole complex skill is now inside us and at our fingertips. We are thinking, but in a different way—with the body and mind completely fused. We are transformed. We possess a form of intelligence that allows us to approximate the instinctual power of animals, but only through a conscious, deliberate, and extended practice.

如果我们学习一项复杂技能，比如驾驶喷气式飞机作战，就必须掌握一系列简单的技能，一个接一个。每当一项技能变得自动化，思维就能解放出来，专注于更高级的技能。在这个过程的最后，当没有其他简单技能需要学习时，大脑已经吸收了海量的信息，所有这些信息都已内化，成为我们神经系统的一部分。如今，这整项复杂技能都已融入我们的体内，触手可及。我们能够思考，但方式不同——身心完全融合。我们蜕变了。我们拥有了一种智慧，它使我们能够接近动物的本能力量，但这只能通过有意识、有计划、持续的练习来实现。

In our culture we tend to denigrate practice. We want to imagine that great feats occur naturally—that they are a sign of someone’s genius or superior talent. Getting to a high level of achievement through practice seems so banal, so uninspiring. Besides, we don’t want to have to think of the 10,000 to 20,000 hours that go into such mastery. These values of ours are oddly counterproductive—they cloak from us the fact that almost anyone can reach such heights through tenacious effort, something that should encourage us all. It is time to reverse this prejudice against conscious effort and to see the powers we gain through practice and discipline as eminently inspiring and even miraculous. The ability to master complicated skills by building connections in the brain is the product of millions of years of evolution, and the source of all of our material and cultural powers. When we sense the possible unity of mind and body in the early stages of practice, we are being guided toward this power. It is the natural bent of our brain to want to move in this direction, to elevate its powers through repetition. To lose our connection to this natural inclination is the height of madness, and will lead to a world in which no one has the patience to master complex skills. As individuals we must resist such a trend, and venerate the transformative powers we gain through practice.

在我们的文化中，我们倾向于贬低练习。我们总想把伟大的壮举想象成自然而然的——它们是某人天才或卓越才能的标志。通过练习获得高水平的成就似乎太平庸，太缺乏启发性了。此外，我们也不想去想为了达到这样的成就需要投入一两万个小时。奇怪的是，我们的这些价值观适得其反——它们掩盖了这样一个事实：几乎任何人都可以通过坚持不懈的努力达到这样的高度，而这本应激励我们所有人。现在是时候扭转这种对有意识努力的偏见，并将我们通过练习和自律获得的力量视为极其鼓舞人心，甚至神奇的力量了。通过在大脑中建立连接来掌握复杂技能的能力是数百万年进化的产物，也是我们所有物质和文化力量的源泉。当我们在练习的早期阶段感受到身心合一的可能性时，我们就被引导着走向这种力量。我们的大脑天生倾向于朝这个方向发展，希望通过重复来提升其能力。失去与这种自然倾向的联系是极其疯狂的，会导致一个无人有耐心掌握复杂技能的世界。作为个体，我们必须抵制这种趋势，并尊重我们通过实践获得的变革力量。

# ↩

4. Internalize the details—The Life Force

4. 内化细节——生命力

As the illegitimate son of the notary Ser Piero da Vinci, Leonardo da Vinci (see here , for more on the artist) was essentially barred from studying and practicing the traditional professional careers—medicine, law, and so on—and from higher education. And so as a boy growing up in the town of Vinci, near Florence, he received little formal education. He spent much of his time roaming around the countryside and venturing into the forests outside his town. He was enchanted by the incredible variety of life he found there, and the dramatic rock formations and waterfalls that were part of the landscape. As his father was a notary, there was a fair amount of paper (a rare commodity at the time) in the family house, and feeling a great desire to draw all that he saw on his walks, he began stealing sheets of paper and carrying them with him.

作为公证人塞尔·皮耶罗·达·芬奇的私生子，列奥纳多·达·芬奇（有关这位艺术家的更多信息，请参见此处）基本上被禁止学习和从事传统的职业生涯——医学、法律等等——并且被禁止接受高等教育。因此，作为一个在佛罗伦萨附近的芬奇镇长大的男孩，他几乎没有接受过正规教育。他大部分时间都在乡间漫游，并冒险进入城外的森林。他被那里发现的令人难以置信的生命多样性以及构成景观的一部分的壮观的岩层和瀑布所迷住。由于他的父亲是一名公证人，家里有很多纸（在当时是一种稀有商品），他非常想画下他在散步时看到的一切，于是他开始偷纸随身携带。

He would sit on a rock and draw the insects, birds and flowers that fascinated him. He never received any instruction. He simply drew what he saw, and he began to notice that in trying to capture these things on paper, he had to think deeply. He had to focus on the details that the eye would often pass over. In drawing plants, for instance, he began to notice the subtle distinctions in the stamens of various flowers and how they were different from one another. He would notice the transformations these plants went through on their way to blossoming, and he would capture these changes in sequential drawings. In going so deeply into their details, he had fleeting intimations of what animated these plants from within, what made them distinct and alive. Soon, thinking and drawing became fused in his mind. Through drawing things in the world around him, he came to understand them.

他会坐在一块岩石上，画下令他着迷的昆虫、鸟类和花朵。他从未接受过任何指导。他只是画下他所看到的。他开始注意到，在试图将这些事物捕捉到纸上时，他必须深入思考。他必须专注于眼睛经常忽略的细节。例如，在画植物时，他开始注意到各种花朵雄蕊的细微差别，以及它们彼此之间的差异。他会注意到这些植物在开花过程中经历的变化，并用连续的画作捕捉这些变化。通过如此深入地探究细节，他能够瞬间感受到是什么赋予了这些植物内在的活力，是什么让它们如此独特而鲜活。很快，思考和绘画在他的脑海中融合在一起。通过描绘周围世界的事物，他开始理解它们。

His progress at drawing was so astounding that his father thought of finding him a position as an apprentice in one of the various studios in Florence. Working in the arts was one of the few professions open to illegitimate sons. In 1466, using his influence as a respected notary in Florence, he managed to secure a position for his fourteen-year-old son in the workshop of the great artist Verrocchio. For Leonardo, this was a perfect fit. Verrocchio was deeply influenced by the enlightened spirit of the times, and his apprentices were taught to approach their work with the seriousness of scientists. For instance, plaster casts of human figures would be placed about the studio with various pieces of fabric draped over them. The apprentices had to learn to concentrate deeply, and recognize the different creases and shadows that would form. They had to learn how to reproduce them realistically. Leonardo loved learning in this way, and soon it became apparent to Verrocchio that his young apprentice had developed an exceptional eye for detail.

他的绘画进步令人惊叹，他的父亲甚至考虑在佛罗伦萨的众多画室里为他找个学徒职位。艺术工作是少数几个允许私生子从事的职业之一。1466年，他利用自己在佛罗伦萨受人尊敬的公证人的影响力，成功地为14岁的儿子在伟大的艺术家韦罗基奥的工作室里谋得了一个职位。对达芬奇来说，这简直是天作之合。韦罗基奥深受当时启蒙精神的影响，他教导学徒们要像科学家一样严肃地对待工作。例如，工作室里摆放着人体石膏模型，上面盖着各种布料。学徒们必须学会高度集中注意力，辨别出模型上形成的各种褶皱和阴影。他们必须学会如何逼真地再现这些痕迹。达芬奇喜欢以这种方式学习，韦罗基奥很快就发现，他的年轻学徒已经培养出了对细节的敏锐洞察力。

By 1472 Leonardo was one of Verrocchio’s top assistants, helping him on his large-scale paintings and taking on a fair amount of responsibility. In Verrocchio’s The Baptism of Christ, Leonardo was given the task of painting one of the two angels off to the side, and this work is now the oldest example we have of his painting. When Verrocchio saw the results of Leonardo’s work he was astounded. The face of the angel had a quality he had never seen before—it seemed to literally glow from within. The look on the angel’s face seemed uncannily real and expressive.

1472年，达芬奇已成为韦罗基奥的得力助手之一，协助他完成巨幅画作，并承担了相当多的责任。在韦罗基奥的《基督受洗》中，达芬奇负责绘制画中两位天使中的一位，这幅作品是我们现存最古老的达芬奇作品。韦罗基奥看到达芬奇的作品时，大为震惊。天使的面容散发着一种他从未见过的光芒——仿佛从内而外散发着光芒。天使脸上的表情显得异常真实，富有表现力。

Although it might have seemed like magic to Verrocchio, recent X-rays have revealed some of the secrets to Leonardo’s early technique. The layers of paint he applied were exceptionally thin, his brush strokes invisible. He had gradually added more layers, each ever so slightly darker than the last. Operating in this way, and experimenting with different pigments, he had taught himself how to capture the delicate contours of human flesh. Because of the thin layers, any light hitting the painting seemed to pass through the angel’s face and illuminate it from within.

尽管在韦罗基奥看来，这或许如同魔术，但最近的X光片揭示了达芬奇早期技法的一些秘密。他涂抹的颜料层异常薄，笔触隐约可见。他逐渐增加颜料层，每一层都比上一层略深。通过这种方式，并尝试不同的颜料，他自学了如何捕捉人体肌肤的细腻轮廓。由于颜料层很薄，任何照射到画上的光线都仿佛穿过天使的脸庞，从内部照亮了它。

What this revealed was that in the six years that he had been working in the studio, he must have applied himself to an elaborate study of the various paints and perfected a style of layering that made everything seem delicate and lifelike, with a feeling of texture and depth. He must have also spent a great deal of time studying the composition of human flesh itself. What this also revealed was the incredible patience of Leonardo, who must have felt a great deal of love for such detailed work.

这揭示了达芬奇在工作室工作的六年里，一定潜心钻研各种颜料，并精进了一种层次丰富的绘画技巧，使一切显得细腻逼真，富有质感和深度。他还一定花费了大量时间研究人体的构成。这也展现了达芬奇惊人的耐心，他一定对如此细致入微的作品怀有极大的热爱。

Over the years, after he left Verrocchio’s studio and established a name for himself as an artist, Leonardo da Vinci developed a philosophy that would guide his artwork and, later, his scientific work as well. He noticed that other artists generally started with an overall image they planned to depict, one that would create a startling or spiritual effect. His mind operated differently. He would find himself beginning with a keen focus on details—the various shapes of noses, the possible turnings of the mouth to indicate a mood, the veins in a hand, the intricate knots of trees. These details fascinated him. He had come to believe that by focusing on and understanding such details he was actually getting closer to the secret of life itself, to the work of the Creator who infused his presence into every living thing and every form of matter. The bones of the hand or the contours of human lips were as inspiring to him as any religious image. For him, painting was a quest to get at the life force that animates all things. In the process of doing so, he believed he could create work that was much more emotional and visceral. And to realize this quest, he invented a series of exercises that he followed with incredible rigor.

多年来，在离开韦罗基奥工作室并确立了自己的艺术声誉后，列奥纳多·达·芬奇逐渐形成了一套哲学理念，这套理念不仅指导了他的艺术创作，也指导了他的科学研究。他注意到，其他艺术家通常从他们计划描绘的整体形象开始，从而创造出一种令人震惊或充满灵性的效果。他的思维方式却截然不同。他发现自己会从敏锐的细节入手——各种鼻子的形状，嘴角可能表达情绪的旋转，手上的血管，以及树木错综复杂的节理。这些细节让他着迷。他开始相信，通过关注和理解这些细节，他实际上正在接近生命本身的秘密，接近造物主的杰作，造物主将他的存在融入每一个生物和每一种物质之中。手的骨骼或人类嘴唇的轮廓对他来说，与任何宗教图像一样鼓舞人心。对他来说，绘画是一种探寻赋予万物生命力的生命力的探索。在此过程中，他相信自己能够创作出更具情感、更发自内心的作品。为了实现这一目标，他发明了一系列练习，并极其严格地遵循着。

During the day he would take endless walks through the city and countryside, his eyes taking in all of the details of the visible world. He would make himself notice something new in every familiar object that he saw. At night, before falling asleep, he would review all of these various objects and details, fixing them in his memory. He was obsessed with capturing the essence of the human face in all of its glorious diversity. For this purpose, he would visit every conceivable place where he could find different types of people—brothels, public houses, prisons, hospitals, prayer corners in churches, country festivals. With his notebook always at hand, he would sketch grimacing, laughing, pained, beatific, leering expressions on an incredible variety of faces. He would follow people in the streets who had a type of face he had never seen before, or some kind of physical deformity, and would sketch them as he walked. He would fill single sheets of paper with dozens of different noses in profile. He seemed particularly interested in lips, finding them just as expressive as eyes. He would repeat all of these exercises at different times of the day, to make sure he could capture the different effects that changing light would have on the human face.

白天，他会在城市和乡村中漫步，用眼睛捕捉着可见世界的所有细节。他会强迫自己在每一个熟悉的事物中发现新的特征。晚上，入睡前，他会回顾所有这些不同的事物和细节，并将它们牢牢地铭刻在记忆中。他痴迷于捕捉人脸的精髓，感受其绚丽多彩的多样性。为此，他会走遍所有能找到不同类型人的地方——妓院、酒吧、监狱、医院、教堂的祈祷角、乡村节日。他总是带着笔记本，在形形色色的面孔上勾勒出各种表情：愁眉苦脸、大笑、痛苦、幸福、斜视。他会在街上跟踪那些长着他从未见过的脸型或身体有某种畸形的人，边走边画。他会在一张纸上画下几十个不同的鼻子侧面像。他似乎对嘴唇特别感兴趣，觉得它们和眼睛一样富有表现力。他会在一天中的不同时间重复所有这些练习，以确保能够捕捉到光线变化对人脸产生的不同效果。

For his great painting The Last Supper , his patron, the duke of Milan, grew increasingly angry with Leonardo for the time he was taking to finish it. It seemed that all that remained was to fill in the face of Judas, but Leonardo could not find an adequate model. He had taken to visiting the worst parts of Milan to find the most perfectly villainous expression to translate onto Judas, but was having no luck. The duke accepted his explanation, and soon enough Leonardo had found the model he wanted.

达芬奇的巨作《最后的晚餐》的赞助人米兰公爵，对达芬奇耗时过长愈发恼火。看来只剩下填充犹大的脸了，但达芬奇却找不到合适的模特。他走遍了米兰最肮脏的街区，想找到最能完美诠释犹大的邪恶表情，却始终无功而返。公爵接受了他的解释，很快达芬奇就找到了他想要的模特。

He applied this same rigor to capturing bodies in motion. Part of his philosophy was that life is defined by continual movement and constant change. The artist must be able to render the sensation of dynamic movement in a still image. Ever since he was a young man he had been obsessed with currents of water, and had become quite proficient at capturing the look of waterfalls, cascades, and rushing water. With people, he would spend hours seated on the side of a street, watching pedestrians as they moved by. He would hurriedly sketch the outlines of their figures, capturing their various movements in a stop-action sequence. (He had reached the point where he could sketch with incredible rapidity.) At home, he would fill in the outlines. To develop his eye for following movement in general, he invented a whole series of different exercises. For instance, one day in his notebook he wrote, “Tomorrow make some silhouettes out of cardboard in various forms and throw them from the top of the terrace through the air; then draw the movements each makes at different stages of descent.”

他将同样的严谨性应用于捕捉运动中的物体。他的哲学理念之一是，生命由持续的运动和不断的变化所定义。艺术家必须能够在静止的画面中呈现动态的流动感。自年轻时起，他就痴迷于水流，并精于捕捉瀑布、小瀑布和湍急水流的景象。为了与人相处，他会一坐就是几个小时，坐在路边，观察来往的行人。他会匆匆勾勒出他们的身影轮廓，以定格动作的序列捕捉他们的各种动作。（他已经达到了能够以惊人的速度进行素描的境界。）回到家，他会填充轮廓。为了培养自己对运动的观察力，他发明了一系列不同的练习。例如，有一天，他在笔记本上写道：“明天用各种形状的纸板做几个剪影，把它们从露台顶部抛向空中；然后画出每个剪影在不同下降阶段的动作。”

His hunger to get at the core of life by exploring its details drove him into elaborate research on human and animal anatomy. He wanted to be able to draw a human or a cat from the inside out. He personally dissected cadavers, sawing through bones and skulls, and he religiously attended autopsies so that he could see as closely as possible the structure of muscles and nerves. His anatomical drawings were far in advance of anything of his time for their realism and accuracy.

他渴望通过探索细节来触及生命的核心，这驱使他对人体和动物的解剖学进行了深入的研究。他渴望能够从内到外地描绘一个人或一只猫。他亲自解剖尸体，锯开骨头和头骨，并虔诚地参加尸检，以便尽可能仔细地观察肌肉和神经的结构。他的解剖图以其逼真性和准确性远远领先于他那个时代的任何东西。

To other artists, Leonardo seemed insane for all of this attention to detail, but in the few paintings that he actually completed, the results of such rigorous practice can be seen and felt. More than the work of any other artist of his time, the landscapes in the backgrounds of his paintings seemed infused with life. Every flower, branch, leaf or stone was rendered in intense detail. But these backgrounds were not simply there to decorate. In an effect known as sfumato, and one that was peculiar to his work, he would soften parts of these backgrounds to the point at which they would melt into the figure in the foreground, giving a dreamlike effect. It was part of his idea that all of life is deeply interconnected and fused on some level.

在其他艺术家眼中，达芬奇对细节的如此关注似乎有些疯狂，但在他真正完成的几幅画作中，我们可以看到并感受到这种严谨练习的成果。与同时代其他艺术家的作品相比，他画作背景中的风景似乎更加充满生机。每一朵花、每一根树枝、每一片叶子或每一块石头都刻画得极其细致。但这些背景并非仅仅为了装饰。他运用一种名为“晕涂法”（sfumato）的特有效果，将背景的部分柔化，直至与前景中的人物融为一体，营造出一种如梦似幻的效果。这体现了他认为所有生命都在某种程度上紧密相连、相互融合的理念。

The faces of the women he painted had a pronounced effect on people, and particularly on men, who often fell in love with the female figures he depicted in religious scenes. It wasn’t any obvious sensual quality in their expression, but in their ambiguous smiles and their beautifully rendered flesh the men would recognize a powerfully seductive quality. Leonard heard many stories of them finding their way to his paintings in various houses and secretly fondling the women in the images and kissing their lips.

他笔下的女性面孔对人们有着显著的影响，尤其是对男性，他们常常爱上他描绘的宗教场景中的女性形象。她们的表情中没有明显的性感，但她们暧昧的微笑和精致的肌肤，让男人们感受到一种强烈的诱惑力。伦纳德听到过很多这样的故事：男人们来到他位于不同房屋的画作前，偷偷地抚摸画中的女人，亲吻她们的嘴唇。

Much of Leonardo’s Mona Lisa has been damaged by attempts to clean and restore it in the past, making it hard to imagine it as it originally appeared, and how its startling qualities shocked the public. Fortunately, we have the critic Vasari’s description of it, before it became hopelessly altered: “The eyebrows, growing thickly in one place and thinly in another, following the pores of the skin, could not have been more lifelike. The nose, with its ravishingly delicate pink nostrils, was life itself. The shaping of the mouth, where the red of the lips merged with the skin tones of the face, seemed not to be made from colors but from living flesh. In the hollow of the throat, the observant onlooker could see the pulsing of the veins.”

达芬奇的《蒙娜丽莎》在过去的清洗和修复过程中，大部分都遭到了损坏，很难想象它最初的面貌，以及它如何震撼公众的惊人特质。幸运的是，在它被彻底改变之前，我们有评论家瓦萨里对它的描述：“眉毛，一处浓，一处稀，顺着皮肤的毛孔生长，栩栩如生。鼻子，有着令人心醉神迷的精致粉红色鼻孔，栩栩如生。嘴巴的形状，嘴唇的红色与脸部肤色融为一体，似乎并非由颜色构成，而是用鲜活的血肉构成。在喉咙的凹陷处，细心的旁观者可以看到血管的搏动。”

Long after Leonardo’s death, his paintings continue to have haunting and disturbing effects on viewers. Numerous security guards in museums around the world have been fired for their weird, obsessive relationships to his work, and Leonardo’s paintings remain the most vandalized in the history of art, all of this attesting to the power of his work to stir up the most visceral emotions.

达芬奇去世多年后，他的画作依然萦绕在观者心头，令人不安。世界各地博物馆的许多保安都因对其作品怪异而痴迷的感情而被解雇，达芬奇的画作至今仍是艺术史上遭受破坏最严重的作品。这一切都证明了他的作品拥有触动人心弦的力量。

The primary problem for artists in Leonardo da Vinci’s day was the constant pressure to produce more and more work. They had to produce at a relatively high rate in order to keep the commissions coming and remain in the public eye. This influenced the quality of their work. A style had developed in which artists could quickly create effects in their painting that would superficially excite viewers. To create such effects they would depend on bright colors, unusual juxtapositions and compositions, and dramatic scenes. In the process, they would inevitably gloss over the details in the background and even in the people they portrayed. They did not pay much attention to the flowers or trees or the hands of figures in the foreground. They had to dazzle on the surface. Leonardo recognized this fact early in his career and it distressed him. It went against his grain in two ways—he hated the feeling of having to hurry with anything, and he loved immersing himself in details for their own sake. He was not interested in creating surface effects. He was animated by a hunger to understand life forms from the inside out and to grasp the force that makes them dynamic, and to somehow express all of this on a flat surface. And so, not fitting in, he went on his own peculiar path, mixing science and art.

列奥纳多·达·芬奇时代艺术家面临的主要问题是不断创作更多作品的压力。为了保证订单的顺利完成并保持在公众视野中，他们必须保持较高的创作速度。这影响了他们作品的质量。一种风格逐渐形成，艺术家们能够快速地在绘画中创造出足以在表面上激起观者兴趣的效果。为了创造这种效果，他们会依赖鲜艳的色彩、独特的并置和构图，以及戏剧性的场景。在这个过程中，他们不可避免地会忽略背景甚至人物的细节。他们不太关注前景中的花草树木或人物的手。他们必须追求表面的炫目效果。列奥纳多在职业生涯早期就意识到了这一点，并为此感到苦恼。这在两个方面违背了他的创作风格——他讨厌匆忙赶工的感觉，他喜欢沉浸在细节之中，只为细节本身。他对创造表面效果不感兴趣。他渴望从内而外地理解生命形态，掌握赋予生命活力的力量，并试图将这一切在平面上展现出来。因此，他不适应这种模式，走上了一条独特的道路，将科学与艺术融为一体。

To complete his quest, Leonardo had to become what he termed “universal”—for each object he had to be able to render all of its details, and he had to extend this knowledge as far as possible, to as many objects in the world as he could study. Through sheer accumulation of such details, the essence of life itself became visible to him, and his understanding of this life force became visible in his artwork.

为了完成他的探索，达芬奇必须达到他所谓的“万能”——他必须能够呈现每一件物品的所有细节，并且必须尽可能地拓展这种知识，去研究世界上尽可能多的物品。正是通过积累这些细节，他才得以领悟生命的本质，并将他对这种生命力的理解展现在他的作品中。

In your own work you must follow the Leonardo path. Most people don’t have the patience to absorb their minds in the fine points and minutiae that are intrinsically part of their work. They are in a hurry to create effects and make a splash; they think in large brush strokes. Their work inevitably reveals their lack of attention to detail—it doesn’t connect deeply with the public, and it feels flimsy. If it gets attention, the attention is momentary. You must see whatever you produce as something that has a life and presence of its own. This presence can be vibrant and visceral, or it can be weak and lifeless. A character in a novel, for instance, will come to life for the reader if the writer has put great effort into imagining the details of that character. The writer does not need to literally lay out these details; readers will feel it in the work and will intuit the level of research that went into the creation of it. All living things are an amalgam of intricate levels of details, animated by the dynamic that connects them. Seeing your work as something alive, your path to mastery is to study and absorb these details in a universal fashion, to the point at which you feel the life force and can express it effortlessly in your work.

在你的作品中，你必须追随达芬奇的脚步。大多数人缺乏耐心去深入思考作品中那些内在的细微之处和细节。他们急于创造效果、引起轰动；他们用大笔触来思考。他们的作品不可避免地暴露出他们对细节的缺乏关注——无法与公众产生深刻共鸣，而且显得单薄。即使引起了关注，这种关注也只是昙花一现。你必须将你创作的任何作品视为拥有生命和存在感的东西。这种存在感可以是鲜活的、发自肺腑的，也可以是虚弱的、毫无生气的。例如，如果作者在小说中花费了大量精力去想象人物的细节，那么这个人物就会在读者面前栩栩如生。作者无需逐字逐句地展现这些细节；读者会在作品中感受到它们，并直观地感受到创作过程中投入的研究水平。所有生物都是由错综复杂的细节组成的，它们被连接在一起的动态赋予生命。将您的工作视为活生生的东西，您通往精通的道路就是以普遍的方式研究和吸收这些细节，直到您感受到生命力并可以在您的工作中毫不费力地表达它。

# ↩

5. Widen your vision—the Global Perspective

5. 拓展视野——全球视野

Early in his career as a boxing trainer, Freddie Roach felt like he knew the business well enough to become highly successful at it. (For more information on Roach see chapter 1 , here , and chapter 3 , here .) He had fought for years as a professional; he had a boxer’s feel for the game. His own trainer had been the legendary Eddie Futch, who had trained Joe Frazier, among others. When Roach’s career as a boxer had ended in the mid-1980s, he had served as an apprentice trainer for several years under Futch himself. On his own, Roach had created a novel training technique based on the use of sparring mitts. Wearing these large mitts, he could spar with and teach his fighters in the ring, in real time. This added another dimension to his instruction. He worked hard at building a personal rapport with his fighters. And finally, he developed the practice of poring over videos of opposing fighters, studying their styles in depth, and devising an effective counter-strategy based on this study.

在其拳击教练生涯早期，弗雷迪·罗奇 (Freddie Roach) 觉得自己对这项业务足够了解，足以在该领域取得巨大成功。 （有关罗奇的更多信息，请参阅此处的第一章和此处的第三章。）他作为职业拳击手征战多年，对比赛有着拳击手的直觉。他的私人教练是传奇人物埃迪·富奇 (Eddie Futch)，富奇还曾训练过乔·弗雷泽 (Joe Frazier) 等人。罗奇的拳击手生涯于 20 世纪 80 年代中期结束，之后在富奇手下担任了数年的学徒教练。罗奇独自创造了一种基于对练手套的新颖训练技术。戴着这些大手套，他可以在擂台上实时与拳手对练并教授他们知识。这为他的教学增添了另一个维度。他努力与拳手建立个人关系。最后，他养成了仔细研究对方拳手视频、深入研究他们的风格并根据研究制定有效反制策略的习惯。

And yet despite all of this work, he sensed that something was missing. Everything would go well in practice, but in actual fights he would often watch from the corner with a helpless feeling as his boxers would go their own way, or would enact only a part of the strategy he had devised. Sometimes he and his fighters would be on the same page, sometimes not. All of this was reflected in the winning percentage of his boxers—good but not great. He could remember back to his own days as a fighter under Futch. He too had done well in practice, but in actual fights and in the heat of the moment, all strategy and preparation would go out the window and he would try to punch his way to a victory. He had always missed something from Futch’s training. Futch had trained him well in all of the separate components of a fight (like offense, defense, and footwork), but Roach never had had a sense of the whole picture or the overall strategy. The connection between himself and Futch had never been that great, and so under pressure in the ring, he would suddenly just revert to his own natural way of fighting. And he now seemed to be having a similar problem with his own fighters.

然而，尽管付出了这么多努力，他还是感觉少了点什么。训练时一切顺利，但在实际比赛中，他常常只能无助地站在角落里看着他的拳手们各行其是，或者只执行他制定的策略的一部分。有时他和他的拳手们能达成共识，有时则不然。所有这些都反映在他拳手们的胜率上——不错，但谈不上出色。他回想起自己在富奇手下打拳的日子。他训练时也表现不错，但在实际比赛中，在关键时刻，所有的策略和准备都会抛诸脑后，他只会一味地用拳头去争取胜利。他总是忽略富奇训练中的一些东西。富奇训练了他拳击的各个组成部分（比如进攻、防守和步法），但罗奇始终缺乏全局观或整体策略。他和富奇之间的默契从来就没那么好，所以在擂台上承受压力时，他会突然恢复到自己自然的战斗方式。现在，他似乎也和自己的拳手们遇到了类似的问题。

Trying to feel his way through to a process that would bring better results, Roach decided he needed to do for his fighters what had never been done for himself in his own career—namely, to give them a feel for the complete picture of the fight. He wanted them to enact this script over all the rounds, and to deepen the connection between fighter and trainer. He began by expanding the mitt work, making it not just a component in the training process, but the focal point. Now he would spend hours sparring with his fighters over several rounds. Day after day, feeling their punches and getting a sense of the rhythm of their footwork, he could almost get inside their skin. He could feel their moods, the level of their focus, and the degree to which they were open to instruction. Without ever having to say a word, he could alter their moods and focus by the intensity of the mitt work he did with them.

为了摸索出一个能带来更好结果的训练方法，罗奇决定为他的拳手们做一件他自己职业生涯中从未做过的事情——让他们感受比赛的全貌。他希望他们在所有回合中都演绎出这个剧本，并加深拳手与教练之间的联系。他首先扩展了拳击手套练习，使其不仅仅是训练过程的一部分，更是训练的焦点。现在，他会花费数小时与拳手进行数回合的对练。日复一日，感受他们的出拳，感受他们步法的节奏，他几乎可以进入他们的内心。他能感受到他们的情绪、专注程度以及他们接受指导的程度。无需多言，他就能通过拳击手套练习的强度来改变他们的情绪和专注力。

Having trained as a fighter since he was six years old, Roach had a feel for every square inch of the ring. With his eyes closed he could gauge exactly where he stood in the ring at any moment. Training his fighters for hours with the mitt work, he could imprint into them his own sixth sense for the space itself, deliberately maneuvering them into bad positions so they could feel in advance how they were approaching such a dangerous space. In the same way, he would impart to them several ways to avoid such dead positions.

罗奇自六岁起就开始接受拳击训练，对拳击台上的每一寸空间都了如指掌。即使闭上眼睛，他也能随时准确地判断自己在拳击台上的位置。他用拳击手套训练拳手数小时，将自己对空间的第六感深深植入他们的心中。他会故意将他们摆成不利的姿势，让他们提前预感到自己即将接近如此危险的空间。同样，他也会教给他们一些避开这种死角的方法。

One day, as he was studying a video of an opposing fighter, he had an epiphany—his way of watching videos was all wrong. In general, he would focus on a fighter’s style, which is something boxers can control and alter for strategic purposes. This suddenly seemed like a superficial way of studying the opponent. A far better strategy would be to look for their habits or tics, the things they couldn’t control no matter how hard they tried. Every fighter has such tics—they are signs of something deeply wired into their rhythms—and they translate into potential weaknesses. Discovering these tics and habits would give Roach a much deeper read on the opponent, cutting to his psyche and to his heart.

有一天，当他研究一位对手的比赛录像时，他突然顿悟——他看录像的方式完全错了。通常，他会关注对手的风格，而风格是拳击手可以控制并根据战略目标进行调整的。突然间，这种研究对手的方式显得肤浅。更好的策略是寻找他们的习惯或动作，那些无论他们多么努力都无法控制的东西。每个拳击手都有这样的动作——它们是某种深深植根于他们节奏的迹象——它们会转化为潜在的弱点。发现这些动作和习惯可以让罗奇更深入地了解对手，直击他的心理和内心。

He began to look for signs of this in the tapes he watched, and in the beginning it would take him several days to see anything. But in the course of watching so many hours on the opposing fighter, he would get a feel for his ways of moving and thinking. Eventually, he would find the habit he was looking for—for instance, a slight motion of the head that always foreshadowed a particular punch. Now that he had found it, he would see it everywhere on the tapes. After doing this for many different fights over several years, he developed a feel for identifying such tics much more quickly.

他开始在自己观看的录像带中寻找这种迹象，一开始要花好几天才能发现。但在长时间观察对方拳手的过程中，他逐渐了解对方的移动和思维方式。最终，他会找到自己想要的习惯——比如，头部轻微的摆动总是预示着某一特定拳法的出击。既然他找到了，他就能从录像带中随处看到它。在多年观看了多场比赛后，他逐渐掌握了识别此类抽搐的技巧，速度快了很多。

Based on these discoveries, he would craft a complete strategy that had built-in flexibility. Depending on what the opponent showed in the first round, Roach would have ready several options for his own fighter that would surprise and upset the opponent, keeping him on his heels and in react mode. His strategy would encompass the entire fight. If necessary, his own fighter could sacrifice a round or two without ever losing control of the overall dynamic. Now, in the mitt work, he would go over the strategy endlessly. Carefully mimicking the tics and rhythms of the opponent he had come to know so well, he could show his fighters how to mercilessly take advantage of their habits and weaknesses; he would go over the various options to adopt, depending on what the opponent revealed in the first round. By the time the fight itself approached, his fighters would feel as if they had already fought and destroyed this opponent, having faced Roach so many times in preparation.

基于这些发现，他会制定一套完整且具有内在灵活性的策略。根据对手在第一回合的表现，罗奇会为己方拳手准备多种出其不意的应对方案，使其措手不及，从而让对手措手不及，并随时准备做出反应。他的策略将贯穿整场比赛。如有必要，己方拳手可以牺牲一两回合，而不会失去对整体局势的控制。现在，在拳击手套练习中，他会反复演练这个策略。他仔细模仿对手的动作和节奏，他已经非常了解对手，他会向拳手们展示如何毫不留情地利用他们的习惯和弱点；他会根据对手在第一回合的表现，反复演练各种可采取的方案。当比赛真正开始时，他的拳手们会感觉自己已经与对手交手并击败了对手，因为他们已经在准备阶段与罗奇交手过无数次。

During the progress of the fights themselves, Roach now had a completely different feeling than in the years before. The connection with his fighters was absolute. His vision of the whole picture—the spirit of the opponent, the way to dominate the ring space within each round, the overall strategy to win the fight—was now deeply imprinted into the footwork, punching, and thinking of his own fighter. He could almost feel himself in the ring exchanging punches, but now he had the ultimate satisfaction of controlling both the mind of his own fighter and that of the opponent’s. He would watch with mounting excitement as his fighters would slowly wear down their opponents, exploiting their habits and getting inside their heads just as he had taught them to.

在比赛进行的过程中，罗奇如今的感受与往年截然不同。他与对手的默契达到了炉火纯青的地步。他对比赛全局的洞见——对手的精神状态，如何在每一回合中掌控擂台空间，以及赢得比赛的整体策略——如今都深深地烙印在对手的步法、出拳和思维方式中。他几乎能感觉到自己在擂台上互相挥拳，但现在，他拥有了控制对手和己方拳手思想的终极满足感。他会越来越兴奋地看着自己的拳手们慢慢地消耗对手，利用他们的习惯，像他教的那样，洞察他们的内心世界。

His winning percentage started to climb to a level that was unprecedented in the sport. His success extended beyond the main fighter in his stable, Manny Pacquiao, to include nearly all of his boxers. Since 2003 he has been named Boxing Trainer of the Year five times, no other previous trainer having received the award more than twice. It seems that in modern boxing he is now in a class all by himself.

他的胜率开始攀升至拳击界前所未有的水平。他的成功不仅惠及他手下的主力拳手曼尼·帕奎奥，几乎惠及他手下的所有拳手。自2003年以来，他已五次荣膺年度最佳拳击教练，此前从未有教练获得过两次以上的殊荣。在现代拳击界，他似乎已然独树一帜。

If we look closely at the career path of Freddie Roach, we can see a transparent example of the development of mastery. His father, a former New England featherweight champion himself, had pushed all of his sons into the sport at a very early age. Freddie Roach himself had begun serious training as a boxer at the age of six, and this continued all the way to the age of eighteen, when he turned professional. Those twelve years added up to an extremely deep level of practice and immersion in the sport. For the next eight years of his life, until he retired from the sport, he fought fifty-three bouts, an intense fighting schedule. As someone who enjoyed practicing and training, the number of hours he spent in the gym as a professional boxer was much higher than that of other fighters. After retirement he stayed around the sport, working as an apprentice trainer for Eddie Futch. By the time he began his own career as a trainer, he had accumulated so many overall hours of work in the sport that he already saw boxing from a perspective that was much wider and deeper than that of other trainers. And so when he felt that there was an even higher level to aim for, this intuition was based on the depth of all those years of practical experience. Inspired by this feeling, he was able to analyze his own work up to that point and see its limitations.

如果我们仔细观察弗雷迪·罗奇的职业道路，就能看到一个清晰的精湛技艺发展历程。他的父亲曾是新英格兰羽量级冠军，从很小的时候就鼓励所有儿子投身拳击运动。弗雷迪·罗奇本人从六岁就开始认真训练拳击手，一直坚持到十八岁成为职业拳击手。这十二年积累了极其深厚的练习和对拳击运动的沉浸感。在接下来的八年里，直到退役，他参加了五十三场比赛，赛程安排紧凑。作为一个热爱练习和训练的人，他在拳击馆里度过的职业拳击手时光比其他拳击手要多得多。退役后，他依然坚持拳击运动，担任埃迪·富奇的学徒教练。到他开始自己的教练生涯时，他已经积累了丰富的拳击训练经验，以至于他看待拳击的视角比其他教练更加广阔和深刻。所以，当他感觉到还有更高的目标时，这种直觉是基于多年实践经验的深度。受这种感觉的启发，他能够分析自己迄今为止的工作，并发现其局限性。

Roach knew from his own career that so much of boxing is mental. A fighter who enters the ring with a clear sense of purpose and strategy, and with the confidence that comes from complete preparation, has a much better chance of prevailing. It was one thing to imagine giving his fighters such an advantage, but it was quite another to bring it to pass. Before a fight there are so many distractions, and during a match it is so easy to simply react emotionally to the punches and lose any sense of strategy. To overcome these problems, he developed a two-pronged approach—he crafted a comprehensive and fluid strategy based on his perception of the opponent’s habits, and he imprinted this strategy into the nervous system of his fighters through hours of mitt work. On this level, his training did not consist of individual elements that he worked on with his boxers, but of an integrated, seamless form of preparation that closely simulated the experience of a fight, repeated over and over again. It took many years of a hit-and-miss process to create this high-level training, but when it all came together his success rate skyrocketed.

罗奇从自己的职业生涯中深知，拳击很大程度上取决于心理。如果一位拳手带着清晰的目标和策略，以及充分准备带来的自信踏入拳台，那么他获胜的几率会大得多。想象能为他的拳手带来这样的优势是一回事，但真正实现它又是另一回事。赛前干扰因素太多，比赛过程中很容易对拳头产生情绪反应，最终失去策略。为了克服这些问题，他开发了一种双管齐下的方法：他根据对手的习惯制定了一套全面而流畅的策略，并通过数小时的拳击手套训练，将这一策略深深地植入拳手的神经系统中。在这个层面上，他的训练并非由他与拳手们单独练习的单个动作组成，而是一种整合的、天衣无缝的准备方式，这种准备方式紧密模拟了比赛的体验，并一遍又一遍地重复。经过多年的摸索，他才创造出这种高水平的训练，但当一切顺利时，他的成功率就猛增。

In any competitive environment in which there are winners or losers, the person who has the wider, more global perspective will inevitably prevail. The reason is simple: such a person will be able to think beyond the moment and control the overall dynamic through careful strategizing. Most people are perpetually locked in the present. Their decisions are overly influenced by the most immediate event; they easily become emotional and ascribe greater significance to a problem than it should have in reality. Moving toward mastery will naturally bring you a more global outlook, but it is always wise to expedite the process by training yourself early on to continually enlarge your perspective. You can do so by always reminding yourself of the overall purpose of the work you are presently engaged in and how this meshes with your long-term goals. In dealing with any problem, you must train yourself to look at how it inevitably connects to a larger picture. If your work is not having the desired effect, you must look at it from all angles until you find the source of the problem. You must not merely observe the rivals in your field, but dissect and uncover their weaknesses. “Look wider and think further ahead” must be your motto. Through such mental training, you will smooth the path to mastery while separating yourself ever further from the competition.

在任何竞争激烈、有输有赢的环境中，拥有更广阔、更全球化视野的人必然会胜出。原因很简单：这样的人能够超越当下，通过精心策划掌控全局。大多数人总是被困在当下。他们的决策过度受眼前事件的影响；他们很容易情绪化，并把问题置于比实际更重要的地位。迈向精通自然会让你拥有更全球化的视野，但尽早训练自己不断拓展视野，以加快这一进程始终是明智之举。你可以不断提醒自己当前工作的总体目标，以及它如何与你的长期目标相契合。在处理任何问题时，你都必须训练自己去思考它与更广阔的图景之间必然存在的联系。如果你的工作没有达到预期的效果，你必须从各个角度审视它，直到找到问题的根源。你不能仅仅观察你所在领域的竞争对手，还要剖析并发现他们的弱点。 “眼界要更开阔，思维要更远大”必须是你的座右铭。通过这样的心理训练，你将铺平通往精通的道路，并在竞争中脱颖而出。

# ↩

6. Submit to the other—The Inside-out Perspective

6. 顺服他人——由内而外的视角

As narrated in chapter 2 ( here ), in December 1977, Daniel Everett, along with his wife, Keren, and their two children, arrived in a remote village in the Amazonian jungles of Brazil, where they would end up spending a good part of the next twenty years of their lives. The village belonged to a tribe scattered in the area known as the Pirahã. Everett had been sent there by the Summer Institute of Languages (SIL)—a Christian organization that trains future missionaries in the linguistic skills that will enable them to translate the Bible into indigenous languages and help spread the Gospel. Everett himself was an ordained minister.

正如第二章（此处）所述，1977年12月，丹尼尔·埃弗里特携妻子凯伦和两个孩子抵达巴西亚马逊丛林中的一个偏远村庄，并在那里度过了人生中接下来的二十年。这个村庄属于一个散居在皮拉罕地区的部落。埃弗里特受夏季语言学院（SIL）的派遣前往那里——这是一个基督教组织，旨在培养未来的传教士的语言技能，使他们能够将圣经翻译成当地语言，并帮助传播福音。埃弗里特本人也是一位被任命的牧师。

The directors at SIL considered Pirahã one of the last frontiers in their quest to translate the Bible into all languages; it represented perhaps the most challenging language for any outsider to learn. The Pirahã had lived for centuries in the same Amazonian basin, resisting all attempts to assimilate or learn Portuguese. Living in such isolation, a point was reached in which no one outside of the Pirahã could speak or understand their language. Several missionaries had been sent there after World War II, and all had failed to make much progress; despite their training and linguistic talents, they found the language maddeningly elusive.

SIL 的主管们认为皮拉罕语是他们寻求将圣经翻译成所有语言的最后前沿阵地之一；它或许是任何外来者学习时最难的语言。皮拉罕人曾在亚马逊盆地生活了几个世纪，抵制一切同化或学习葡萄牙语的尝试。如此与世隔绝的生活，导致皮拉罕人以外的人都无法说或听懂他们的语言。二战后，几位传教士被派往那里，但都未能取得多大进展；尽管他们受过训练，拥有语言天赋，但他们却发现这种语言难以捉摸。

Daniel Everett was one of the most promising linguists the SIL had seen in a long time, and when the institute presented him with the challenge of the Pirahã he was more than excited. His wife’s parents had been missionaries stationed in Brazil, and Keren had grown up in an environment not too dissimilar to a Pirahã village. It seemed the family was up to the task, and in his first months there Everett made good progress. He attacked the Pirahã language with great energy. Using the methods he had learned at SIL, he slowly built up a vocabulary and the ability to speak some rudimentary sentences. He copied everything down on index cards and carried them in his belt loop. He was a tireless researcher. Although life in the village presented some challenges for him and his family, he was comfortable with the Pirahã and hoped they had accepted his presence. But soon he began to feel that all was not right.

丹尼尔·埃弗里特是SIL长期以来最有前途的语言学家之一。当学院向他提出皮拉罕语的挑战时，他兴奋不已。他岳父岳母曾是驻扎在巴西的传教士，而凯伦的成长环境与皮拉罕村落并无太大差异。看来，这家人能够胜任这项任务，埃弗里特在最初的几个月里取得了长足的进步。他全力以赴地学习皮拉罕语。运用在SIL学到的方法，他慢慢积累了词汇量，并能说一些基本的句子。他把所有东西都抄在索引卡上，挂在腰带环里。他是一位不知疲倦的研究者。尽管村里的生活给他和家人带来了一些挑战，但他与皮拉罕人相处融洽，并希望他们能够接受他的存在。但很快，他就开始感到一切都不对劲了。

Part of the SIL method was to encourage immersion in the indigenous culture as the best means for learning the language. Missionaries are essentially abandoned to their fate, to sink or swim in the local culture without any crutches to lean on. Perhaps unconsciously, however, Everett could not help but keep some distance and feel ever so slightly superior to the backward culture of the Pirahã. He became aware of this inner distance after several incidents that occurred in the village.

SIL教学法的一部分是鼓励沉浸于本土文化，将其作为学习语言的最佳途径。传教士们基本上被抛弃，任由命运摆布，在当地文化中沉浮沉浮，没有任何依靠。然而，或许是无意识的，埃弗里特情不自禁地与落后的皮拉罕文化保持着一定的距离，并感到自己略微优越于他们。村里发生的几件事让他意识到了这种内心的疏离感。

First, several months into their stay, his wife and daughter nearly died from malaria. He was rather perturbed by the lack of empathy from the Pirahã about this. A little later, Everett and his wife tried desperately to nurse back to health a Pirahã infant that was gravely ill. The Pirahã were certain the baby would die, and seemed bothered by the missionaries’ efforts. Then one day, Everett and his wife discovered the baby was dead; the Pirahã had forced alcohol down its throat to kill it. Although he tried to rationalize this event to himself, he could not help but feel some disgust. On another occasion, for apparently no reason, a group of Pirahã men had gotten very drunk and were looking for him in order to kill him. He managed to escape the threat, and nothing else ever happened, but it made him wonder about the safety of his family.

首先，在他们居住几个月后，他的妻子和女儿险些死于疟疾。皮拉罕人对此缺乏同情，这让他颇为不安。不久之后，埃弗里特和他的妻子拼命照顾一个病重的皮拉罕婴儿。皮拉罕人确信婴儿必死无疑，似乎对传教士的举动感到不安。后来有一天，埃弗里特和他的妻子发现婴儿死了；皮拉罕人强迫婴儿喝酒，想杀死它。尽管他试图为这件事找到合理的解释，但还是忍不住感到一阵恶心。还有一次，一群皮拉罕人似乎毫无缘由地喝得酩酊大醉，四处寻找他，想要杀死他。他设法逃脱了威胁，之后再也没有发生其他事情，但这让他对家人的安全感到担忧。

More than anything, however, he began to feel disappointed by the Pirahã themselves. He had read much about Amazonian tribes, and by any standards the Pirahã did not measure up. They had virtually no material culture—no important tools, artwork, costumes, or jewelry. If women needed a basket, they would find some moist palm leaves, quickly weave them together, use the basket once or twice, and then abandon it. They placed no value on material things, and nothing in their villages was designed to last very long. They had few rituals, and as far as he could tell no real folklore or creation myths. One time he had been woken up by excitement in the village—apparently a spirit who lived above the clouds had been sighted and was warning them not to go into the jungle. He looked at what they were looking at and saw nothing. There were no colorful stories being told about this, no relation to any myth, just some villagers excitedly staring off into empty space. They seemed to him like Boy Scouts on a camping trip, or a group of hippies—a tribe that had somehow lost its own culture.

然而，最让他失望的是，皮拉罕人本身也让他感到失望。他读过很多关于亚马逊部落的资料，但无论以何种标准衡量，皮拉罕人都远远达不到他们的要求。他们几乎没有任何物质文化——没有重要的工具、艺术品、服饰或珠宝。如果妇女需要篮子，她们会找一些潮湿的棕榈叶，快速地把它们编在一起，用一两次就扔掉。他们不重视物质，村子里的东西也都不是设计用来长久使用的。他们几乎没有什么仪式，据他所知，也没有任何真正的民间传说或创世神话。有一次，他被村子里的一阵骚动惊醒——显然是有人看到了一个居住在云层之上的神灵，警告他们不要进入丛林。他望向他们所看到的景象，却什么也没看到。没有关于此事的精彩故事，也没有任何神话传说，只有一些村民兴奋地凝视着空旷的天空。在他看来，他们就像是野营旅行中的童子军，或者一群嬉皮士——一个不知何故失去了自己文化的部落。

This disappointment and unease coincided with frustration in his own work. He had made some progress with the language, but it seemed that the more words and phrases he learned, the more questions and puzzles he uncovered. He would think that he had mastered a particular expression, only to find it meant something different or something larger than he had imagined. He could see the children learning the language so easily, but to him who now lived among them, it seemed beyond his reach. Then one day he experienced what he would later realize was a turning point.

这种失望和不安与他自己工作中的挫败感不谋而合。他的语言学习取得了一些进步，但似乎学的单词和短语越多，他发现的问题和谜题就越多。他以为自己掌握了某个表达方式，却发现它的含义与他想象的不同，或者比他想象的更深刻。他看到孩子们学语言学得如此轻松，但对于如今生活在他们中间的他来说，这似乎遥不可及。后来有一天，他经历了后来他意识到的转折点。

The thatch roof of his family’s hut needed replacing, and he decided to enlist some villagers in the effort. Although he felt he had integrated himself into their lives, he had never ventured very far into the surrounding jungles with the Pirahã men. Finally, on this occasion he would go much farther than before to gather the necessary materials. Suddenly, during this trip, he saw an entirely different side to them. While he was stomping and whacking his way through the brush, they seemed to glide through the thick jungle without being touched by a single branch. He was not able to keep up with them, and so he stopped and rested. In the distance he could hear strange sounds—the Pirahã men were clearly speaking to one another, but their words were somehow transposed into whistles. He realized that in the jungle they used this different form of communication, one that would not stand out from the jungle hum. It was a marvelous way to talk without attracting attention, and must have been a great help in hunting.

他家茅草屋顶需要更换，于是他决定招募一些村民一起帮忙。虽然他觉得自己已经融入了他们的生活，但他从未和皮拉罕人一起深入周围的丛林。这次，他终于可以走得比以前更远，去收集必要的材料了。突然间，在这次旅程中，他看到了他们截然不同的一面。当他跺脚、劈啪作响地穿过灌木丛时，他们仿佛在茂密的丛林中滑行，连一根树枝都没碰到。他跟不上他们，于是停下来休息。远处传来奇怪的声音——皮拉罕人显然在互相交谈，但他们的声音不知何故被转换成了口哨声。他意识到，在丛林里，他们使用着这种独特的交流方式，一种不会在丛林嗡嗡声中被忽略的方式。这是一种绝妙的交流方式，既不引人注意，又能有效地帮助狩猎。

Now he joined them on subsequent forays into the jungle, and his respect for them increased. They could hear and see things he could not perceive at all—dangerous animals, signs of something different or suspicious. Occasionally, it would rain when it was not the rainy season, and in the jungle they had a sixth sense for the weather and knew when a heavy rain was coming hours before it arrived. (They could even predict the arrival of a plane several hours in advance, although he never figured out how.) They could identify every plant and its possible medicinal purposes, and knew every square inch of the jungle. If they saw bubbles or ripples in the river, they could instantly tell whether the movement was from a falling rock or from some dangerous animal lurking below the surface. They had a mastery of their environment that he could not sense by seeing them in the village. And as he became aware of this, he began to understand that their life and culture, which at first glance had seemed rather poor according to our standards, was actually something remarkably rich. Over the course of hundreds of years they had adapted a way of life that was perfectly wedded to the harsh circumstances of their environment.

如今，他又一次加入他们深入丛林的探险，对他们的敬意与日俱增。他们能听到和看到他根本无法察觉的东西——危险的动物，以及某种异常或可疑迹象。偶尔，雨季之外也会下雨，而丛林里的他们拥有对天气的第六感，能在暴雨来临前几小时预知何时到来。（他们甚至可以提前几个小时预测飞机的到来，尽管他始终不明白是怎么回事。）他们能识别每一种植物及其可能的药用价值，对丛林的每一寸土地都了如指掌。如果他们看到河里有气泡或涟漪，他们就能立刻判断出这动静是落石造成的，还是潜伏在水面下的危险动物造成的。他们对周围环境的掌控力，是他在村子里无法察觉的。当他意识到这一点时，他开始明白，他们的生活和文化，乍一看，以我们的标准来看，似乎相当贫瘠，但实际上却异常丰富。数百年来，他们已经适应了一种与恶劣环境完美契合的生活方式。

Now, as he looked back on the same incidents that had troubled him before, he could see them in a new light. Living so closely to death on a daily basis (the jungle was teeming with dangers and diseases), they had developed a rather stoic attitude. They could not afford to waste time or energy on mourning rituals or on too much empathy. They could sense when someone was going to die, and being certain that the infant the Everetts had tried to nurse was doomed, they thought it easier and better to hasten its death and not look back. The village men who had thought of killing him had heard that he did not like their drinking; they feared that he was yet another outsider who was going to impose his values and authority on them. They had their reasons for behaving as they did, but only with time could he see them clearly.

如今，当他回想起那些曾经困扰他的事件时，他有了新的视角。他们每天都与死亡擦肩而过（丛林中危机四伏，疾病肆虐），养成了相当坚忍的心态。他们没时间或精力浪费在哀悼仪式或过多的同情上。他们能预感到何时有人会死去，而埃弗雷特夫妇努力抚养的那个婴儿注定要死去，他们认为加速它的死亡，不再回头，是更轻松、更好的选择。那些想过要杀了他的村子里的人听说他不喜欢他们喝酒；他们担心他又是一个外来者，会把自己的价值观和权威强加给他们。他们这样做自有其理由，但只有随着时间的推移，他才能看清这些理由。

He extended his participation in their lives to other aspects—hunting and fishing excursions, gathering roots and vegetables in the fields, and so on. He and his family would share meals with them and interacted with them as much as possible, and in this way he slowly immersed himself in the Pirahã culture. Although it was not immediately apparent, this also initiated a change in his learning of the language itself. It started to come more naturally—less from the tireless work of a field researcher and more from within, from simply living inside their culture. He began to think like a Pirahã, to foresee their reactions to what some visiting Westerner would ask of them; he got inside their sense of humor, and the kinds of stories they liked to relate around the campfire.

他将自己对皮拉罕人生活的参与延伸到了其他方面——狩猎捕鱼、在田间采集根茎蔬菜等等。他和家人会与他们一起用餐，并尽可能多地与他们互动，就这样，他慢慢地融入了皮拉罕文化。虽然并非一蹴而就，但这也引发了他学习语言本身的转变。这种转变开始变得更加自然——不再是来自田野研究员的孜孜不倦的努力，而是来自内心，源于简单地融入他们的文化。他开始像皮拉罕人一样思考，预见他们对来访的西方人提出的问题的反应；他了解他们的幽默感，以及他们喜欢在篝火旁讲述的那些故事。

And as he began to understand more aspects of their culture and to communicate with a higher degree of proficiency, he noticed more and more peculiarities to the Pirahã language. Everett had been indoctrinated in the prevailing beliefs in linguistics championed by Noam Chomsky. According to Chomsky all languages share certain features, which he designates as Universal Grammar. This grammar implies a common neurological trait to the brain that allows for the learning of languages among children. According to this theory, we are hardwired for language. But the more time Everett spent among the Pirahã, the more signs he saw that their language did not share some of these common features. They had no numbers and no system for counting. They had no specific words for colors, but rather described colors through phrases that related to real objects.
