随着他开始了解更多皮拉罕文化的方面并更熟练地交流，他注意到皮拉罕语言越来越多的特点。埃弗里特被灌输了诺姆乔姆斯基所倡导的语言学主流观点。根据乔姆斯基的说法，所有语言都具有某些共同的特征，他将这些特征称为普遍语法。这种语法意味着大脑具有一种共同的神经特性，使得儿童能够学习语言。根据这一理论，我们天生就具有语言能力。但埃弗里特在皮拉罕人中生活的时间越长，他就越发现有迹象表明他们的语言并不具备这些共同特征。他们没有数字，也没有计数系统。他们没有专门描述颜色的词汇，而是通过与真实物体相关的短语来描述颜色。

According to Universal Grammar, the most important trait shared by all languages is what is known as recursion, the embedding of phrases within phrases that gives language an almost infinite potential to relate experiences. An example would be, “the food you are eating smells good.” Everett could find absolutely no evidence for recursion in Pirahã. They would express such ideas in simple, assertive phrases, such as “You are eating food. That food smells good.” These exceptions to Universal Grammar began to pile up as he looked for them.

根据普遍语法，所有语言最重要的共同特征是所谓的递归，即短语嵌套短语，这赋予了语言几乎无限的关联体验的潜力。例如，“你正在吃的食物闻起来很香”。埃弗里特在皮拉罕语中完全找不到任何递归的证据。他们会用简单、肯定的短语来表达这种想法，例如“你正在吃食物。那食物闻起来很香”。随着他不断寻找，这些违反普遍语法的例外情况开始逐渐增多。

At the same time, the Pirahã culture began to make increasing sense to him, which altered his conception of their language. For instance, one time he learned a new word that a Pirahã explained to him meant “what is in your head when you sleep.” The word then means to dream. But the word was used with a special intonation that Pirahã use when they are referring to a new experience. Questioning further, he saw that to them dreaming is simply a different form of experience, not at all a fiction. A dream is as real and immediate to them as anything they encounter in waking life. With more and more of these examples, a theory began to stir in his head, one that he would call the Immediate Experience Principle (IEP). What this means is that for the Pirahã all that concerns them are things that can be experienced in the here and now, or that relate to something that someone personally has experienced in the very recent past.

与此同时，皮拉罕文化对他来说也越来越清晰，这改变了他对皮拉罕语言的理解。例如，有一次，他学到了一个新词，一个皮拉罕人向他解释，意思是“你睡觉时脑子里在想什么”。这个词的意思是做梦。但这个词的语调很特别，皮拉罕人在描述新体验时会用这种语调。进一步探究后，他发现，对他们来说，做梦只是一种不同的体验形式，而非虚构。梦境对他们来说，就像他们在清醒时遇到的任何事物一样真实、直接。随着这样的例子越来越多，一个理论开始在他脑海中萌生，他称之为“直接体验原则”（IEP）。这意味着，对皮拉罕人来说，他们所关注的都是当下可以体验到的事物，或者与某人在不久前亲身经历过的事物相关。

This would account for the peculiarities of their language—colors and numbers are abstractions that do not fit IEP. Instead of recursion, they have simple declarative statements on what they have seen. His theory would account for their lack of material culture, or of creation myths and stories that refer to something in the past. They had developed this form of culture as the perfect adaptation to their environment and needs; it made them profoundly immersed in the present and remarkably happy. It helped them to psychologically transcend the difficulties of their environment. Because they had no need for anything beyond their immediate experience, they had no words for such things. Everett’s theory was the fruit of years and years of deep immersion in their culture. As it came together in his mind, it explained so many things. It could not have been seen or understood in the course of a few months or years observing them from the outside.

这可以解释他们语言的特殊性——颜色和数字是抽象概念，不符合IEP。他们没有递归，而是对所见事物进行简单的陈述。他的理论可以解释他们缺乏物质文化，或者缺乏与过去事物相关的创世神话和故事。他们发展了这种文化形式，完美地适应了他们的环境和需求；它让他们深深地沉浸在当下，感到无比快乐。它帮助他们在心理上超越了环境的困境。因为他们不需要任何超越直接经验的东西，所以他们没有语言来形容这些东西。埃弗里特的理论是多年来深入研究他们文化的成果。当这个理论在他脑海中形成时，它解释了很多事情。仅仅通过几个月或几年的外部观察是无法看到或理解的。

The conclusion that he drew from this, one that would provoke much controversy within the field of linguistics, is that culture plays an enormous role in the development of language, and that languages are more different than we have imagined. Although there are certainly common aspects to all human languages, there can be no universal grammar that overrides the relevance of culture. Such a conclusion, he determined, can only come through years of intense fieldwork. Those who make assumptions from far away, based on universal theories, do not see the whole picture. It takes great time and effort to see the differences, to participate in a culture. And because it is so much harder to perceive these differences, culture has not been given its due as one of the primary shaping forces for language and for how we experience the world.

他由此得出的结论在语言学领域引发了诸多争议：文化在语言发展中扮演着重要角色，而且不同语言之间的差异远超乎我们的想象。尽管所有人类语言确实存在一些共同点，但不可能存在一种超越文化相关性的通用语法。他断言，这样的结论只有通过多年深入的田野调查才能得出。那些基于普遍理论、从遥远的地方做出假设的人，并没有看到全局。要发现差异、融入一种文化，需要花费大量的时间和精力。而由于感知这些差异极其困难，文化尚未被赋予应有的地位，成为塑造语言以及我们体验世界方式的主要力量之一。

The deeper he immersed himself into Pirahã culture, the more it changed him. He not only grew disenchanted with the top-down form of research in linguistics and the ideas it led to, but also with his work as a missionary. These were both attempts to impose on the Pirahã alien ideas and values. He could only imagine that spreading the Gospel and converting them to Christianity would completely ruin their culture, which had shaped itself so perfectly to their circumstances and made them so content. With these ideas, he lost his faith in Christianity itself, and finally left the church. Learning an alien culture from so deeply inside it, he could no longer accept the superiority of one particular belief or value system. To hold such an opinion, he determined, is merely an illusion that comes from remaining on the outside.

他越是深入皮拉罕文化，就越是被它改变。他不仅对自上而下的语言学研究模式及其衍生的理念感到幻灭，也对自己的传教工作感到厌倦。这两种做法都试图将外来的思想和价值观强加给皮拉罕人。他只能想象，传播福音并让他们皈依基督教会彻底摧毁他们的文化，而这种文化完美地契合了他们的处境，也让他们如此满足。带着这些想法，他对基督教本身失去了信仰，最终离开了教会。在如此深入地了解一种外来文化之后，他再也无法接受某种特定信仰或价值体系的优越性。他认定，持有这种观点只是一种局外人产生的幻觉。

For many researchers in circumstances similar to Daniel Everett’s, the natural response is to rely on the skills and concepts they have learned for research purposes. This would mean studying the Pirahã as closely as Everett had done in the beginning, taking extensive notes, and trying to make this alien culture fit into the framework already designated by the prevailing theories in linguistics and anthropology. Doing so, such researchers would be rewarded with articles in prestigious journals and solid positions within academia. But in the end they would remain on the outside looking in, and a good portion of their conclusions would simply be confirmations of what they had already assumed. The wealth of information that Everett had uncovered about their language and culture would remain unnoticed. Imagine how often this has occurred in the past and still occurs in the present, and how many secrets of indigenous cultures have been lost to us because of this outsider approach.

对于许多与丹尼尔·埃弗里特处境相似的研究人员来说，自然而然的反应是依靠他们所学的技能和概念进行研究。这意味着他们要像埃弗里特最初那样，对皮拉罕人进行深入研究，做大量的笔记，并试图将这种外来文化纳入语言学和人类学主流理论所设定的框架。这样做，这些研究人员将在著名期刊上发表文章，并在学术界获得稳固的地位。但最终，他们仍将停留在局外观察，他们的很大一部分结论只是在证实他们已有的假设。埃弗里特所发现的关于皮拉罕语言和文化的丰富信息将无人问津。想象一下，这种情况在过去发生过多少次，现在仍然在发生，有多少土著文化的秘密因为这种局外人的方式而失传。

Part of this predilection for the outside perspective originates from a prejudice among scientists. Studying from the outside, many would say, preserves our objectivity. But what kind of objectivity is it when the researcher’s perspective is tainted by so many assumptions and predigested theories? The reality of the Pirahã could only be seen from within and from participating in their culture. This does not taint the observer with subjectivity. A scientist can participate from within and yet retain his or her reasoning powers. Everett could stand back from their culture and devise his IEP theory. The intuitive and the rational, the inside perspective and science, can easily coexist. For Everett, choosing this inside path required a great deal of courage. It meant physically subjecting himself to the dangers of their life in the jungle. It led to a difficult confrontation with other linguists and all of the problems such conflict presented for his future career as a professor. It led to a profound disenchantment with Christianity, which had meant so much to him as a young man. But he felt compelled to do so by his desire to uncover the reality. And by moving in this unconventional direction, he was able to master an unbelievably complex language system and gain invaluable insights into their culture and the role of culture in general.

这种对外部视角的偏爱，部分源于科学家的偏见。许多人会说，从外部进行研究能保持我们的客观性。但当研究者的视角被如此多的假设和预设理论所玷污时，这算什么客观性呢？皮拉罕人的现实只有从内部、通过参与他们的文化才能被洞察。这并不会玷污观察者的主观性。科学家可以从内部参与，同时又能保留其推理能力。埃弗里特可以远离他们的文化，设计出他的个人化教育计划（IEP）理论。直觉与理性、内部视角与科学，可以轻松地共存。对埃弗里特来说，选择这条内部道路需要极大的勇气。这意味着他必须亲自面对丛林生活中的危险。这导致了与其他语言学家的艰难对抗，以及这种冲突给他未来的教授生涯带来的所有问题。这也导致他对基督教产生了深深的幻灭，而基督教在他年轻时曾对他意义非凡。但他渴望揭示真相，这驱使他不得不这么做。通过朝着这个非传统的方向探索，他掌握了一套极其复杂的语言系统，并对他们的文化以及文化在总体上的作用获得了宝贵的见解。

Understand: we can never really experience what other people are experiencing. We always remain on the outside looking in, and this is the cause of so many misunderstandings and conflicts. But the primal source of human intelligence comes from the development of mirror neurons (see here ), which gives us the ability to place ourselves in the skin of another and imagine their experience. Through continual exposure to people and by attempting to think inside them we can gain an increasing sense of their perspective, but this requires effort on our part. Our natural tendency is to project onto other people our own beliefs and value systems, in ways in which we are not even aware. When it comes to studying another culture, it is only through the use of our empathic powers and by participating in their lives that we can begin to overcome these natural projections and arrive at the reality of their experience. To do so we must overcome our great fear of the Other and the unfamiliarity of their ways. We must enter their belief and value systems, their guiding myths, their way of seeing the world. Slowly, the distorted lens through which we first viewed them starts to clear up. Going deeper into their Otherness, feeling what they feel, we can discover what makes them different and learn about human nature. This applies to cultures, individuals, and even writers of books. As Nietzsche once wrote, “As soon as you feel yourself against me you have ceased to understand my position and consequently my arguments! You have to be the victim of the same passion .”

要明白：我们永远无法真正体会他人的感受。我们总是局外人，这才是造成诸多误解和冲突的根源。但人类智慧的本源在于镜像神经元（参见此处），它使我们能够设身处地为他人着想，想象他们的经历。通过不断与他人接触，并尝试设身处地地思考，我们可以越来越理解他们的视角，但这需要我们付出努力。我们本能地倾向于将自己的信仰和价值体系投射到他人身上，甚至在不知不觉中。在研究另一种文化时，只有运用我们的共情能力，并参与他们的生活，我们才能克服这些自然的投射，理解他们体验的真谛。要做到这一点，我们必须克服对他人的强烈恐惧以及对他们生活方式的陌生感。我们必须融入他们的信仰和价值体系、他们的指导性神话以及他们看待世界的方式。慢慢地，我们最初看待他们的那副扭曲的眼镜开始清晰起来。深入了解他们的“他者性”，感受他们的感受，我们就能发现他们的不同之处，并了解人性。这适用于不同的文化、不同的个体，甚至不同的作家。正如尼采曾经写道：“一旦你觉得自己与我为敌，你就不再理解我的立场，进而不再理解我的论点！你必然会成为这种激情的受害者。”

# ↩

7. Synthesize all forms of knowledge—
7. 综合各种形式的知识——
The Universal Man/Woman
万能的男人/女人

Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) grew up in an unhappy home in Frankfurt, Germany. His father had a failed career in local politics that had left him embittered, and he had become estranged from his young wife. To make up for his own lack of success, Johann’s father made certain that his son received the finest education possible. He learned the arts, the sciences, numerous languages, various crafts, fencing, and dancing. But Johann found life in the house under the watchful eye of his father unbearable and stultifying. When he finally left home to study at the university in Leipzig, it was as if he had been set free from prison. All of his pent-up energies, his restlessness, his hunger for women and adventures, were suddenly released and he went wild.

约翰·沃尔夫冈·冯·歌德（1749-1832）在德国法兰克福一个不幸的家庭长大。他的父亲在地方政坛的职业生涯失败，让他心怀怨恨，并与年轻的妻子关系疏远。为了弥补自身的不足，约翰的父亲确保儿子接受尽可能最好的教育。他学习了艺术、科学、多种语言、各种手艺、击剑和舞蹈。但约翰却觉得在父亲的严密监视下，家庭生活难以忍受，令人窒息。当他最终离开家，前往莱比锡大学学习时，他仿佛从监狱中解脱出来。他所有被压抑的精力、躁动不安的情绪、对女人和冒险的渴望，都突然被释放，他变得狂野起来。

He lived the life of a dandy, dressing in the most fashionable clothes and seducing as many young women as he could find. He threw himself into the intellectual life of Leipzig; he could be seen in all of the taverns arguing about this or that philosophy with professors and fellow students. His ideas went against the grain—he ranted against Christianity and yearned for the pagan religion of the ancient Greeks. As one professor noted, “It was the well-nigh universal opinion that he had a slate loose in the upper story.”

他过着纨绔子弟的生活，穿着最时髦的衣服，勾引他能找到的所有年轻女性。他全身心投入莱比锡的知识生活；在所有的酒馆里都能看到他与教授和同学们争论各种哲学。他的想法与世隔绝——他大声斥责基督教，却向往古希腊的异教。正如一位教授所说：“几乎所有人都认为，他的楼上有一块松动的石板。”

And then young Johann fell in love, and any remnant of self-control was finally gone. His letters to friends about this love affair caused them great concern. He swung from elation to deep depression, from adoration to distrust. He stopped eating. He proposed marriage, then broke it off. To many it looked like he was on the edge of madness. “I’m going downhill faster every day,” he wrote to a friend. “Three months will see the end of me.” Then suddenly in 1768, in the middle of all this, he collapsed. He awoke to find himself bathed in blood. He had suffered a lung hemorrhage, and for days he was near death. To the doctors, his recovery seemed miraculous; fearful of a relapse, they made him return to his home in Frankfurt, where he was to be confined to his bed for many months.

年轻的约翰坠入爱河，他所有的自制力都彻底崩塌。他写信给朋友们，诉说这段恋情，令他们忧心忡忡。他时而欣喜若狂，时而沮丧失落，时而爱慕，时而猜忌。他停止进食，求婚后又提出分手。在许多人看来，他已濒临疯狂。“我每天都在走下坡路，”他写信给一位朋友，“三个月后我就会死去。” 1768年，在这一切进行到一半时，他突然晕倒了。醒来后，他发现自己浑身是血。他肺部出血，有好几天都奄奄一息。医生们认为他的康复堪称奇迹；由于担心病情复发，他们让他回到法兰克福的家中，在那里卧床数月。

As he emerged from his illness, young Goethe felt like a different person. He was struck now by two ideas that would remain with him for the rest of his life. First, he had the sensation that he possessed a type of inner spirit that he named his daemon . This spirit was an incarnation of all of his intense, restless, demonic energy. It could turn destructive, as it had done in Leipzig. Or he could master it and channel it into something productive. This energy was so powerful that it made him swing from one mood or idea to the opposite—from spirituality to sensuality, from naïveté to craftiness. This daemon, he decided, was a spirit implanted in him at birth and it encompassed his whole being. How he managed this daemon would determine the length of his life and the success of his endeavors.

病愈后，年轻的歌德感觉自己仿佛变了一个人。他突然被两种想法所震撼，并终生铭记。首先，他感觉自己拥有一种内在的灵魂，他称之为“守护神”。这股灵魂是他所有强烈、躁动、恶魔般能量的化身。它可能会变得具有破坏性，就像在莱比锡那样。或者，他可以驾驭它，并将其转化为有益的东西。这股能量如此强大，以至于让他在情绪或想法之间摇摆不定——从灵性到感官享受，从天真到狡猾。他认定，这股守护神是与生俱来的，它包裹着他的整个生命。他如何驾驭这股守护神，将决定他的寿命和事业的成功。

Second, coming so close to death at such an early age made him feel the presence of death in his bones, and this feeling stayed with him for weeks after recovering. As he returned to life, he was suddenly struck by the strangeness of being alive—of possessing a heart and lungs and brain that functioned beyond his conscious control. He felt that there was a life force that transcended the individual incarnations of life, a force not from God (Goethe would remain a pagan his entire life), but from nature itself. In his convalescence he would take long walks in the country, and his personal sense of the strangeness of life was transferred to the sight of plants and trees and animals. What force brought them to their present, perfectly adapted states of life? What was the source of the energy that made them grow?

其次，如此年轻就濒临死亡，让他感受到死亡的气息深入骨髓，这种感觉在他康复数周后依然萦绕不去。当他重获新生时，他突然被活着的奇异感所震撼——拥有一颗不受意识控制的心脏、肺和大脑。他感到有一种超越个体生命化身的生命力，这种力量并非来自上帝（歌德终其一生都是异教徒），而是来自自然本身。在康复期间，他会在乡间长途跋涉，他对生命奇异感的个人感受转移到对一草一木和动物的观察上。是什么力量将它们带到了如今这种完美适应的生命状态？是什么力量驱动着它们生长？

Feeling as if he had been reprieved from a death sentence, he experienced an insatiable curiosity for this life force. An idea came to him for a story based on the famous German legend of a scholar named Faust, who desperately wants to discover the secret of life, and who meets an incarnation of the devil named Mephistopheles who helps him in this quest in exchange for possession of his soul. If ever the restless Faust experiences a moment of contentment and wants nothing more from life, then he is to die and the devil will own his soul. Goethe began to take notes on this drama, and in the dialogues he wrote between the devil and Faust he could hear his own inner voices, his own demonic dualities talking to each other.

他感觉自己仿佛从死刑中获得了缓刑，对这股生命力产生了永不满足的好奇心。他萌生了一个想法，要创作一个基于著名德国传说的故事。故事讲述一位名叫浮士德的学者，他渴望探索生命的奥秘，却遇到了魔鬼的化身——梅菲斯特，梅菲斯特帮助他完成了这一探索，条件是占有他的灵魂。如果焦躁不安的浮士德体验到片刻的满足，不再渴望生活，那么他就会死去，魔鬼将占有他的灵魂。歌德开始记录这出戏，在他记录的魔鬼与浮士德的对话中，他仿佛听到了自己内心的声音，听到了自己魔鬼般的二元性在彼此对话。

Several years later, Goethe began life as a lawyer in Frankfurt. And as before in Leipzig, his daemon seemed to take control of him. He hated the conventional life of a lawyer, and he hated all of the conventions that seemed to dominate social life and to disconnect people from nature. He entertained deeply rebellious thoughts, which he channeled into an epistolary novel— The Sorrows of Young Werther . Although the story was loosely based on people he knew and on a young friend who had committed suicide over a failed romance, most of the ideas in it came from his experiences. The novel promoted the superiority of the emotions, and advocated a return to a life of sensation and to living closer to nature. It was the precursor of the movement that would come to be known throughout Europe as Romanticism, and it created a powerful reaction in Germany and beyond. Overnight, young Goethe became a celebrity. Almost everyone read the book. Hundreds of young people committed suicide in imitation of the despairing Werther.

几年后，歌德在法兰克福开始了律师生涯。和之前在莱比锡一样，他的守护神似乎控制了他。他痛恨律师的墨守成规，也痛恨所有那些似乎主宰着社会生活、将人与自然割裂开来的习俗。他怀有强烈的反叛精神，并将这些思想倾注于书信体小说《少年维特的烦恼》。虽然故事大致取材于他认识的人以及一位因失恋而自杀的年轻朋友，但其中的大部分思想都源于他的经历。这部小说宣扬情感的优越性，提倡回归感性生活，回归自然。它是后来席卷欧洲的浪漫主义运动的先驱，并在德国乃至世界引起了强烈的反响。一夜之间，年轻的歌德成了名人。几乎每个人都读过这本书。数百名年轻人效仿绝望的维特自杀。

For Goethe, this success surprised and baffled him. Suddenly, he was hobnobbing with the most famous writers of his time. Slowly, the daemon reared its ugly head. He gave himself up to a life of wine, women, and parties. His moods began to swing wildly back and forth. He felt a rising disgust—at himself and the world he was frequenting. The circle of writers and intellectuals who dominated his social life annoyed him to no end. They were so smug, and their world was as disconnected from reality and nature as that of lawyers. He felt increasingly constricted by his reputation as a sensational writer.

对歌德来说，这份成功让他既惊讶又困惑。突然之间，他开始与当时最著名的作家们交往。然而，他内心的恶魔却慢慢露出了丑陋的面目。他沉溺于酒色和派对之中。他的情绪开始剧烈波动。他感到一阵阵厌恶——厌恶自己，厌恶他所处的这个世界。主宰他社交生活的那些作家和知识分子圈子让他恼火不已。他们如此自鸣得意，他们的世界与现实和自然脱节，如同律师的世界一样。他越来越感到自己作为“煽情作家”的名声所束缚。

In 1775, a year after the publication of Werther, he received an invitation from the duke of Weimar to stay in his duchy and serve as a personal adviser and minister. The duke was a great admirer of his writing, and was trying to recruit more artists to his rather dull court. For Goethe, however, this was the opportunity he was waiting for. He could say good-bye to the literary world and bury himself in Weimar. He could pour his energies into political work and into science, taming that damnable inner daemon. He accepted the invitation, and except for one later trip to Italy, he would spend the rest of his life in Weimar.

1775年，《维特的烦恼》出版一年后，歌德收到魏玛公爵的邀请，留在公国担任私人顾问和大臣。公爵非常欣赏歌德的作品，并试图招募更多艺术家加入他那略显沉闷的宫廷。然而，对歌德来说，这却是他等待的机会。他可以告别文坛，全身心投入魏玛。他可以全身心投入政治和科学，驯服内心那该死的恶魔。他接受了邀请，除了后来一次去意大利之外，他的余生都在魏玛度过。

In Weimar Goethe had the idea of trying to modernize the local government, but he quickly realized that the duke was weak and undisciplined and that any attempt at reforming the duchy was doomed. There was too much corruption. And so slowly he poured his energies into his new passion in life, the sciences. He focused on geology, botany, and anatomy. His years of writing poetry and novels were over. He began to collect a large amount of stones, plants, and bones that he could study in his house at all hours. And as he looked deeply into these sciences, he began to see strange connections between them. In geology, changes in the earth occur with great slowness, over immensely long periods of time, too slowly to be observed in the span of a single lifetime. Plants are in a continual state of metamorphosis, from the most primitive beginnings of the seed to the flower or tree. All life on the planet is in an ever-present state of development, one life form growing out of another. He began to entertain the radical idea that humans themselves evolved from primitive life forms—that was the way, after all, of nature.

在魏玛共和国，歌德曾试图推动地方政府的现代化，但他很快意识到公爵软弱无能，任何改革公国的尝试都注定要失败。腐败现象猖獗。于是，他慢慢地将精力投入到他人生的新热情——科学领域。他专注于地质学、植物学和解剖学。他写诗写小说的岁月结束了。他开始收集大量的石头、植物和骨头，以便随时在家中研究。随着他深入研究这些科学，他开始发现它们之间奇特的联系。地质学认为，地球的变化发生得非常缓慢，持续的时间非常长，慢到在人的一生中无法观察到。植物处于不断的变态阶段，从最原始的种子到花朵或树木。地球上所有的生命都处于一种持续不断的发展状态，一种生命形式由另一种生命形式发展而来。他开始接受一个激进的观点：人类本身就是从原始生命形式进化而来的——毕竟，这是自然规律。

One of the main arguments of the time against such evolutionary theory was the nonexistence of the intermaxillary bone in humans. It exists in all lower animals in the jaw, including primates, but at the time could not be found in the human skull. This was paraded as evidence that man is separate and created by a divine force. Based on his idea that all of nature is interconnected, Goethe could not accept such a hypothesis, and through much research he discovered remnants of the intermaxillary bone in the upper cheekbones of human infants, the ultimate indication of our connection to all other life forms.

当时反对这种进化论的主要论点之一是人类不存在颌间骨。所有低等动物的颌骨中都存在颌间骨，包括灵长类动物，但在当时人类的头骨中却找不到。这被吹捧为人类独立存在、由神力创造的证据。基于他所有自然界万物相互联系的理念，歌德无法接受这种假设，并通过大量研究，在人类婴儿的上颧骨中发现了颌间骨的残留，这最终证明了我们与所有其他生命形式之间存在着联系。

His style of science was unconventional for the time. He had the idea that there existed a form of archetypal plant that could be deduced from the shape and development of all plants. In his study of bones, he liked to compare all life forms to see whether there were similarities in the construction of parts such as the vertebral column. He was obsessed with the connections between life forms, the result of his Faustian desire to get at the essence of all life. He felt that phenomena in nature contained the theory of their essence in their own structure, if we could only grasp it with our senses and our minds. Almost all scientists at the time ridiculed his work, but in the decades to follow it was recognized that he had developed perhaps the first real concept of evolution, and his other work was the precursor to such later sciences as morphology and comparative anatomy.

他的科学风格在当时颇具突破性。他认为存在一种原型植物，可以通过所有植物的形状和发育推断出来。在骨骼研究中，他喜欢比较所有生命形式，以探究其结构（例如脊柱）是否存在相似之处。他痴迷于生命形式之间的联系，这源于他浮士德式的渴望，即探寻所有生命本质。他认为，如果我们能够运用感官和思维去理解，自然现象在其自身结构中就蕴含着其本质的理论。当时几乎所有科学家都嘲笑他的工作，但在随后的几十年里，人们认识到他或许是第一个真正意义上的进化论概念，而他的其他工作则是形态学和比较解剖学等后期学科的先驱。

In Weimar, Goethe was a changed man—a sober scientist and thinker. But in 1801 another bout of illness came close to killing him yet again. It took years to recover, but by 1805 he felt his strength returning, and with it a return to sensations he had not experienced since his youth. That year initiated one of the strangest and most amazing periods of productivity in the history of the human mind, stretching from his midfifties to his late sixties. The daemon he had repressed for several decades broke loose once more, but now he had the discipline to channel it into all kinds of work. Poems, novels, and plays came pouring out of him. He took up Faust again, writing most of it in this period. His day was an almost insane medley of different studies—writing in the morning, experiments and scientific observations (which were now expanded to chemistry and meteorology) in the afternoon, discussions with friends about aesthetics, science, and politics in the evening. He seemed to be tireless, and to be going through a second youth.

在魏玛共和国，歌德已然脱胎换骨——一位冷静的科学家和思想家。然而，1801年，他再次病倒，险些再次夺去他的生命。他花了数年时间才康复，但到了1805年，他感觉体力逐渐恢复，并恢复了自年轻以来从未体验过的感觉。这一年，歌德开启了人类思想史上最奇特、最令人惊叹的创作时期之一，从五十五岁一直延续到六十几岁。他压抑了数十年的“恶魔”再次爆发，但现在他已经能够自律地将其引导到各种创作中。诗歌、小说和戏剧如泉涌般涌现。他重拾《浮士德》，大部分作品都创作于这一时期。他的一天几乎是各种学习的疯狂组合——上午写作，下午进行实验和科学观察（如今已扩展到化学和气象学），晚上则与朋友讨论美学、科学和政治。他似乎不知疲倦，正在经历第二次青春。

Goethe had now come to the conclusion that all forms of human knowledge are manifestations of the same life force he had intuited in his near-death experience as a young man. The problem with most people, he felt, is that they build artificial walls around subjects and ideas. The real thinker sees the connections, grasps the essence of the life force operating in every individual instance. Why should any individual stop at poetry, or find art unrelated to science, or narrow his or her intellectual interests? The mind was designed to connect things, like a loom that knits together all of the threads of a fabric. If life exists as an organic whole and cannot be separated into parts without losing a sense of the whole, then thinking should make itself equal to the whole.

歌德如今得出结论：所有形式的人类知识都体现着他年轻时在濒死体验中直觉到的同一种生命力。他认为，大多数人的问题在于，他们在各个主题和思想周围筑起了人为的壁垒。真正的思想家能够洞察其中的联系，把握生命力在每一个个体中运作的本质。为什么有人应该止步于诗歌，或者去寻找与科学无关的艺术，或者缩小自己的知识兴趣？心智的设计就是为了连接事物，就像织布机将布料上的所有线都编织在一起一样。如果生命作为一个有机整体存在，并且无法被分割成各个部分而不失去整体感，那么思考就应该使自己与整体相等。

Friends and acquaintances noticed a strange phenomenon in this twilight period of Goethe’s life—he loved to talk about the future, decades and centuries ahead. In his Weimar years he had added to his studies, reading many books on economics, history, and political science. Gaining new insights from these readings and adding to them his own reasoning, he loved to predict the tide of historical events, and those who witnessed these predictions were later shocked at his prescience. Years before the French Revolution he had predicted the fall of the Bourbon monarchy, intuiting that it had lost its legitimacy in the eyes of the people. Participating on the German side in battles to overturn the French Revolution, and witnessing the victory of the French civilian army at the battle of Valmy, he exclaimed, “Here and now begins a new historical era; and you can all say you have seen it.” He meant the coming era of democracies and civilian armies.

歌德晚年时，朋友和熟人注意到一个奇怪的现象——他喜欢谈论未来，谈论几十年甚至几百年后的事情。魏玛共和国时期，他深入研究，阅读了大量经济学、历史学和政治学著作。他从这些著作中汲取新的见解，并融入自己的逻辑，喜欢预测历史事件的走向。那些见证过这些预言的人，后来都对他的先见之明感到震惊。早在法国大革命爆发前，他就预言了波旁王朝的覆灭，直觉地认为它在民众眼中已经失去了合法性。在与德军一起参与推翻法国大革命的战斗，并目睹法国平民军队在瓦尔米战役中取得胜利后，他感叹道：“一个新的历史时代就此开启；你们都可以说，你们已经见证了它。” 他指的是即将到来的民主和平民军队时代。

Now in his seventies, he would tell people that petty nationalism was a dying force and that one day Europe would form a union like the United States, a development he welcomed. He talked excitedly of the United States itself, predicting that it would some day be the great power in the world, its borders slowly expanding to fill the continent. He discussed his belief that a new science of telegraphy would connect the globe, and that people would have access to the latest news by the hour. He called this future “the velocipedic age,” one determined by speed. He was concerned that it could lead to a deadening of the human spirit.

他已年逾古稀，却仍会告诉人们，狭隘的民族主义正在消亡，终有一天欧洲会像美国一样形成一个联盟，他对此表示欢迎。他兴奋地谈论美国本身，预言它终有一天会成为世界强国，其疆域将缓慢扩张，覆盖整个大陆。他坚信，一种新的电报技术将连接全球，人们将能够随时获取最新资讯。他将这个未来称为“自行车时代”，一个由速度决定的时代。他担心这会导致人类精神的麻木。

Finally, at the age of eighty-two, he could sense that the end was near, even though his mind was sparking with more ideas than ever before. He said to a friend that it was a shame that he could not live another eighty years—what new discoveries he could make, with all of his accumulated experience! He had been postponing it for years, but now it was time to finally write the ending to Faust itself: the scholar would find a moment of happiness, the devil would take his soul, but divine forces would forgive Faust for his great intellectual ambition, for his relentless quest for knowledge, and would save him from hell—perhaps Goethe’s own judgment on himself.

最终，在八十二岁高龄之际，他感到人生的终点已近，尽管他的脑海里迸发出的想法比以往任何时候都多。他对一位朋友说，很遗憾自己不能再活八十年——凭借他积累的经验，他还能做出多少新发现！他多年来一直拖延着这一刻，但现在终于到了为《浮士德》写结局的时候了：这位学者会找到片刻的幸福，魔鬼会夺走他的灵魂，但神力会原谅浮士德伟大的求知抱负，原谅他对知识的不懈追求，并将他从地狱中拯救出来——这或许是歌德对自己的评判。

A few months later, he wrote his friend, the great linguist and educator Wilhelm von Humboldt, the following: “The human organs, by means of practice, training, reflection, success or failure, furtherance or resistance…learn to make the necessary connections unconsciously, the acquired and the intuitive working hand-in-hand, so that a unison results which is the world’s wonder…The world is ruled by bewildered theories of bewildering operations; and nothing is to me more important than, so far as is possible, to turn to the best account what is in me and persists in me, and keep a firm hand upon my idiosyncrasies.” These would be the last words he would write. Within a few days he was dead, at the age of eighty-three.

几个月后，他给他的好友、伟大的语言学家和教育家威廉·冯·洪堡写信如下：“人体器官通过实践、训练、反思、成功或失败、发展或抵抗……学会在无意识中建立必要的联系，后天习得的和直觉的携手并进，从而产生一种令世界惊叹的和谐……世界被各种令人眼花缭乱的理论和运作所统治；对我来说，没有什么比尽可能地充分利用我身上存在的和持续存在的东西，并牢牢控制我的特质更重要了。” 这将成为他留下的最后话语。几天后，他去世了，享年八十三岁。

For Goethe, a turning point came in his life with the great success of The Sorrows of Young Werther . He could not help but be dazzled by his sudden fame. The people around him were clamoring for an encore. He was only twenty-five at the time. For the rest of his life he would deny the public such an encore, and none of his subsequent writings would approach the success of Werther , although in his last years he was recognized as Germany’s great genius. To deny the public what it wanted was an act of tremendous courage. To decline to exploit such fame would mean that it would probably never return. He would have to give up all of that attention. But Goethe felt something within him that was much stronger than the lure of fame. He did not want to be imprisoned by this one book, devoting his life to literature and creating a sensation. And so he chose his own unique and strange path in life, guided by an inner force that he called his daemon—a spirit of restlessness that impelled him to explore beyond literature, to the core of life itself. All that was necessary was to master and channel this spirit, implanted in him at birth.

对歌德来说，《少年维特的烦恼》的巨大成功是他人生的转折点。他不禁为突如其来的名声而目眩神迷。周围的人都吵着要他再来一次。当时他只有二十五岁。在他的余生中，他一直拒绝让公众再次看到他的作品，尽管在他晚年被公认为德国最伟大的天才，但他后来的作品也无一能与《少年维特的烦恼》相比。拒绝公众所渴望的东西需要极大的勇气。拒绝利用这样的名声，意味着它可能永远不会再回来。他将不得不放弃所有这些关注。但歌德内心深处有一种比名声的诱惑更强烈的感觉。他不想被这本书束缚，不想将自己的一生奉献给文学，创造轰动效应。于是，他选择了一条独特而奇特的人生之路，由一种他称之为“守护神”的内在力量指引——一种躁动不安的精神，驱使他探索文学之外的领域，直抵生命本身的内核。他所需要的，只是掌握并引导这股与生俱来的精神。

In the sciences, he followed his unique path, looking for deep patterns in nature. He extended his studies to politics, economics and history. Returning to literature in the last phase of his life, his head now teemed with links between all forms of knowledge. His poetry, novels, and plays were suffused with science, and his scientific investigations were suffused with poetic intuitions. His insights into history were uncanny. His mastery was not over this subject or that one, but in the connections between them, based on decades of deep observation and thinking. Goethe epitomizes what was known in the Renaissance as the Ideal of the Universal Man—a person so steeped in all forms of knowledge that his mind grows closer to the reality of nature itself and sees secrets that are invisible to most people.

在科学领域，他走上了他独特的道路，探寻自然的深层规律。他将研究范围拓展至政治、经济和历史。晚年回归文学，他的头脑中充满了各种知识之间的联系。他的诗歌、小说和戏剧都洋溢着科学的气息，他的科学研究也洋溢着诗意的直觉。他对历史的洞见令人叹为观止。他的精通之处不在于对某个学科的掌握，而在于它们之间的联系，这种联系建立在数十年深入观察和思考的基础上。歌德是文艺复兴时期“全能者”的典范——博览群书，使他的思想更加贴近自然本身，并洞悉大多数人无法触及的秘密。

Today some might see a person such as Goethe as a quaint relic of the eighteenth century, and his ideal of unifying knowledge as a Romantic dream, but in fact the opposite is the case, and for one simple reason: the design of the human brain—its inherent need to make connections and associations—gives it a will of its own. Although this evolution might take various twists and turns in history, the desire to connect will win out in the end because it is so powerfully a part of our nature and inclination. Aspects of technology now offer unprecedented means to build connections between fields and ideas. The artificial barriers between the arts and the sciences will melt away under the pressure to know and to express our common reality. Our ideas will become closer to nature, more alive and organic. In any way possible, you should strive to be a part of this universalizing process, extending your own knowledge to other branches, further and further out. The rich ideas that will come from such a quest will be their own reward.

如今，有些人或许会将像歌德这样的人视为十八世纪的古怪遗物，将他统一知识的理想视为浪漫主义的梦想，但事实恰恰相反，原因很简单：人类大脑的设计——其与生俱来的建立联系和联想的需求——赋予了它自身的意志。尽管这种进化在历史上可能经历各种曲折，但渴望联系的愿望最终将胜出，因为它是我们天性和倾向中如此强大的一部分。如今，科技的各个方面提供了前所未有的手段来在各个领域和思想之间建立联系。在了解和表达我们共同现实的压力下，艺术与科学之间的人为障碍将会消融。我们的思想将更加贴近自然，更加鲜活、更加有机。你应该尽一切可能，努力成为这一普遍化进程的一部分，将你的知识扩展到其他领域，并不断拓展。这种探索所带来的丰富思想本身就是回报。

REVERSAL

逆转

The reversal to mastery is to deny its existence or its importance, and therefore the need to strive for it in any way. But such a reversal can only lead to feelings of powerlessness and disappointment. This reversal leads to enslavement to what we shall call the false self .

逆转掌控欲，就是否定掌控欲的存在及其重要性，从而否定以任何方式努力追求掌控欲的必要性。但这种逆转只会导致无力感和失望。这种逆转会导致被我们称之为“虚假自我”的奴役。

Your false self is the accumulation of all the voices you have internalized from other people—parents and friends who want you to conform to their ideas of what you should be like and what you should do, as well as societal pressures to adhere to certain values that can easily seduce you. It also includes the voice of your own ego, which constantly tries to protect you from unflattering truths. This self talks to you in clear words, and when it comes to mastery, it says things like, “Mastery is for the geniuses, the exceptionally talented, the freaks of nature. I was simply not born that way.” Or it says, “Mastery is ugly and immoral. It is for those who are ambitious and egotistical. Better to accept my lot in life and to work to help other people instead of enriching myself.” Or it might say, “Success is all luck. Those we call Masters are only people who were at the right place at the right time. I could easily be in their place if I had a lucky break.” Or it might also say, “To work for so long at something that requires so much pain and effort, why bother? Better to enjoy my short life and do what I can to get by.”

你的虚假自我是你内化了的来自他人的声音的累积——父母朋友希望你遵从他们关于你应该是什么样的人、你应该做什么的想法，以及社会压力，要求你坚持某些很容易诱惑你的价值观。它也包括你自我意识的声音，它不断试图保护你免受不讨人喜欢的真相的伤害。这个自我用清晰的语言与你对话，当谈到精通时，它会说：“精通是天才、才华横溢的人、怪胎的专属。我并非生来如此。”或者它会说：“精通是丑陋且不道德的。它只属于那些雄心勃勃、自负的人。与其让自己致富，不如接受我的命运，努力帮助他人。”或者它会说：“成功全靠运气。我们所谓的大师，只不过是在正确的时间出现在正确地点的人而已。如果我运气好，我也能轻易取代他们。”或者它可能会说：“花这么长时间去做一件需要付出这么多痛苦和努力的事情，何必呢？不如享受我短暂的人生，尽我所能去度过。”

As you must know by now, these voices do not speak the truth. Mastery is not a question of genetics or luck, but of following your natural inclinations and the deep desire that stirs you from within. Everyone has such inclinations. This desire within you is not motivated by egotism or sheer ambition for power, both of which are emotions that get in the way of mastery. It is instead a deep expression of something natural, something that marked you at birth as unique. In following your inclinations and moving toward mastery, you make a great contribution to society, enriching it with discoveries and insights, and making the most of the diversity in nature and among human society. It is in fact the height of selfishness to merely consume what others create and to retreat into a shell of limited goals and immediate pleasures. Alienating yourself from your inclinations can only lead to pain and disappointment in the long run, and a sense that you have wasted something unique. This pain will be expressed in bitterness and envy, and you will not recognize the true source of your depression.

你现在肯定已经明白，这些声音并非真理。成就卓越并非基因或运气的问题，而是追随你与生俱来的倾向和内心深处的渴望。每个人都有这样的倾向。你内心的渴望并非出于自私自利或纯粹的权力野心，这两种情绪都会阻碍你成就卓越。相反，它是某种自然特质的深层表达，某种你与生俱来的独特特质。追随你的倾向，迈向卓越，你将为社会做出巨大贡献，用发现和洞见丰富社会，并充分利用自然界和人类社会的多样性。事实上，仅仅消费他人创造的东西，退缩到狭隘的目标和眼前的享乐的壳里，才是自私的极致。疏远你的倾向，最终只会导致痛苦和失望，以及一种你浪费了独一无二的东西的感觉。这种痛苦会以苦涩和嫉妒的形式表现出来，而你将无法认识到你抑郁的真正根源。

Your true self does not speak in words or banal phrases. Its voice comes from deep within you, from the substrata of your psyche, from something embedded physically within you. It emanates from your uniqueness, and it communicates through sensations and powerful desires that seem to transcend you. You cannot ultimately understand why you are drawn to certain activities or forms of knowledge. This cannot really be verbalized or explained. It is simply a fact of nature. In following this voice you realize your own potential, and satisfy your deepest longings to create and express your uniqueness. It exists for a purpose, and it is your Life’s Task to bring it to fruition.

你真正的自我并非用言语或陈词滥调来表达。它的声音源自你的内心深处，源自你心灵的底层，源自你内在某种物质层面的根基。它源于你的独特性，并通过那些似乎超越你自身的感觉和强烈的渴望进行交流。你无法最终理解为何你会被某些活动或知识形式所吸引。这无法用言语表达或解释。这只是一个自然规律。追随这声音，你便能意识到自身的潜能，并满足你内心深处对创造和表达自身独特性的渴望。它的存在是为了一个目的，而你的人生任务就是将其付诸实践。

Because we think well of ourselves, but nonetheless never suppose ourselves capable of producing a painting like one of Raphael’s or a dramatic scene like one of Shakespeare’s, we convince ourselves that the capacity to do so is quite extraordinarily marvelous, a wholly uncommon accident, or, if we are still religiously inclined, a mercy from on high. Thus our vanity, our self-love, promotes the cult of the genius: for only if we think of him as being very remote from us, as a miraculum, does he not aggrieve us…. But, aside from these suggestions of our vanity, the activity of the genius seems in no way fundamentally different from the activity of the inventor of machines, the scholar of astronomy or history, the master of tactics. All these activities are explicable if one pictures to oneself people whose thinking is active in one direction, who employ everything as material, who always zealously observe their own inner life and that of others, who perceive everywhere models and incentives, who never tire of combining together the means available to them. Genius too does nothing but learn first how to lay bricks then how to build, and continually seek for material and continually form itself around it. Every activity of man is amazingly complicated, not only that of the genius: but none is a ‘miracle.’

因为我们自视甚高，却从未想过自己能够创作出像拉斐尔那样的画作，或像莎士比亚那样的戏剧场景，于是我们便会说服自己，拥有这样的能力非同凡响，纯属偶然，或者，如果我们仍然怀有宗教信仰，则是上天的恩赐。因此，我们的虚荣心，我们的自爱，助长了对天才的崇拜：因为只有当我们把他视为离我们很远、像个奇迹一样时，他才不会让我们感到委屈……但是，抛开这些虚荣心的暗示，天才的活动似乎与机器发明者、天文学家或历史学家、战术大师的活动并无根本区别。如果我们想象这样的人，他们的思维活跃于一个方向，他们把一切都当作素材，他们总是热切地观察自己和他人的内心世界，他们处处都能看到榜样和激励，他们不知疲倦地将他们所能利用的手段结合起来，所有这些活动都是可以解释的。天才也不过是先学会砌砖，再学会建造，不断寻找素材，并以此为基础不断塑造自身。人类的每一项活动都极其复杂，天才的才华更是如此：但凡事都不能称之为“奇迹”。

—F RIEDRICH N IETZSCHE

—弗里德里希·尼采

# ↩

CONTEMPORARY
当代
MASTER BIOGRAPHIES
大师传记

Santiago Calatrava was born in 1951, in Valencia, Spain. He earned his architecture degree from the Polytechnic University of Valencia, and then went on to obtain a PhD in civil engineering from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, in Zurich, Switzerland. Because of his civil engineering background, Calatrava has focused primarily on large-scale public projects such as bridges, train stations, museums, cultural centers, and sports complexes. Inspired by organic shapes in nature, Calatrava has sought to infuse these public projects with a mythic, yet futuristic quality, featuring parts of buildings that move and change shape. Among his notable designs are BCE Place Galleria in Toronto, Canada (1992), Oriente Railway Station in Lisbon, Portugal (1998), the extension to the Milwaukee Art Museum (2001), the Puente de la Mujer in Buenos Aires, Argentina (2001), Auditorio de Tenerife in Santa Cruz, the Canary Islands (2003), the Athens Olympic Sports Complex (2004), the Turning Torso Tower in Malmo, Sweden (2005), and the Light Railway Bridge in Jerusalem, Israel (2008). He is currently designing the Transportation Hub at the World Trade Center in New York City, expected to open in 2014. Calatrava is also a renowned sculptor whose work has been shown in galleries all around the world. Among his numerous awards, he has received the Gold Medal from the Institution of Structural Engineers (1992) and the Gold Medal from the American Institute of Architects (2005).

圣地亚哥·卡拉特拉瓦于1951年出生于西班牙瓦伦西亚。他毕业于瓦伦西亚理工大学，获得建筑学学位，后又在瑞士苏黎世联邦理工学院获得土木工程博士学位。凭借其土木工程背景，卡拉特拉瓦主要专注于大型公共项目，例如桥梁、火车站、博物馆、文化中心和体育中心。受自然界有机形态的启发，卡拉特拉瓦力求为这些公共项目注入一种神秘而又充满未来感的特质，并赋予建筑中可移动和变形的部件。他的著名设计包括加拿大多伦多的 BCE Place Galleria（1992 年）、葡萄牙里斯本的东方火车站（1998 年）、密尔沃基艺术博物馆扩建项目（2001 年）、阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯的女人桥（2001 年）、加那利群岛圣克鲁斯的特内里费礼堂（2003 年）、雅典奥林匹克体育中心（2004 年）、瑞典马尔默的旋转塔（2005 年）和以色列耶路撒冷轻轨桥（2008 年）。他目前正在设计纽约世界贸易中心的交通枢纽，预计 2014 年开放。卡拉特拉瓦也是一位著名的雕塑家，其作品曾在世界各地的画廊展出。他获得过无数奖项，其中包括美国结构工程师学会金奖（1992 年）和美国建筑师学会金奖（2005 年）。

Daniel Everett was born in 1951, in Holtville, California. He received a degree in foreign missions from the Moody Bible Institute of Chicago, and became an ordained minister. After studying linguistics at the Summer Institute of Languages, a Christian organization, Everett and his family were sent as missionaries to the Amazon basin, to live with a small group of hunter and gatherers known as the Pirahã, whose language is not related to any other living dialect. After spending many years among the Pirahã, Everett was finally able to crack the code of their seemingly indecipherable language, and in the process made some discoveries about the nature of human language that continue to stir controversy in linguistics. He has also conducted research, and published articles, on more than a dozen distinct Amazonian languages. Everett has a PhD in linguistics from the State University of Campinas in Brazil. He served as professor of Linguistics and Anthropology at the University of Pittsburgh, where he was also chairman of the Department of Linguistics. He has also taught at the University of Manchester (England) and Illinois State University. Everett is currently the dean of Arts and Sciences at Bentley University. He has published two books: the best-selling Don’t Sleep, There are Snakes: Life and Language in the Amazonian Jungle (2008), and Language: The Cultural Tool (2012). His work with the Pirahã is the subject of a documentary, The Grammar of Happiness (2012).

丹尼尔·埃弗里特于 1951 年出生于加利福尼亚州霍尔特维尔。他获得了芝加哥慕迪圣经学院的外国传教学位，并成为一名被任命的牧师。在基督教组织夏季语言学院学习语言学之后，埃弗里特和他的家人被派往亚马逊河流域作为传教士，与一小群被称为皮拉罕人的狩猎采集者一起生活，他们的语言与其他任何现存方言都没有关联。在皮拉罕人中生活多年后，埃弗里特终于破解了他们看似难以理解的语言密码，并在此过程中对人类语言的本质做出了一些发现，这些发现至今仍在语言学界引发争议。他还对十几种不同的亚马逊语言进行了研究并发表过论文。埃弗里特拥有巴西坎皮纳斯州立大学的语言学博士学位。他曾任匹兹堡大学语言学和人类学教授，并担任该校语言学系主任。他还曾在英国曼彻斯特大学和伊利诺伊州立大学任教。埃弗里特目前担任本特利大学文理学院院长。他出版了两本著作：畅销书《别睡觉，有蛇：亚马逊丛林中的生活与语言》（2008年）和《语言：文化工具》（2012年）。他与皮拉罕人的研究成果被拍摄成纪录片《幸福的语法》（2012年）。

Teresita Fernández was born in 1968, in Miami, Florida. She received a BFA from Florida International University, and her MFA from Virginia Commonwealth University. Fernández is a conceptual artist who is best known for her public sculptures and for her large-scale pieces in unconventional materials. In her work she likes to explore how psychology impacts our perception of the world around us; for this purpose, she creates immersive environments that challenge our conventional views of art and nature. Her work has been exhibited in prominent museums around the world, including the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, and the Corcoran Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C. Her large-scale commissions include a recent site-specific work titled Blind Blue Landscape at the renowned Bennesee Art site in Naoshima, Japan. Fernández has received numerous awards, including a Guggenheim Fellowship, an American Academy in Rome Affiliated Fellowship, and a National Endowment for the Arts Artist’s Grant. In 2005 she was awarded a MacArthur Foundation Fellowship, also known as the “genius grant.” In 2011 President Barack Obama appointed Fernández to serve on the U.S. Commission on Fine Arts.

特雷西塔·费尔南德斯于1968年出生于佛罗里达州迈阿密。她先后在佛罗里达国际大学和弗吉尼亚联邦大学获得美术学士学位和硕士学位。费尔南德斯是一位概念艺术家，以其公共雕塑和运用非传统材料创作的大型作品而闻名。她喜欢在作品中探索心理学如何影响我们对周围世界的感知；为此，她创造了沉浸式环境，挑战我们对艺术和自然的传统看法。她的作品曾在世界各地著名博物馆展出，包括纽约现代艺术博物馆、旧金山现代艺术博物馆和华盛顿特区科科伦美术馆。她近期的大型委托创作包括在日本直岛著名的本尼西艺术中心创作的场域特定作品《盲蓝风景》。费尔南德斯曾荣获众多奖项，包括古根海姆奖学金、罗马美国学院附属奖学金以及美国国家艺术基金会艺术家奖。 2005 年，她荣获麦克阿瑟基金会奖学金，该奖项也被称为“天才奖”。2011 年，美国总统巴拉克·奥巴马任命费尔南德斯为美国美术委员会委员。

Paul Graham was born in 1964, in Weymouth, England. His family moved to the United States when he was four, and he was raised in Monroeville, Pennsylvania. Graham obtained a BA in philosophy from Cornell University, and a PhD in computer science from Harvard University. He studied painting at the Rhode Island School of Design and the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence, Italy. In 1995 he cofounded Viaweb, the first application service provider that allowed users to set up their own Internet stores. After Yahoo! acquired Viaweb for close to $50 million (and renamed it Yahoo! Store), Graham went on to write a highly popular series of online essays about programming, tech startups, the history of technology, and art. Inspired by the reaction to a talk he gave at the Harvard Computer Society in 2005, Graham created Y Combinator, an apprenticeship system that provides seed funding, advice, and mentorship to young tech entrepreneurs. It has since become one of the most successful tech incubators in the world. Its portfolio of over two hundred companies is currently worth more than $4 billion, and includes DropBox, Reddit, loopt, and AirBnB. He has published two books: On Lisp (1993) about the computer programming language, and Hackers and Painters (2004). His online essays can be viewed at PaulGraham.com.

保罗·格雷厄姆于1964年出生于英国韦茅斯。他四岁时随家人移居美国，并在宾夕法尼亚州门罗维尔长大。格雷厄姆在康奈尔大学获得哲学学士学位，在哈佛大学获得计算机科学博士学位。他曾在罗德岛设计学院和意大利佛罗伦萨美术学院学习绘画。1995年，他与他人共同创立了Viaweb，这是第一家允许用户创建个人网络商店的应用服务提供商。在雅虎以近5000万美元收购Viaweb（并将其更名为雅虎商店）后，格雷厄姆撰写了一系列广受欢迎的网络文章，内容涵盖编程、科技初创企业、科技史和艺术。受2005年在哈佛计算机学会发表演讲的反响启发，格雷厄姆创建了Y Combinator，这是一个学徒制系统，为年轻的科技创业者提供种子资金、建议和指导。如今，Y Combinator已成为全球最成功的科技孵化器之一。该公司投资组合涵盖超过两百家公司，目前市值超过40亿美元，其中包括DropBox、Reddit、loopt和Airbnb。他出版了两本著作：关于计算机编程语言的《论Lisp》（1993年）和《黑客与画家》（2004年）。他的在线文章可在PaulGraham.com上阅读。

Temple Grandin was born in 1947, in Boston, Massachusetts. At the age of three she was diagnosed with autism. Through special mentoring and work with a speech therapist, she slowly mastered the language skills that allowed her to develop intellectually and to attend various schools, including a high school for gifted children, where she excelled in science. Grandin went on to receive a bachelor’s degree in psychology from Franklin Pierce College, a master’s degree in animal science from Arizona State University, and a doctorate in animal science from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. After graduation, she worked as a designer of livestock-handling facilities. Half the cattle in the United States are handled by equipment she has designed. Her work in this area is devoted to making more humane, stress-free environments for animals in slaughterhouses. For this purpose, she has created a series of guidelines for handling cattle and pigs at meat plants that are now used by companies such as McDonald’s. Grandin has become a popular lecturer on animal rights and on autism. She has written several best-selling books, including Thinking in Pictures: My Life with Autism (1996), Animals in Translation: Using the Mysteries of Autism to Decode Animal Behavior (2005), and The Way I See It: A Personal Look at Autism and Aspergers (2009). In 2010 she was the subject of an HBO biopic about her life, titled Temple Grandin . She is currently a professor of animal science at Colorado State University.

坦普·格兰丁于1947年出生于马萨诸塞州波士顿。三岁时，她被诊断患有自闭症。在特殊指导和语言治疗师的指导下，她逐渐掌握了语言技能，这使她能够发展智力并进入不同的学校学习，其中包括一所天才儿童高中，她在学校的科学成绩优异。格兰丁后来获得了富兰克林·皮尔斯学院的心理学学士学位、亚利桑那州立大学的动物科学硕士学位和伊利诺伊大学香槟分校的动物科学博士学位。毕业后，她担任牲畜处理设施设计师。美国一半的牛是由她设计的设备处理的。她在这方面的工作致力于为屠宰场的动物创造更人性化、更轻松的环境。为此，她制定了一系列肉类加工厂处理牛和猪的指南，这些指南目前已被麦当劳等公司采用。格兰丁已成为一位广受欢迎的动物权利和自闭症讲师。她撰写过多本畅销书，包括《图像思维：我的自闭症人生》（1996年）、《动物翻译：用自闭症的奥秘解读动物行为》（2005年）以及《我的看法：个人视角下的自闭症和阿斯伯格症》（2009年）。2010年，HBO以她为主角拍摄了一部传记电影，名为《坦普·格兰丁》。她目前是科罗拉多州立大学的动物科学教授。

Yoky Matsuoka was born in 1972, in Tokyo, Japan. As a promising young tennis player, Matsuoka came to the United States to attend a high-level tennis academy. She ended up staying, completing her high school studies in the States, and then attending the University of California at Berkeley, where she received a BS in electrical engineering and computer science. She received her PhD in electrical engineering and artificial intelligence from MIT. While at MIT she was the chief engineer at Barrett Technology, where she developed a robotic hand that became an industry standard. She has served as a professor of robotics and mechanical engineering at Carnegie Mellon University and professor of computer science and engineering at the University of Washington at Seattle. At the University of Washington, Matsuoka created a new field, which she called “neurobotics,” and established the university’s neurobotics laboratory, where robotic models and virtual environments are used to understand the biomechanics and neuromuscular control of human limbs. In 2007, Matsuoka was awarded a MacArthur Foundation Fellowship, or “genius grant.” She was a cofounder of Google’s X division, where she served as Head of Innovation. Matsuoka is currently the vice president of technology at Nest Labs, a green technology firm that develops energy-efficient consumer products such as the Nest Learning Thermostat.

松冈洋基（Yoky Matsuoka）1972年出生于日本东京。作为一名前途无量的年轻网球运动员，松冈洋基来到美国，就读于一所高水平的网球学院。她最终留在了美国，在美国完成了高中学业，之后进入加州大学伯克利分校学习，并获得了电气工程和计算机科学学士学位。之后，她在麻省理工学院获得了电气工程和人工智能博士学位。在麻省理工学院期间，她担任巴雷特技术公司的首席工程师，并在那里开发了一款成为行业标准的机械手。她曾担任卡内基梅隆大学的机器人和机械工程教授，以及华盛顿大学西雅图分校的计算机科学与工程教授。在华盛顿大学，松冈洋基开创了一个名为“神经机器人学”的新领域，并建立了该校的神经机器人学实验室，利用机器人模型和虚拟环境来理解人体肢体的生物力学和神经肌肉控制。2007年，松冈洋基荣获麦克阿瑟基金会奖学金，又称“天才奖”。她曾是谷歌X部门的联合创始人，并担任创新主管。松冈目前担任Nest Labs的技术副总裁，这是一家绿色科技公司，致力于开发节能消费产品，例如Nest Learning Thermostat。

Vilayanur S. Ramachandran was born in 1951, in Madras, India. He trained as a doctor, then switched fields to study visual psychology at Trinity College at the University of Cambridge in England, where he received his PhD. In 1983 he was appointed assistant professor of psychology at the University of California at San Diego (UCSD). He is currently a Distinguished Professor in the Psychology Department and Neurosciences Program at UCSD, and also serves as the director of the university’s Center for Brain and Cognition. He is best known for his work on bizarre neurological syndromes such as phantom limbs, various body-identity disorders, Capgras delusion (in which the sufferer believes that family members have been replaced by impostors), and for his theories on mirror neurons and synesthesia. Among his numerous awards, he has been elected to an honorary life membership to the Royal Institution of Great Britain, fellowships from Oxford University and Stanford University, and the annual Ramon Y Cajal award from the International Neuropsychiatry Society. In 2011 Time magazine listed him as “one of the most influential people in the world.” He is the author of the best-selling Phantoms in the Brain (1998), as well as A Brief Tour of Human Consciousness: From Impostor Poodles to Purple Numbers (2005), and The Tell-Tale Brain: A Neuroscientist’s Quest for What Makes Us Human (2010).

维拉亚努尔·S·拉马钱德兰1951年出生于印度马德拉斯。他曾接受过医学培训，后转入英国剑桥大学三一学院学习视觉心理学，并于该校获得博士学位。1983年，他被任命为加州大学圣地亚哥分校（UCSD）心理学助理教授。他目前是加州大学圣地亚哥分校心理学系和神经科学项目的杰出教授，并担任该校大脑与认知研究中心主任。他最为人熟知的研究领域包括幻肢、各种身体认同障碍、卡普格拉妄想症（患者认为家人被冒名顶替者取代），以及镜像神经元和联觉理论。他荣获众多奖项，包括英国皇家学会终身荣誉会员、牛津大学和斯坦福大学院士，以及国际神经精神病学学会年度拉蒙·Y·卡哈尔奖。2011年，《时代》杂志将他评为“全球最具影响力人物之一”。他是畅销书《大脑中的幽灵》（1998年）、《人类意识简史：从冒名顶替的贵宾犬到紫色数字》（2005年）和《泄密的大脑：一位神经科学家探寻人类之本》（2010年）的作者。

Freddie Roach was born in 1960, in Dedham, Massachusetts. He began training as a boxer at the age of six. By the time he turned professional in 1978, Roach had fought 150 amateur bouts. Training under the legendary Eddie Futch, as a professional Roach compiled a record of 41 wins (17 by knockout) and 13 losses. After retiring as a fighter in 1986, Roach apprenticed as a trainer under Futch, then started his own career several years later, opening in 1995 his Wild Card Boxing Club in Hollywood, California, where he now trains his stable of fighters. As a trainer Roach has worked with 28 world champion boxers including Manny Pacquiao, Mike Tyson, Oscar De La Hoya, Amir Khan, Julio César Chávez Jr., James Toney, and Virgil Hill. He is also the coach of UFC Welterweight Champion Georges St. Pierre, and one of the top female boxers in the world, Lucia Rijker. In 1990 Roach was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, but has been able to largely control the effects of it through medication and his rigorous training regimen. Among his numerous awards, he has been named Trainer of Year by the Boxing Writers Association of America an unprecedented five times, and was recently inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. Roach is the focus of the current HBO series On Freddie Roach , directed by Peter Berg.

弗雷迪·罗奇 1960 年出生于马萨诸塞州戴德姆。他从六岁开始接受拳击训练。到 1978 年转为职业拳击手时，罗奇已参加过 150 场业余比赛。在传奇拳手埃迪·富奇的训练下，罗奇作为职业拳手取得了 41 胜（17 胜 13 负）的战绩。1986 年退役后，罗奇在富奇手下担任教练，几年后开始了自己的职业生涯，并于 1995 年在加利福尼亚州好莱坞开设了自己的 Wild Card 拳击俱乐部，现在他在那里训练他的拳手。作为教练，罗奇曾与 28 位世界冠军拳击手合作过，其中包括曼尼·帕奎奥、迈克·泰森、奥斯卡·德·拉·霍亚、阿米尔·汗、胡里奥·塞萨尔·查韦斯、詹姆斯·托尼和维吉尔·希尔。他还是UFC次中量级冠军乔治·圣皮埃尔和世界顶级女子拳击手之一露西亚·里杰克的教练。1990年，罗奇被诊断出患有帕金森病，但通过药物治疗和严格的训练，他在很大程度上控制了病情的影响。他荣获众多奖项，其中包括史无前例地五次被美国拳击作家协会评为年度最佳教练，最近还入选了国际拳击名人堂。罗奇是彼得·博格执导的HBO电视剧《弗雷迪·罗奇》的主角。

Cesar Rodriguez Jr. was born in 1959, in El Paso, Texas. After graduating from the Citadel, the Military College of South Carolina, with a degree in business administration, Rodriguez entered the Air Force Undergraduate Pilot Training Program. Trained as a command fighter pilot on the F-15, among other jets, he slowly rose through the ranks, becoming major in 1993, lieutenant colonel in 1997, and full colonel in 2002. He compiled over 3,100 fighter flight hours, 350 of which were in combat operations. He distinguished himself in aerial combat, as he is credited with downing three enemy aircraft—two Iraqi MiG fighters during Operation Desert Storm (1991) and a Yugoslavian Air Force MiG during the Yugoslav War (1999). His three kills in active duty are the most of any American pilot since the Vietnam War. Rodriguez commanded the 332nd Expeditionary Operations Group during Operation Iraqi Freedom (2003). Rodriguez retired from the air force in 2006. He is a graduate of the U.S. Air Force Air Command and Staff College, and the U.S. Naval War College. Among his numerous medals, he has been awarded three Distinguished Flying Crosses, the Legion of Merit, and the Bronze Star. He is currently employed by Raytheon as the director of International Programs and Growth for their Air Warfare Systems Product line.

塞萨尔·罗德里格斯二世于 1959 年出生于德克萨斯州埃尔帕索。从南卡罗来纳军事学院城堡分校毕业并获得工商管理学位后，罗德里格斯进入了空军本科飞行员训练计划。他接受了 F-15 等战斗机指挥飞行员的训练，并逐渐晋升，1993 年晋升为少校，1997 年晋升为中校，2002 年晋升为上校。他累计拥有超过 3,100 小时的战斗机飞行时间，其中 350 小时用于作战行动。他在空战中表现出色，击落三架敌机——沙漠风暴行动 (1991 年) 期间击落两架伊拉克米格战斗机，南斯拉夫战争 (1999 年) 期间击落一架南斯拉夫空军米格战斗机。他在现役期间的三次击落记录是自越南战争以来美国飞行员中最多的。罗德里格斯在2003年的伊拉克自由行动中指挥了第332远征作战大队。罗德里格斯于2006年从空军退役。他毕业于美国空军指挥参谋学院和美国海军战争学院。他荣获过无数勋章，其中包括三枚杰出飞行十字勋章、一枚功绩军团勋章和一枚铜星勋章。他目前受雇于雷神公司，担任其空战系统产品线的国际项目和发展总监。

ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

致谢

First and foremost I would like to thank Anna Biller for all of her invaluable contributions to this book—including her many insightful ideas, her skillful editing, her help with the research, and her loving support throughout the long writing process. Her work and assistance made this book possible, and I am eternally grateful.

首先，我要感谢安娜·比勒对本书做出的宝贵贡献——包括她许多深刻的见解、她娴熟的编辑技巧、她在研究方面的帮助，以及她在漫长写作过程中给予的悉心支持。她的辛勤付出和帮助使本书得以问世，我对此永远心怀感激。

I would like to thank my agent, Michael Carlisle at Inkwell Management, for deftly navigating this project past the occasional obstacles that came up, and for all of his editorial and life advice. He is truly the Master agent. Also at Inkwell, my thanks go to Lauren Smythe for all of her help, and to Alexis Hurley for bringing the book to a worldwide audience.

我要感谢我的经纪人，Inkwell Management 的 Michael Carlisle，他巧妙地引导我克服了项目中偶尔遇到的障碍，并提供了编辑和人生方面的建议。他真是经纪人大师。同时，我要感谢 Inkwell 的 Lauren Smythe 提供的所有帮助，以及 Alexis Hurley 将这本书带给全球读者。

I would like to thank Molly Stern for setting the whole project in motion, and all of those at Viking who played such an important role in the production of the book. That would include my editor Josh Kendall, who helped and influenced the project on so many levels; Carolyn Carlson, who took over the editorial reins and worked her magic; Maggie Payette, who designed the cover; Daniel Lagin, who designed the layout; Noirin Lucas, who ably shepherded the book through production; marketing director Nancy Sheppard and publicity director Carolyn Coleburn, who both did such a wonderful job in promoting the book; and last but not least Margaret Riggs, who lent all of her logistical support. I must also thank Clare Ferraro for her patience and her overall masterful direction of the project.

我要感谢 Molly Stern 启动了整个项目，也感谢维京出版社所有在本书制作过程中发挥重要作用的同事。这其中包括我的编辑 Josh Kendall，他在很多层面上都给予了帮助和影响；Carolyn Carlson，她接手编辑工作并发挥了她的魔力；Maggie Payette，她设计了封面；Daniel Lagin，她设计了版式；Noirin Lucas，她出色地指导了本书的制作；市场总监 Nancy Sheppard 和宣传总监 Carolyn Coleburn，她们在本书的推广方面做得非常出色；最后，同样重要的是 Margaret Riggs，她提供了所有的后勤支持。我还必须感谢 Clare Ferraro 的耐心和她对整个项目的精湛指导。

I would like to thank Ryan Holiday, author of Trust Me I’m Lying: Confessions of a Media Manipulator (Penguin 2012), for his invaluable assistance on the research and for helping find and coordinate interviews with the various contemporary Masters.

我要感谢《相信我，我在撒谎：一个媒体操纵者的自白》（企鹅出版社 2012 年出版）的作者瑞安·霍利迪 (Ryan Holiday)，感谢他对研究的宝贵帮助，以及帮助寻找和协调与各位当代大师的访谈。

Along the way, several people contributed with their advice and ideas. First on the list would have to be 50 Cent. Our discussions back in 2007 planted the seed for this book. 50’s literary agent, Marc Gerald, played his usual midwife role in the early stages. In this vein, I would also like to thank Casper Alexander, Keith Ferrazzi, and Neil Strauss; Professor William Ripple; Francisco Gimenez; my great friends Eliot Schain, Michiel Schwarz, and Joost Elffers; and Katerina Kantola, whose memory will live on forever. I would also like to thank my sister Leslie for all of her inspiring ideas about animals and our Pleistocene ancestors.

一路走来，不少人贡献了他们的建议和想法。名单上第一位的当属50 Cent。我们2007年的讨论为这本书埋下了伏笔。50 Cent的文学经纪人马克·杰拉德在早期阶段发挥了他一贯的助产士作用。同时，我还要感谢卡斯珀·亚历山大、基思·法拉齐和尼尔·施特劳斯；威廉·里普尔教授；弗朗西斯科·吉梅内斯；我的挚友艾略特·沙因、米歇尔·施瓦茨和约斯特·埃尔弗斯；以及卡特琳娜·坎托拉，她的记忆将永存。我还要感谢我的妹妹莱斯利，感谢她关于动物和我们更新世祖先的所有启发性想法。

I am, of course, eternally grateful to the contemporary Masters who agreed to be interviewed for this book. I had made it a condition that all interviews be conducted in person, with no real time limit, and that the interview subjects had to be as candid as possible about their creative process, their early struggles, and even failures along the way. All of the people I interviewed were extremely generous with their time and gracious in dealing with my often-irritating questions. They displayed the kind of open spirit that I believe plays an essential role in mastery and success in life.

当然，我永远感激那些同意接受本书采访的当代大师们。我提出一个条件：所有采访都必须面对面进行，没有时间限制，并且受访者必须尽可能坦诚地讲述他们的创作过程、早期的挣扎，甚至一路上的失败。所有接受我采访的人都非常慷慨地付出时间，并且非常有风度地回答了我那些常常令人恼火的问题。他们展现出一种开放的精神，我相信这种精神对于人生的精进和成功至关重要。

In helping me to set up these interviews I must thank graduate student Elizabeth Seckel, who works with Professor V.S. Ramachandran at UCSD; Jessica Livingston, wife of Paul Graham and founding partner of Y Combinator; Andrew Franklin, my extraordinary publisher at Profile Books in the United Kingdom, who helped with the Daniel Everett interview; David Gordon, former director of the Calatrava-enhanced Milwaukee Art Museum, who helped set up the Santiago Calatrava interview; Mrs. Tina Calatrava; Cheryl Miller, executive assistant to Temple Grandin; Stephanie Smith, partner at Lehmann Maupin, who helped with the Teresita Fernández interview; and agents Nick Khan and Evan Dick at CAA, who both represent Freddie Roach.

在帮助我安排这些采访时，我必须感谢研究生伊丽莎白塞克尔 (Elizabeth Seckel)，她与加州大学圣地亚哥分校的 V.S. 拉马钱德兰 (V.S. Ramachandran) 教授一起工作；杰西卡利文斯顿 (Jessica Livingston)，保罗格雷厄姆 (Paul Graham) 的妻子和 Y Combinator 的创始合伙人；安德鲁富兰克林 (Andrew Franklin)，我在英国 Profile Books 的杰出出版商，他帮助我进行了丹尼尔埃弗里特 (Daniel Everett) 的采访；大卫戈登 (David Gordon)，卡拉特拉瓦增强版密尔沃基艺术博物馆的前馆长，他帮助安排了圣地亚哥卡拉特拉瓦 (Santiago Calatrava) 的采访；蒂娜卡拉特拉瓦夫人；谢丽尔米勒 (Cheryl Miller)，坦普尔格兰丁 (Temple Grandin) 的行政助理；斯蒂芬妮史密斯 (Stephanie Smith)，立木画廊 (Lehmann Maupin) 的合伙人，她帮助我进行了特雷西塔费尔南德斯 (Teresita Fernández) 的采访；以及 CAA 的经纪人尼克汗 (Nick Khan) 和埃文迪克 (Evan Dick)，他们都是弗雷迪罗奇 (Freddie Roach) 的经纪人。

I must also thank my mother, Laurette, for all of her patience and love, and for being my biggest fan. And, of course, I cannot fail to mention Brutus, the greatest cat who has ever lived and Master hunter.

我还要感谢我的母亲劳雷特，感谢她所有的耐心和爱，以及她一直是我最忠实的粉丝。当然，我也不能不提布鲁图斯，它是有史以来最伟大的猫，也是狩猎大师。

Finally, I would like to thank all those in the past—masters, mentors, and teachers—who over the years slowly opened my eyes to so many ideas, and taught me how to think. Their presence and spirit are suffused throughout this book.

最后，我要感谢所有过去给予我的恩师、导师和老师们，他们多年来慢慢地开阔了我的眼界，让我领悟到了许多新奇的理念，并教会了我如何思考。他们的存在和精神贯穿了整本书。
